5.260.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
kathaṃ nityā bhagavatī harapatnī yaśasvinī ..
yogasiddhiṃ sumahatīṃ prāpa māsacatuṣṭaye .. 1 ..
5.260.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
कथं नित्या भगवती हरपत्नी यशस्विनी ..
योगसिद्धिं सुमहतीं प्राप मासचतुष्टये .. 1 ..
5.260.m: Nārada said: / "How did the eternal goddess, the renowned consort of Hara, / attain the great perfection of yoga in the four months

5.260.s:
mantrarājamimaṃ japtvā dvādaśākṣarasaṃbhavam ..
etanme vistareṇa tvaṃ kathayasva yathātatham..2.. ..
5.260.d:
मन्त्रराजमिमं जप्त्वा द्वादशाक्षरसंभवम् ..
एतन्मे विस्तरेण त्वं कथयस्व यथातथम्..2.. ..
5.260.m: by reciting this king of mantras originating from twelve syllables? / Tell this to me in detail, just as it happened."

5.260.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
cāturmāsye harau supte pārvatī niyatavratā ..
manasā karmaṇā vācā haribhaktiparāyaṇā .. 3 ..
5.260.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
चातुर्मास्ये हरौ सुप्ते पार्वती नियतव्रता ..
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा हरिभक्तिपरायणा .. 3 ..
5.260.m: Brahmā said: / During the Cāturmāsya, while Hari slept, Pārvatī was observant of her vows, / devoted to devotion to Hari with mind, deed, and speech.

5.260.s:
cāruśṛṃge piturnityaṃ tiṣṭhaṃtī tapasi sthitā ..
devadvijāgnigo'śvatthātithipūjāparāyaṇā .. 4 ..
5.260.d:
चारुशृंगे पितुर्नित्यं तिष्ठंती तपसि स्थिता ..
देवद्विजाग्निगोऽश्वत्थातिथिपूजापरायणा .. 4 ..
5.260.m: Constantly abiding on the lovely peak of her father, dedicated to austerity, / she was devoted to the worship of the gods, twice-born, fire, cows, the aśvattha tree, and guests.

5.260.s:
cāturmāsye'tha saṃprāpte vimale harivāsare ..
jajāpa paramaṃ maṃtraṃ yathādiṣṭaṃ pinākinā .. 5 ..
5.260.d:
चातुर्मास्येऽथ संप्राप्ते विमले हरिवासरे ..
जजाप परमं मंत्रं यथादिष्टं पिनाकिना .. 5 ..
5.260.m: Then, when the Cāturmāsya arrived, on a spotless day sacred to Hari, / she recited the supreme mantra as instructed by the wielder of Pināka.

5.260.s:
śaṃkhacakradharo viṣṇuścaturhastaḥ kirīṭadhṛk ..
meghaśyāmoṃ'bujākṣaśca sūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ .. 6 ..
garuḍādhiṣṭhito hṛṣṭo vasanvyāpya jagattrayam ..
śrīvatsakaustubhayutaḥ pītakauśeyavastrakaḥ ..7..
5.260.d:
शंखचक्रधरो विष्णुश्चतुर्हस्तः किरीटधृक् ..
मेघश्यामोंऽबुजाक्षश्च सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभः .. 6 ..
गरुडाधिष्ठितो हृष्टो वसन्व्याप्य जगत्त्रयम् ..
श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभयुतः पीतकौशेयवस्त्रकः ..7..
5.260.m: Viṣṇu, bearing a conch and discus, four-armed and wearing a crown, / dark as a cloud, lotus-eyed, and equal in radiance to ten million suns, / seated upon Garuḍa, delighted, abiding pervasive across the three worlds, / adorned with the Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha, wearing yellow silk garments,

5.260.s:
sarvābharaṇaśobhābhirabhidīptamahāvapuḥ ..
babhāṣe pārvatīṃ viṣṇuḥ prasannavadanaḥ śubhām..
devi tuṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te kathayasva tavepsitam .. 8 ..
5.260.d:
सर्वाभरणशोभाभिरभिदीप्तमहावपुः ..
बभाषे पार्वतीं विष्णुः प्रसन्नवदनः शुभाम्..
देवि तुष्टो ऽस्मि भद्रं ते कथयस्व तवेप्सितम् .. 8 ..
5.260.m: his vast body shining with the splendors of all ornaments, / his face cheerful, addressed the auspicious Pārvatī: / “O goddess, I am pleased; hail to you! Tell [me] your desire.”

5.260.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
tajjñānamamalaṃ dehi yena nāvarttanaṃ bhavet ..
ityuktaḥ sa mahāviṣṇuḥ pratyuvāca harapriyām ..9..
5.260.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
तज्ज्ञानममलं देहि येन नावर्त्तनं भवेत् ..
इत्युक्तः स महाविष्णुः प्रत्युवाच हरप्रियाम् ..9..
5.260.m: Pārvatī said: / “Grant that spotless knowledge by which there may be no return.” / Addressed thus, that Mahāviṣṇu replied to the beloved of Hara:

5.260.s:
sa eva devadeveśastava vakṣyatyasaṃśayam ..
sa eva bhagavānsākṣī dehāṃtarabahiḥsthitaḥ ..6.261.10...
5.260.d:
स एव देवदेवेशस्तव वक्ष्यत्यसंशयम् ..
स एव भगवान्साक्षी देहांतरबहिःस्थितः ..6.261.10...
5.260.m: “He himself, the Lord of the gods of gods, will tell you without doubt. / He alone is the Lord, the Witness, residing inside and outside the body.

5.260.s:
viśvasraṣṭā ca goptā ca pavitrāṇāṃ ca pāvanaḥ ..
anādinidhano dharmo dharmādīnāṃ prabhurhi saḥ .. 11 ..
5.260.d:
विश्वस्रष्टा च गोप्ता च पवित्राणां च पावनः ..
अनादिनिधनो धर्मो धर्मादीनां प्रभुर्हि सः .. 11 ..
5.260.m: He is the creator and protector of the universe, and the purifier of purifiers; / he is dharma without beginning or end, and indeed the lord of dharma and the rest.

5.260.s:
akṣaratrayasevyaṃ yatsakalaṃ brahma eva saḥ ..
mūrttāmūrttasvarūpeṇa yo'jo janmadharo hi saḥ .. 12 ..
5.260.d:
अक्षरत्रयसेव्यं यत्सकलं ब्रह्म एव सः ..
मूर्त्तामूर्त्तस्वरूपेण योऽजो जन्मधरो हि सः .. 12 ..
5.260.m: He is indeed that whole Brahman to be served by the three syllables. / He who, unborn, assumes birth through embodied and unembodied forms,

5.260.s:
mamādhikāro naivāsti vaktuṃ tava na saṃśayaḥ ..
ityuktvā bhagavānīśo virarāma prahṛṣṭavān ..13..
5.260.d:
ममाधिकारो नैवास्ति वक्तुं तव न संशयः ..
इत्युक्त्वा भगवानीशो विरराम प्रहृष्टवान् ..13..
5.260.m: I certainly have no authority to speak [of this] to you, no doubt.” / Having spoken thus, the Lord became silent, filled with joy.

5.260.s:
etasminnaṃtare śaṃbhurgirijāśramamabhyagāt ..
sarvabhūta gaṇairyukto vimāne sārvakāmike .. 14 ..
5.260.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे शंभुर्गिरिजाश्रममभ्यगात् ..
सर्वभूत गणैर्युक्तो विमाने सार्वकामिके .. 14 ..
5.260.m: In the meantime, Śambhu arrived at the hermitage of the daughter of the mountain, / accompanied by the troops of all beings, in an aerial chariot that fulfills all desires.

5.260.s:
tayā vai bhagavāndevaḥ pūjitaḥ parameśvaraḥ ..
sakhīnāmapi pratyakṣamāścaryaṃ samajāyata .. 15 ..
5.260.d:
तया वै भगवान्देवः पूजितः परमेश्वरः ..
सखीनामपि प्रत्यक्षमाश्चर्यं समजायत .. 15 ..
5.260.m: By her indeed was the Lord, the Supreme God, worshipped. / Even before the eyes of her companions, a wonder took place:

5.260.s:
stutvā'tha taṃ mahādevaṃ viṣṇurdehe layaṃ yayau ..
athovāca maheśānaḥ pārvatīṃ parameśvaraḥ .. 16 ..
5.260.d:
स्तुत्वाऽथ तं महादेवं विष्णुर्देहे लयं ययौ ..
अथोवाच महेशानः पार्वतीं परमेश्वरः .. 16 ..
5.260.m: having praised that Mahādeva, Viṣṇu dissolved into his body. / Then Maheśāna, the Supreme Lord, said to Pārvatī:

5.260.s:
vimānavaramāruhya tuṣṭo'haṃ tava suvrate ..
gatvaikāṃtapradeśaṃ te kathaye paramaṃ mahaḥ .. 17 ..
5.260.d:
विमानवरमारुह्य तुष्टोऽहं तव सुव्रते ..
गत्वैकांतप्रदेशं ते कथये परमं महः .. 17 ..
5.260.m: “Mount the excellent aerial chariot; I am pleased with you, O woman of good vows! / Going to a solitary place, I shall tell you of the supreme splendor.”

5.260.s:
evamuktvā bhagavatīṃ kare gṛhya mudānvitaḥ ..
vimānavaramāropya līlayā prayayau tadā .. 19 ..
nānādhātumayānadrīnnānāratnavicitritān ..
nadīnirjharakuṃjāṃśca nadānkokilakūjitān ..19..
akhātāndevakhātāṃśca gaṃgādyāḥ saritastathā ..
saugaṃdhikāṃśca kalhārānsahasradalapiṃjarān ..6.261.2...
5.260.d:
एवमुक्त्वा भगवतीं करे गृह्य मुदान्वितः ..
विमानवरमारोप्य लीलया प्रययौ तदा .. 19 ..
नानाधातुमयानद्रीन्नानारत्नविचित्रितान् ..
नदीनिर्झरकुंजांश्च नदान्कोकिलकूजितान् ..19..
अखातान्देवखातांश्च गंगाद्याः सरितस्तथा ..
सौगंधिकांश्च कल्हारान्सहस्रदलपिंजरान् ..6.261.2...
5.260.m:
Having spoken thus to the goddess, taking her by the hand, filled with joy, / placing her upon the excellent aerial chariot, he then set forth sportively,
showing mountains composed of various minerals, variegated with various jewels, / rivers, waterfalls, bowers, and streams echoing with the songs of cuckoos,
natural ponds and ponds dug by gods, and rivers such as the Gaṅgā, / and fragrant water lilies, red and reddish-yellow with a thousand petals,

5.260.s:
darśanyakarṇikārāṃśca kovidārānmahādrumān ..
tālāṃstamālānhiṃtālānpriyaṃgūnpanasānapi .. 21 ..
5.260.d:
दर्शन्यकर्णिकारांश्च कोविदारान्महाद्रुमान् ..
तालांस्तमालान्हिंतालान्प्रियंगून्पनसानपि .. 21 ..
5.260.m: showing also karṇikāras, kovidāras, and great trees, / palmyras, tamālas, hintālas, priyaṅgus, and breadfruit trees,

5.260.s:
tilakānbakulāṃścaiva bahūnapi ca puṣpitān ..
kṣetrāṇi kalanābhāni piñjarāṇi vidarśayan .. 22 ..
5.260.d:
तिलकान्बकुलांश्चैव बहूनपि च पुष्पितान् ..
क्षेत्राणि कलनाभानि पिञ्जराणि विदर्शयन् .. 22 ..
5.260.m: tilakas and bakulas, many of them flowering, / and showing fields shining like crescent crescents, reddish-yellow.

5.260.s:
yayau devanadītīre gataṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat ..
phullakāśaṃ svarṇamayaṃ śarastaṃbagaṇānvitam .. 23 ..
5.260.d:
ययौ देवनदीतीरे गतं शरवणं महत् ..
फुल्लकाशं स्वर्णमयं शरस्तंबगणान्वितम् .. 23 ..
5.260.m: He went to the bank of the divine river where lay the great forest of reeds, / with blooming kāśa grass, full of gold, filled with clusters of reed stalks,

5.260.s:
hema bhūmivibhāgasthaṃ vahnikāṃtimṛgadvijam ..
tatra tīragatānāṃ ca munīnāmūrdhvaretasām .. 24 ..
5.260.d:
हेम भूमिविभागस्थं वह्निकांतिमृगद्विजम् ..
तत्र तीरगतानां च मुनीनामूर्ध्वरेतसाम् .. 24 ..
5.260.m: standing on a tract of golden ground, with beasts and birds having the radiance of fire. / And standing at the front of the aerial chariot, he showed to his wife

5.260.s:
āśramānsa vimānāgre tiṣṭhanpatnyai pradarśayat ..
ṣaṭkṛttikāśca dadṛśe pārvatī vanasannidhau .. 25 ..
5.260.d:
आश्रमान्स विमानाग्रे तिष्ठन्पत्न्यै प्रदर्शयत् ..
षट्कृत्तिकाश्च ददृशे पार्वती वनसन्निधौ .. 25 ..
5.260.m: the hermitages of the chaste ascetics who had gone to that bank. / And near the forest, Pārvatī beheld the six Kṛttikās,

5.260.s:
snātāḥ svalaṃkṛtāścandrapatnyastā virajāṃbarāḥ ..
ūcustā yojitakarā ke'yaṃ putrāya gamyate .. 26 ..
5.260.d:
स्नाताः स्वलंकृताश्चन्द्रपत्न्यस्ता विरजांबराः ..
ऊचुस्ता योजितकरा केऽयं पुत्राय गम्यते .. 26 ..
5.260.m: bathed, well adorned, the wives of the Moon, with clean garments. / With folded hands they said: “For what son is this journey being made?

5.260.s: tatkathyatāṃ mahābhāge sa ca te darśanaṃ gataḥ .. 27 ..
5.260.d: तत्कथ्यतां महाभागे स च ते दर्शनं गतः .. 27 ..
5.260.m: Let that be told, O fortunate one, and he has come into your sight.”

5.260.s:
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
mama bhāgyavaśātputraḥ kathamutsaṃgamāharet ..
na hyabhāgyavaśātpuṃsāṃ kvāpi saukhyaṃ nirantaram..28..
5.260.d:
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
मम भाग्यवशात्पुत्रः कथमुत्संगमाहरेत् ..
न ह्यभाग्यवशात्पुंसां क्वापि सौख्यं निरन्तरम्..28..
5.260.m: Pārvatī said: / “By what good fortune of mine could a son take to my lap? / Indeed, through misfortune, there is never continuous happiness for people.

5.260.s:
sutanāmnāpyahaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavatīnāṃ ca darśanāt..
kimarthamiha saṃprāptāḥ kathyatāmavilaṃbitam..29..
5.260.d:
सुतनाम्नाप्यहं दृष्ट्वा भवतीनां च दर्शनात्..
किमर्थमिह संप्राप्ताः कथ्यतामविलंबितम्..29..
5.260.m: Even upon the name of a son, having seen [this], and from the sight of you ladies— / for what purpose have you come here? Let it be told without delay.”

5.260.s:
kṛttikā ūcuḥ..
vayaṃ tava sutaṃ nyastaṃ pradātumiha sundari..
cāturmāsye ravau snātumāgatā devanimnagām..6.261.30...
5.260.d:
कृत्तिका ऊचुः..
वयं तव सुतं न्यस्तं प्रदातुमिह सुन्दरि..
चातुर्मास्ये रवौ स्नातुमागता देवनिम्नगाम्..6.261.30...
5.260.m: The Kṛttikās said: / “We have come here, O beautiful one, to give over your son who was deposited [with us]. / During the Cāturmāsya, when the sun was shining, we came to bathe in the river of the gods.”

5.260.s:
pārvatyuvāca..
na hāsyāvasaraḥ sakhyaḥ satyameva hi kathyatām..
ekāṃtāvasare hāsyaṃ jāyate cetaretaram..31..
5.260.d:
पार्वत्युवाच..
न हास्यावसरः सख्यः सत्यमेव हि कथ्यताम्..
एकांतावसरे हास्यं जायते चेतरेतरम्..31..
5.260.m: Pārvatī said: / “This is not a time for jest, friends; speak only the truth! / In an intimate setting, joking arises between one another.”

5.260.s:
kṛttikā ūcuḥ..
satyaṃ vadāmahe devi tava trailokyaśobhite..
asya staṃbasamūhasya madhyasthaṃ bālakaṃ vṛṇu..32..
5.260.d:
कृत्तिका ऊचुः..
सत्यं वदामहे देवि तव त्रैलोक्यशोभिते..
अस्य स्तंबसमूहस्य मध्यस्थं बालकं वृणु..32..
5.260.m: The Kṛttikās said: / “We speak the truth, O goddess who adorns the three worlds! / Choose the boy standing in the midst of this clump of reeds.”

5.260.s:
kṛttikānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śaṃkitā pārvatī tadā..
dadarśa bālaṃ dīptābhaṃ ṣaṇmukhaṃ dīptavarcasam..33..
5.260.d:
कृत्तिकानां वचः श्रुत्वा शंकिता पार्वती तदा..
ददर्श बालं दीप्ताभं षण्मुखं दीप्तवर्चसम्..33..
5.260.m: Hearing the words of the Kṛttikās, Pārvatī, then full of wonder, / saw the boy of brilliant radiance, six-faced, of blazing splendor,

5.260.s:
taḍitkoṭipratīkāśaṃ rūpadivyaśriyā yutam..
vahniputraṃ ca gāṃgeyaṃ kārtikeyaṃ mahābalam.. 34..
5.260.d:
तडित्कोटिप्रतीकाशं रूपदिव्यश्रिया युतम्..
वह्निपुत्रं च गांगेयं कार्तिकेयं महाबलम्.. 34..
5.260.m: resembling ten million flashes of lightning, endowed with divine beauty of form, / the son of Fire, the son of Gaṅgā, Kārtikeya of great strength.

5.260.s:
sā vatseti gṛhītvā taṃ kumāraṃ pāṇinā mudā..
vimānamadhyamādāya kṛtvotsaṃge hyuvāca ha.. 35..
5.260.d:
सा वत्सेति गृहीत्वा तं कुमारं पाणिना मुदा..
विमानमध्यमादाय कृत्वोत्संगे ह्युवाच ह.. 35..
5.260.m: Saying “O child!”, taking Kumāra with her hand in joy, / bringing him into the middle of the aerial chariot and placing him on her lap, she said:

5.260.s:
ciraṃjīva ciraṃ nanda ciraṃ naṃdaya bādhavān..
ityuktvā gāḍhamāliṃgya mūrdhni cāghrāya taṃ sutam..36..
5.260.d:
चिरंजीव चिरं नन्द चिरं नंदय बाधवान्..
इत्युक्त्वा गाढमालिंग्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय तं सुतम्..36..
5.260.m: “Live long, rejoice long, give joy long to your kinsmen!” / Having spoken thus, firmly embracing him and smelling that son upon the head,

5.260.s:
saṃhṛṣṭā paramodāraṃ bhāsvaraṃ hṛṣṭamānasam..
kārtikeyo mahāpremṇā praṇipatya maheśvaram..37..
5.260.d:
संहृष्टा परमोदारं भास्वरं हृष्टमानसम्..
कार्तिकेयो महाप्रेम्णा प्रणिपत्य महेश्वरम्..37..
5.260.m: she was overjoyed at the supremely generous, radiant one with a delighted mind. / Having bowed down to Maheśvara with great love,

5.260.s:
tataḥ prāṃjaliravyagraḥ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā..
tadvimānaṃ yayau śīghraṃ tīrtvā nadanadīpatīn..38..
5.260.d:
ततः प्रांजलिरव्यग्रः प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना..
तद्विमानं ययौ शीघ्रं तीर्त्वा नदनदीपतीन्..38..
5.260.m: thereupon, with folded hands, composed, with a joyful inner self, / Kārtikeya [sat]. That aerial chariot swiftly departed, crossing the lords of rivers and streams.

5.260.s:
jaṃbudvīpamatikramya lakṣayojanamāyatam..
tataḥ samudraṃ dviguṇaṃ lavaṇodaṃ tathaiva ca..39..
uttarāṃśca kurūnnītvā vimānenārkatejasā..
samudradviguṇaṃ dvīpaṃ kuśanābheti kīrtitam..6.261.4...
5.260.d:
जंबुद्वीपमतिक्रम्य लक्षयोजनमायतम्..
ततः समुद्रं द्विगुणं लवणोदं तथैव च..39..
उत्तरांश्च कुरून्नीत्वा विमानेनार्कतेजसा..
समुद्रद्विगुणं द्वीपं कुशनाभेति कीर्तितम्..6.261.4...
5.260.m:
Having passed beyond Jambudvīpa, which extends for a hundred thousand yojanas, / and then the salt-water ocean, which is twice as large,
and having traversed the Northern Kurus in the aerial chariot with the radiance of the sun, / [they reached] the continent known as Kuśadvīpa, twice the size of the ocean,

5.260.s:
divyalokasamākrāṃtaṃ divyaparvatasaṃkulam..
ikṣūdādviguṇaṃ dvīpaṃ taddvīpāddviguṇaḥ punaḥ..41..
5.260.d:
दिव्यलोकसमाक्रांतं दिव्यपर्वतसंकुलम्..
इक्षूदाद्विगुणं द्वीपं तद्द्वीपाद्द्विगुणः पुनः..41..
5.260.m: pervaded by divine worlds and crowded with divine mountains. / Twice the size of the sugarcane-juice ocean is the continent, and twice that continent again,

5.260.s:
tamatikramya tatsindhordaviguṇaṃ krauṃcasaṃjñitam..
tato'pi dviguṇaḥ sindhuḥ surodo yakṣasevitaḥ..42..
5.260.d:
तमतिक्रम्य तत्सिन्धोर्दविगुणं क्रौंचसंज्ञितम्..
ततोऽपि द्विगुणः सिन्धुः सुरोदो यक्षसेवितः..42..
5.260.m: having crossed that, twice the size of that ocean is the one named Krauñca; / twice as large as that is the wine ocean, frequented by yakṣas.

5.260.s:
tato'pi dviguṇaṃ dvīpaṃ śākadvīpetisaṃjñitam..
arṇavadviguṇaṃ tasmādājyarūpaṃ sunirmitaṃ..43..
5.260.d:
ततोऽपि द्विगुणं द्वीपं शाकद्वीपेतिसंज्ञितम्..
अर्णवद्विगुणं तस्मादाज्यरूपं सुनिर्मितं..43..
5.260.m: Twice the size of that is the continent known as Śākadvīpa; / twice that is the well-fashioned ocean consisting of clarified butter,

5.260.s:
paramasvādasaṃpūrṇaṃ yatra siddhāḥ samaṃtataḥ..
tasmācca dviguṇaṃ dvīpaṃ śālmalīvṛkṣasaṃjñitam..44..
5.260.d:
परमस्वादसंपूर्णं यत्र सिद्धाः समंततः..
तस्माच्च द्विगुणं द्वीपं शाल्मलीवृक्षसंज्ञितम्..44..
5.260.m: full of supreme flavor, where perfected beings dwell on every side. / And twice the size of that is the continent named after the śālmali tree.

5.260.s:
samudro dviguṇastatra dadhimaṃḍodasaṃbhavaḥ..
sādhyā vasaṃti niyataṃ mahattapasi saṃsthitāḥ.. 45..
5.260.d:
समुद्रो द्विगुणस्तत्र दधिमंडोदसंभवः..
साध्या वसंति नियतं महत्तपसि संस्थिताः.. 45..
5.260.m: Twice as large there is the ocean arising from curd-water; / there the Sādhyas constantly dwell, established in great austerity.

5.260.s:
tato'pi dviguṇaṃ dvīpaṃ plakṣanāmeti viśrutam..
kṣīrodo dviguṇastatra yatrayatramaharṣayaḥ..
ṣaḍimāni sudivyāni bhaumaḥ svarga udāhṛtaḥ..
tatra svarṇamayī bhūmistathā rajatasaṃyutā..47..
5.260.d:
ततोऽपि द्विगुणं द्वीपं प्लक्षनामेति विश्रुतम्..
क्षीरोदो द्विगुणस्तत्र यत्रयत्रमहर्षयः..
षडिमानि सुदिव्यानि भौमः स्वर्ग उदाहृतः..
तत्र स्वर्णमयी भूमिस्तथा रजतसंयुता..47..
5.260.m: Twice as large as that is the continent famous under the name Plakṣa; / twice as large there is the milk ocean, where great seers dwell everywhere. / These six very divine [places] are proclaimed as earthly heaven; / there the ground is made of gold, and likewise endowed with silver.

5.260.s:
dṛṣṭavā madhūpalasvādaiḥ sarvakāmapradāyakā..
yatra strīpuruṣāṇāṃ ca kalpavṛkṣā gṛhe sthitāḥ..48..
5.260.d:
दृष्टवा मधूपलस्वादैः सर्वकामप्रदायका..
यत्र स्त्रीपुरुषाणां च कल्पवृक्षा गृहे स्थिताः..48..
5.260.m: having tastes like wine and sugar crystals, bestowing all desires, / where wish-fulfilling trees stand in the home for women and men. (48)

5.260.s:
vāsāṃsi bhūṣaṇānāṃ ca samūhānharṣayaṃti ca..
etāni dakṣacihnāni dvīpāni munisattama..49..
maheśvaro vimānena vyatikrāmadvihāyasā..
plakṣadvīpasya ca prāṃte dviguṇaḥ kṣīrasāgaraḥ..6.261.5...
5.260.d:
वासांसि भूषणानां च समूहान्हर्षयंति च..
एतानि दक्षचिह्नानि द्वीपानि मुनिसत्तम..49..
महेश्वरो विमानेन व्यतिक्रामद्विहायसा..
प्लक्षद्वीपस्य च प्रांते द्विगुणः क्षीरसागरः..6.261.5...
5.260.m:
They delight [them] with collections of garments and ornaments. / These are the islands with auspicious marks, O best of sages. (49)
Maheśvara traversed across the sky in his aerial chariot. / And at the border of Plakṣadvīpa lies the milk-ocean, twice as large. (50)

5.260.s:
tanmadhye sumahdvīpaṃ śvetaṃ nāma suniścitam..
ramyakaḥ parvatastatra śataśṛṃgomitadrumaḥ..51..
5.260.d:
तन्मध्ये सुमह्द्वीपं श्वेतं नाम सुनिश्चितम्..
रम्यकः पर्वतस्तत्र शतशृंगोमितद्रुमः..51..
5.260.m: In the middle of it lies a very great island, certainly named Śveta. / The Ramyaka mountain is there, with a hundred peaks and countless trees. (51)

5.260.s:
tasya śṛṃge mahaddivye vimānaṃ sthāpitaṃ tadā..
tadā'mṛtaphalairvṛkṣaiḥ sevite hemavāluke..52..
5.260.d:
तस्य शृंगे महद्दिव्ये विमानं स्थापितं तदा..
तदाऽमृतफलैर्वृक्षैः सेविते हेमवालुके..52..
5.260.m: On its great divine peak the aerial chariot was then halted, / which was visited by trees with immortal fruit and possessed golden sands, (52)

5.260.s:
kṣīracchedena vihṛte śilātalasusaṃvṛte..
vivikte sarvasubhage maṇiratnasamanvite..53..
5.260.d:
क्षीरच्छेदेन विहृते शिलातलसुसंवृते..
विविक्ते सर्वसुभगे मणिरत्नसमन्विते..53..
5.260.m: surrounded by channels of milk, fully covered with stone slabs, / solitary, charming in every way, and endowed with gems and jewels. (53)

5.260.s:
umāyai kathayāmāsa devadevaḥ pinākadhṛk ..

5.260.d:

कार्तिकेयोऽपि शुश्राव गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं महत् ..54 .
ध्यानयोगं मंत्ररूपं द्वादशाक्षरसंज्ञितम् .1
5.260.m:
The god of gods, bearer of the Pināka, told Umā; / Kārtikeya also heard the great secret more secret than the secret: (54)
the yoga of meditation in the form of a mantra, known as the twelve-syllable [mantra],

5.260.s: praṇavena yutaṃ sāgraṃ sarahasyaṃ śruteḥ param .. .. 55 ..
5.260.d: प्रणवेन युतं साग्रं सरहस्यं श्रुतेः परम् .. .. 55 ..
5.260.m: endowed with the praṇava, complete with its crest, accompanied by its esoteric meaning, higher than the Veda. (55)

तुरीयकलयाऽशेषब्रह्मांडगणसेवितः 57 ..
5.260.m: Īśvara said: / This mantra, composed of three syllables, is imperishable when uttered once. / It is beneficial in the month of Māgha, free from agitation, free from illusion, the purifier of the universe; / attainable by Viṣṇu, centered on Viṣṇu, endowed with three mantras, / served by the entire host of universes through its fourth digit. (56–57)

5.260.s:
niṣkāmairmunibhiḥ sevyo mahāvidyādisevitaḥ ..

निष्कामैर्मुनिभिः सेव्यो महाविद्यादिसेवितः ..
नाभितः शिरसि व्याप्त अखण्डसुखदायकः. 988 ..

ज्ञात्वा सर्वगतं ब्रह्म देहशोधनतत्परः 1.
पद्मासनपरो भूत्वा संपूज्य ज्ञानलोचनः .. 6.261.60 ..
नेत्रे मुकुलिते कृत्वा शुरो करौ कृत्वा तु संहतौ ..

चन्द्रलक्षसमच्छन्नं पुरुषं द्योतिताखिलम् 1. 62..
मूर्त्तामूर्त्तवैराजं तं सदसद्रूप मव्यम् ..
चिंतयित्वा विराड्रूपं न भूयःस्तनपो भवेत् ..
चातुर्मास्ये सकृदपि ध्यानात्कल्मषसंक्षयः.. 63 .1
5.260.m:
It is to be resorted to by sages free from desire, attended by the great sciences and the rest; / pervading from the navel to the head, it bestows unbroken bliss. (58)
The utterance of 'Oṃ' to you, O beloved, destroys great sorrow. / Having first meditated on that praṇava, which is of the nature of knowledge, the abode of happiness, (59)
having known the all-pervading brahman, intent on purifying the body, / devoted to the lotus posture, having worshipped, with the eye of knowledge, (60)
having closed the eyes, and having joined the hands at the head, / in the mind one should contemplate the auspicious Śiva through meditation, (61)
resembling ten million lightning flashes, having the radiance of ten million suns, / clothed like a hundred thousand moons, the Puruṣa illuminating everything, (62)
that cosmic form with and without form, the immutable reality of being and non-being. / Having contemplated that cosmic form, one does not drink from a breast again. / Through meditation even once during Cāturmāsya, sins are destroyed. (63)

5.260.s:
evaṃ ca madrūpamidaṃ murāreramoghavīryaṃ guṇa topyapāram 1.
vilokayedyo'ghavināśanāya kṣaṇaṃ prabhurjanmaśatodbhavāya .. 64 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīsāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye dhyānayogonāmaikaṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 261 ..
5.260.d:
एवं च मद्रूपमिदं मुरारेरमोघवीर्यं गुण तोप्यपारम् 1.
विलोकयेद्योऽघविनाशनाय क्षणं प्रभुर्जन्मशतोद्भवाय .. 64 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये ध्यानयोगोनामैकषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 261 ..
5.260.m: And thus whoever gazes for a moment upon this form of mine, of Murāri—unfailing in virility and boundless in virtues—in order to destroy sins arising from a hundred births, becomes a master. (64) / Thus ends the two hundred sixty-first chapter, named 'Yoga of Meditation', in the praise of Cāturmāsya, in the narrative of the one who reclines on Śeṣa, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara sacred field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa in the great Skandapurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. (261)

5.261.m:
Pārvatī said: / Having attained the yoga of meditation, may I attain the yoga of knowledge. / Act in such a way, O Lord of gods, that I become immortal! (1)
Īśvara said:

5.261.s:
pratyukto'yaṃ maṃtrarājo dvādaśākṣarasaṃjñitaḥ ..
japtavyaḥ sukumārāṃgi vedasāraḥ sanātanaḥ .. 2 ..
5.261.d:
प्रत्युक्तोऽयं मंत्रराजो द्वादशाक्षरसंज्ञितः ..
जप्तव्यः सुकुमारांगि वेदसारः सनातनः .. 2 ..
5.261.m: This king of mantras, known as the twelve-syllable [mantra], has been explained; / it should be recited, O tender-limbed one; it is the eternal essence of the Veda. (2)

5.261.s:
praṇavaḥ sarvavedādyaḥ sarvabrahmāṃḍayājakaḥ ..
prathamaḥ sarvakāryeṣu sarvasiddhipradāyakaḥ .. 3 ..
5.261.d:
प्रणवः सर्ववेदाद्यः सर्वब्रह्मांडयाजकः ..
प्रथमः सर्वकार्येषु सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकः .. 3 ..
5.261.m: The praṇava is the beginning of all Vedas, the sacrificer of all universes, / the first in all rites, the bestower of all perfections. (3)

5.261.s:
sitavarṇo madhucchaṃdā ṛṣirbrahmā tu devatā ..
paramātmā tu gāyatrī niyogaḥ sarvakarmasu .. 4 ..
5.261.d:
सितवर्णो मधुच्छंदा ऋषिर्ब्रह्मा तु देवता ..
परमात्मा तु गायत्री नियोगः सर्वकर्मसु .. 4 ..
5.261.m: Its color is white, the seer is Madhucchandas, Brahmā is the deity, / the Paramātman is the Gāyatrī [meter], and its application is in all rites. (4)

5.261.s:
etadbrahmamayaṃ bījaṃ viśvamatra samanvitam 1.
vedavedāṃga tattvākhyaṃ sadasadūpamavyayam .. 5 ..
5.261.d:
एतद्ब्रह्ममयं बीजं विश्वमत्र समन्वितम् 1.
वेदवेदांग तत्त्वाख्यं सदसदूपमव्ययम् .. 5 ..
5.261.m: This seed-syllable consists of brahman; the universe is contained within it. / Known as the essence of the Veda and Vedāṅgas, it is the immutable form of being and non-being. (5)

5.261.s:
nakāraḥ pītavarṇastu jalabījaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
bījaṃ pṛthvī manaśchando viṣahā viniyogataḥ .. 6 ..
5.261.d:
नकारः पीतवर्णस्तु जलबीजः सनातनः ..
बीजं पृथ्वी मनश्छन्दो विषहा विनियोगतः .. 6 ..
5.261.m: The syllable 'na' is yellow, the eternal seed of water; / its seed is the earth, its meter is manas, and by ritual application it counteracts poison. (6)

5.261.s:
mokāraḥ pṛthivī bījo viśvāmitrasamanvitaḥ ..
raktavarṇo mahātejā dhanado viniyojitaḥ . 7 ..

मोकारः पृथिवी बीजो विश्वामित्रसमन्वितः ..
रक्तवर्णो महातेजा धनदो विनियोजितः . 7 ..
5.261.m: The syllable 'mo' has earth as its seed, is associated with Viśvāmitra, / is red in color, of great splendor, and when applied bestows wealth. (7)

5.261.s:
bhakāraḥ paṃcavarṇastu jalabījaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
marīcinā samāyuktaḥ pūjitaḥ sarvabhogadaḥ .. 8 ..
5.261.d:
भकारः पंचवर्णस्तु जलबीजः सनातनः ..
मरीचिना समायुक्तः पूजितः सर्वभोगदः .. 8 ..
5.261.m: The syllable 'bha' has five colors, is the eternal seed of water, / associated with Marīci; worshipped, it grants all enjoyments. (8)

5.261.s:
gakāro hemaraktābho bharadvājasamanvitaḥ ..
vāyubījo viniryogaṃ kurvatāmādibhogadaḥ ... 9 ..
vakāraḥ kundadhavalo vyomabījo mahābalaḥ ..
ṛṣimaṃtripuraskṛtya yojito mokṣadāyakaḥ .. 6.262.10 .1
5.261.d:
गकारो हेमरक्ताभो भरद्वाजसमन्वितः ..
वायुबीजो विनिर्योगं कुर्वतामादिभोगदः ... 9 ..
वकारः कुन्दधवलो व्योमबीजो महाबलः ..
ऋषिमंत्रिपुरस्कृत्य योजितो मोक्षदायकः .. 6.262.10 .1
5.261.m:
The syllable 'ga' has the luster of red gold, is associated with Bharadvāja, / has wind as its seed, and grants primal enjoyment to those who apply it. (9)
The syllable 'va' is white as a kunda flower, has space as its seed, is very powerful; / placed in front of the seer and mantra, when employed it bestows liberation. (10)

5.261.s:
takāro vidyudvikāraḥ somabījaṃ mahatsmṛtam ..
aṃgirāvarddhamūlaṃ ca varjitaṃ karmakā mikam 1. 11 ..
5.261.d:
तकारो विद्युद्विकारः सोमबीजं महत्स्मृतम् ..
अंगिरावर्द्धमूलं च वर्जितं कर्मका मिकम् 1. 11 ..
5.261.m: The syllable 'ta' is a transformation of lightning, regarded as the great seed of Soma; / it has Aṅgiras as its half-root and is free from self-interested ritual action. (11)

5.261.s:
vākāro dhūmravarṇaśca sūryabījaṃ manojavam ..
pulastyarṣisamāyuktaṃ niyuktaṃ sarvasaukhyadam .1 12 ..
5.261.d:
वाकारो धूम्रवर्णश्च सूर्यबीजं मनोजवम् ..
पुलस्त्यर्षिसमायुक्तं नियुक्तं सर्वसौख्यदम् .1 12 ..
5.261.m: The syllable 'vā' is smoke-colored, the seed of the Sun, swift as thought; / associated with the seer Pulastya, when applied it grants all happiness. (12)

5.261.s:
sukāraścākṣaro nityaṃ japākusuma bhāsvaraḥ ..
mano bījaṃ durviṣahyaṃ pulahāśritamarthidam .. 13 ..
dekārākṣarakaṃ bījaṃ haṃsarūpaṃ ca karburam .1 .
5.261.d:
सुकारश्चाक्षरो नित्यं जपाकुसुम भास्वरः ..
मनो बीजं दुर्विषह्यं पुलहाश्रितमर्थिदम् .. 13 ..
देकाराक्षरकं बीजं हंसरूपं च कर्बुरम् .1 .
5.261.m:
The eternal syllable 'su' shines like a hibiscus flower; / its seed is the mind, hard to endure, supported by Pulaha, bestowing wealth. (13)
The seed-syllable 'de' has the form of a goose and is variegated;

5.261.s: siddhibījaṃ mahāsattvaṃ kratau kratuniyojitam .. 14 ..
5.261.d: सिद्धिबीजं महासत्त्वं क्रतौ क्रतुनियोजितम् .. 14 ..
5.261.m: it is the seed of perfection, possessed of great being, employed in sacrifice after sacrifice. (14)

5.261.s:
vākāro nirmalo nityaṃ yajamānastu bījabhṛt ..
pracetāśriyamāśreyaṃ mokṣe mokṣapradāyakam .. 15 ..
5.261.d:
वाकारो निर्मलो नित्यं यजमानस्तु बीजभृत् ..
प्रचेताश्रियमाश्रेयं मोक्षे मोक्षप्रदायकम् .. 15 ..
5.261.m: The syllable 'vā' is ever spotless; the patron of the sacrifice bears the seed; / resorting to the prosperity of Pracetas, it bestows liberation in times of release. (15)

5.261.s:
yakārasya mahābījaṃ piṃgavarṇaśca khecarī ..
bhūcarī ca mahāsiddhiḥ sarvadā bhūvicintanam .. 16 ..
5.261.d:
यकारस्य महाबीजं पिंगवर्णश्च खेचरी ..
भूचरी च महासिद्धिः सर्वदा भूविचिन्तनम् .. 16 ..
5.261.m: The great seed of the syllable 'ya' is reddish-brown, [associated with] Khecarī / and Bhūcarī, a great perfection, ever contemplating the earth. (16)

5.261.s:
bhṛguyantre samāśrāṃtiniyoge sarvakarmakṛt ..
gāyatrīchaṃda eteṣāṃ dehanyāsakramo bhavet .. 17 ..
5.261.d:
भृगुयन्त्रे समाश्रांतिनियोगे सर्वकर्मकृत् ..
गायत्रीछंद एतेषां देहन्यासक्रमो भवेत् .. 17 ..
5.261.m: In the yantra of Bhṛgu it brings total peace; in application it accomplishes all rites. / Their meter is Gāyatrī; this is the sequence of ritual placement on the body: (17)

5.261.s:
oṃkāraṃ sarvadā nyasyannakāraṃ pādayordvayoḥ ..
mokāraṃ guhyadeśe tu bhakāraṃ nābhipaṃkaje .. 18 ..
5.261.d:
ओंकारं सर्वदा न्यस्यन्नकारं पादयोर्द्वयोः ..
मोकारं गुह्यदेशे तु भकारं नाभिपंकजे .. 18 ..
5.261.m: One should always place the oṃkāra, and the syllable 'na' on both feet, / the syllable 'mo' in the secret region, and the syllable 'bha' on the navel lotus, (18)

5.261.s:
gakāraṃ hṛdaye nyasya vakāraḥ kaṇṭha madhyagaḥ ..
tekāraṃ dakṣiṇe haste vākāro vāmahastagaḥ .. 19 ..
5.261.d:
गकारं हृदये न्यस्य वकारः कण्ठ मध्यगः ..
तेकारं दक्षिणे हस्ते वाकारो वामहस्तगः .. 19 ..
5.261.m: having placed the syllable 'ga' in the heart; the syllable 'va' is situated in the middle of the throat; / the syllable 'te' on the right hand, and the syllable 'vā' on the left hand, (19)

5.261.s:
sukāraṃ mukhajihvāyāṃ dekāraḥ karṇayordvayoḥ ..
vākāraścakṣuṣordvandve yakāraṃ mastake nyaset .. 6.262.20 ..
5.261.d:
सुकारं मुखजिह्वायां देकारः कर्णयोर्द्वयोः ..
वाकारश्चक्षुषोर्द्वन्द्वे यकारं मस्तके न्यसेत् .. 6.262.20 ..
5.261.m: the syllable 'su' on the mouth and tongue, the syllable 'de' on both ears, / the syllable 'vā' on both eyes, and one should place the syllable 'ya' on the head. (20)

5.261.s:
liṃgamudrā yonimudrā dhenumudrā tathā trayam ..
sakalaṃ kṛtametaddhi maṃtrarūpe bijākṣaram .. 21 ..
5.261.d:
लिंगमुद्रा योनिमुद्रा धेनुमुद्रा तथा त्रयम् ..
सकलं कृतमेतद्धि मंत्ररूपे बिजाक्षरम् .. 21 ..
5.261.m: The liṅgamudrā, the yonimudrā, and likewise the dhenumudrā: these three / are completely formed in this seed-syllable that takes the form of a mantra. (21)

5.261.s:
yojayetpratyahaṃ devi na sa pāpaiḥ pralipyate ..
etaddvādaśaliṃgāraṃ kūrmasthaṃ dvādaśākṣaram .. 22 ..
5.261.d:
योजयेत्प्रत्यहं देवि न स पापैः प्रलिप्यते ..
एतद्द्वादशलिंगारं कूर्मस्थं द्वादशाक्षरम् .. 22 ..
5.261.m: Whoever applies it daily, O goddess, is not tainted by sins. / This twelve-syllable [mantra] has twelve liṅgas and rests upon the tortoise. (22)

5.261.s:
śālagrāmaśilāścaiva dvādaśaiva hi pūjitāḥ ..
tābhiḥ sahākarairebhiḥ pratyakṣaiḥ saha saṃsadi .. 23 ..
5.261.d:
शालग्रामशिलाश्चैव द्वादशैव हि पूजिताः ..
ताभिः सहाकरैरेभिः प्रत्यक्षैः सह संसदि .. 23 ..
5.261.m: Indeed, twelve Śālagrāma stones are worshipped; / together with them and these visible syllables in the assembly, (23)

5.261.s:
yathāvarṇamanudhyānairmunibījasamanvitaiḥ ..
viniyogena sahitaiśchandobhiḥ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ .. 24 ..
5.261.d:
यथावर्णमनुध्यानैर्मुनिबीजसमन्वितैः ..
विनियोगेन सहितैश्छन्दोभिः समलंकृतैः .. 24 ..
5.261.m: accompanied by continuous meditations according to each syllable, endowed with the sages and seeds, / accompanied by application and adorned with meters, (24)

5.261.s:
dhyānaijapaiḥ pūjitaiśca bhaktānāṃ munisattama ..
mokṣo bhavati bandhebhyaḥ karmajebhyo na saṃśayaḥ .. 258 ..
ayaṃ hi dhyānakarmākhyo yogo duṣprāpya eva hi ..
dhyānayogaṃ punarvacmi śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasā .. 26 ..
dhyānayogena pāpānāṃ kṣayo bhavati nānyathā ..
japadhyānamayo yogaḥ karmayogo na saṃśayaḥ .. 27 ..
śabdabrahmasamudbhūto vedena dvādaśākṣaraḥ ..
dhyānena sarvamāpnoti dhyānenāpnoti śuddhatām .. 28 ..
dhyānena paramaṃ brahma mūrttau yogastu dhyānajaḥ ..
sāvalambo dhyānayogo yannārāyaṇadarśanam .. 29..
dvitīyo nikhilālambo jñānayogena kīrtitaḥ ..
arūpamaprameyaṃ yatsarvakāyaṃ mahaḥ sadā .. 6.262.30 ..
taḍitkoṭisamaprakhyaṃ sadoditamakhaṃḍitam ..
niṣkalaṃ sakalaṃ vāpi niraṃjanamayaṃ viyat .. 31 ..
5.261.d:
ध्यानैजपैः पूजितैश्च भक्तानां मुनिसत्तम ..
मोक्षो भवति बन्धेभ्यः कर्मजेभ्यो न संशयः .. 258 ..
अयं हि ध्यानकर्माख्यो योगो दुष्प्राप्य एव हि ..
ध्यानयोगं पुनर्वच्मि शृणुष्वैकाग्रमानसा .. 26 ..
ध्यानयोगेन पापानां क्षयो भवति नान्यथा ..
जपध्यानमयो योगः कर्मयोगो न संशयः .. 27 ..
शब्दब्रह्मसमुद्भूतो वेदेन द्वादशाक्षरः ..
ध्यानेन सर्वमाप्नोति ध्यानेनाप्नोति शुद्धताम् .. 28 ..
ध्यानेन परमं ब्रह्म मूर्त्तौ योगस्तु ध्यानजः ..
सावलम्बो ध्यानयोगो यन्नारायणदर्शनम् .. 29..
द्वितीयो निखिलालम्बो ज्ञानयोगेन कीर्तितः ..
अरूपमप्रमेयं यत्सर्वकायं महः सदा .. 6.262.30 ..
तडित्कोटिसमप्रख्यं सदोदितमखंडितम् ..
निष्कलं सकलं वापि निरंजनमयं वियत् .. 31 ..
5.261.m:
worshipped with meditations and recitations by devotees, O best of sages, / there is liberation from the bonds born of karma, without a doubt. (25)
This yoga called meditation and ritual action is indeed difficult to attain. / I shall speak again of the yoga of meditation; listen with single-pointed mind: // 26
Through the yoga of meditation, the destruction of sins takes place—not otherwise. / Yoga consisting of recitation and meditation is karma-yoga, without a doubt. // 27
Originating from the sound-Brahman, [taught] through the Veda, is the twelve-syllabled [mantra]. / Through meditation one obtains everything; through meditation one obtains purity. // 28
Through meditation [one attains] the supreme Brahman; in an image, however, yoga is born of meditation. / The yoga of meditation with support is the darśana of Nārāyaṇa. // 29
The second, having all as support, is proclaimed by the yoga of knowledge: / that which is formless, immeasurable, omnipresent, eternal radiance, // 30
resembling ten million lightnings, ever risen, unbroken, / partless or with parts, taintless space; // 31

5.261.s:
tatsvarūpaṃ bhogarūpaṃ turyātītamanopamam ..
vibhrāṃtakaraṇaṃ mūrtaṃ prakṛtisthaṃ ca śāśvatam.. 32 ..
dṛśyādṛśyamajaṃ caiva vairājaṃ satatojjvalam ..
bahulaṃ sarvajaṃ dharmyaṃ nirvikalpamanīśvaram .. 33 ..
agotraṃ varaṇaṃ vāpi brahmāṃḍaśatakāraṇam ..
nirīhaṃ nirmamaṃ buddhiśūnyarūpaṃ ca nirmalam .. 34 ..
tadīśarūpaṃ nirdehaṃ nirdvaṃdvaṃ sākṣimātrakam ..
śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ dhyātṛdhyeyavivarjitam ..
nopameyamagādhaṃ tvaṃ svīkuruṣva svatejasā .. 35 ..
.. pārvatyuvāca .. ..
tatkathaṃ prāpyate samyagjñānaṃ yogisvarūpiṇam..
nārāyaṇamamūrtaṃ ca sthānaṃ tasya vada prabho .. 36 ..
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
śiraḥ pradhānaṃ gātreṣu śirasā dhāryate mahān.. .. 37..
śirasā pūjito devaḥ pūjitaṃ sakalaṃ jagat ..
śirasā dhāryate yogaḥ śirasā dhriyate balam .. 38 ..
5.261.d:
तत्स्वरूपं भोगरूपं तुर्यातीतमनोपमम् ..
विभ्रांतकरणं मूर्तं प्रकृतिस्थं च शाश्वतम्.. 32 ..
दृश्यादृश्यमजं चैव वैराजं सततोज्ज्वलम् ..
बहुलं सर्वजं धर्म्यं निर्विकल्पमनीश्वरम् .. 33 ..
अगोत्रं वरणं वापि ब्रह्मांडशतकारणम् ..
निरीहं निर्ममं बुद्धिशून्यरूपं च निर्मलम् .. 34 ..
तदीशरूपं निर्देहं निर्द्वंद्वं साक्षिमात्रकम् ..
शुद्धस्फटिकसंकाशं ध्यातृध्येयविवर्जितम् ..
नोपमेयमगाधं त्वं स्वीकुरुष्व स्वतेजसा .. 35 ..
.. पार्वत्युवाच .. ..
तत्कथं प्राप्यते सम्यग्ज्ञानं योगिस्वरूपिणम्..
नारायणममूर्तं च स्थानं तस्य वद प्रभो .. 36 ..
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
शिरः प्रधानं गात्रेषु शिरसा धार्यते महान्.. .. 37..
शिरसा पूजितो देवः पूजितं सकलं जगत् ..
शिरसा धार्यते योगः शिरसा ध्रियते बलम् .. 38 ..
5.261.m:
that essential nature of enjoyment, beyond the fourth [state], beyond the mind, / confusing the senses, formed yet resting in prakṛti, and eternal; // 32
visible and invisible, unborn, cosmic, constantly blazing, / abundant, born of all, righteous, conceptualization-free, without a lord; // 33
without lineage or choice, the cause of hundreds of universes, / free from longing, free from possessiveness, having a nature devoid of intellect, and spotless. // 34
That form of the Lord is bodiless, beyond duality, a mere witness, / resembling pure crystal, devoid of meditator and meditated upon, / incomparable, unfathomable—accept it by your own splendor! // 35
Pārvatī said: / How is that true knowledge, whose form is the yogin, / and the formless Nārāyaṇa, to be properly attained? Speak of his place, O Lord! // 36
Īśvara said: / The head is principal among the limbs; the great [being] is borne in the head. / Honored by the head, the god is honored; the whole universe is honored. / Yoga is held in the head; strength is held in the head; // 38

5.261.s:
śirasā dhriyate tejo jīvitaṃ śirasi sthitam ..
sūryaḥ śiro hyamūrttasya mūrtasyāpi tathaiva ca .. 39 ..
urastu pṛthivīlokaḥ pādaścaiva rasātalam ..
ayaṃ brahmāṃḍarūpe ca mūrttāmūrttasvarūpataḥ .. 6.262.40 ..
viṣṇureva brahmarūpo jñānayogāśrayaḥ svayam ..
sṛjate sarvabhūtāni pālayatyapi sarvaśaḥ .. 41 ..
vināśayati sarvaṃ hi sarvadevamayo hyayam ..
sarvamāseṣvādhipatyaṃ yasya viṣṇoḥ sanātanam .. 42 ..
tasmātsarveṣu māseṣu sarveṣu divaseṣvapi ..
sarveṣu yāmakāleṣu saṃsmaranmucyate harim .. 43 ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa dhyānamātrātpramucyate ..
amūrttasevanaṃ gaṃgātīrthadhyānādvaraṃ param .. 44 ..
sarvadānottaraṃ caiva cāturmāsye na saṃśayaḥ ..
sarvamāsakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ cāturmāsye śubhāśubham .. 45 ..
akṣayyaṃ tadbhaveddevi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena jñānayogo bahūttamaḥ .. .. 46 ..
5.261.d:
शिरसा ध्रियते तेजो जीवितं शिरसि स्थितम् ..
सूर्यः शिरो ह्यमूर्त्तस्य मूर्तस्यापि तथैव च .. 39 ..
उरस्तु पृथिवीलोकः पादश्चैव रसातलम् ..
अयं ब्रह्मांडरूपे च मूर्त्तामूर्त्तस्वरूपतः .. 6.262.40 ..
विष्णुरेव ब्रह्मरूपो ज्ञानयोगाश्रयः स्वयम् ..
सृजते सर्वभूतानि पालयत्यपि सर्वशः .. 41 ..
विनाशयति सर्वं हि सर्वदेवमयो ह्ययम् ..
सर्वमासेष्वाधिपत्यं यस्य विष्णोः सनातनम् .. 42 ..
तस्मात्सर्वेषु मासेषु सर्वेषु दिवसेष्वपि ..
सर्वेषु यामकालेषु संस्मरन्मुच्यते हरिम् .. 43 ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण ध्यानमात्रात्प्रमुच्यते ..
अमूर्त्तसेवनं गंगातीर्थध्यानाद्वरं परम् .. 44 ..
सर्वदानोत्तरं चैव चातुर्मास्ये न संशयः ..
सर्वमासकृतं पापं चातुर्मास्ये शुभाशुभम् .. 45 ..
अक्षय्यं तद्भवेद्देवि नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन ज्ञानयोगो बहूत्तमः .. .. 46 ..
5.261.m:
splendor is held in the head; life is situated in the head. / The sun is indeed the head of the formless one, and likewise of the formed one. // 39
The chest is the earthly realm, and the foot is Rasātala. / This [universe] is in the form of the cosmic egg, through formed and formless nature. // 40
Viṣṇu alone is the nature of Brahman, himself the resort of the yoga of knowledge. / He creates all beings and protects [them] in every way; // 41
and he destroys everything, for he consists of all gods. / Eternal is the sovereignty of this Viṣṇu over all months. // 42
Therefore, in all months, on all days, / [and] at all watches of the day, remembering Hari, one is liberated. // 43
During the four-month rainy season especially, one is fully liberated by mere meditation. / Service of the formless is superior to meditation at the sacred ford of the Gaṅgā; // 44
and it surpasses all gifts in the four-month rainy season, without a doubt. / Good and evil sin committed in all months, in the four-month rainy season // 45
becomes imperishable, O goddess; there is no deliberation to be made here. / Therefore, with all effort, the yoga of knowledge is far superior. // 46

5.261.s:
sevito viṣṇurūpeṇa brahmamokṣapradāyakaḥ ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahitā bhūtvā mūrttāmūrte sthitiṃ śubhe .. 407 ..
na kathyeyaṃ yasya kasya sutasyāpya parasya ca ..
adāṃtāyātha duṣṭāya calacittāya dāṃbhike .. 48 ..
svavākcyutāya niṃdyāya na vācyā yogajā kathā ..
nityabhaktāya dāṃtāya śamādi guṇine tathā .. 49 .. .
viṣṇubhaktāya dātavyā śūdrāyāpi dvijanmane ..
abhaktāyāpyaśucaye brahmasthānaṃ na kathyate .. 6.262.50 ..
madbhaktyā yogasiddhiṃ tvaṃ gṛhāṇāśu tapodhane ..
abhūtaṃ jñānagamyaṃ taṃ viddhi nārāyaṇaṃ param .. 51 ..
nādarūpeṇa śirasi tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ sarvadehinām ..
sa eva jīvaśirasi varttate sūryabiṃbavat .. 52 ..
sadoditaḥ sūkṣmarūpo mūrtto mūrtyā praṇīyate ..
abhyāsena sadā devi prāpyate paramātmakaḥ .. 53 ..
5.261.d:
सेवितो विष्णुरूपेण ब्रह्ममोक्षप्रदायकः ..
शृणुष्वावहिता भूत्वा मूर्त्तामूर्ते स्थितिं शुभे .. 407 ..
न कथ्येयं यस्य कस्य सुतस्याप्य परस्य च ..
अदांतायाथ दुष्टाय चलचित्ताय दांभिके .. 48 ..
स्ववाक्च्युताय निंद्याय न वाच्या योगजा कथा ..
नित्यभक्ताय दांताय शमादि गुणिने तथा .. 49 .. .
विष्णुभक्ताय दातव्या शूद्रायापि द्विजन्मने ..
अभक्तायाप्यशुचये ब्रह्मस्थानं न कथ्यते .. 6.262.50 ..
मद्भक्त्या योगसिद्धिं त्वं गृहाणाशु तपोधने ..
अभूतं ज्ञानगम्यं तं विद्धि नारायणं परम् .. 51 ..
नादरूपेण शिरसि तिष्ठंतं सर्वदेहिनाम् ..
स एव जीवशिरसि वर्त्तते सूर्यबिंबवत् .. 52 ..
सदोदितः सूक्ष्मरूपो मूर्त्तो मूर्त्या प्रणीयते ..
अभ्यासेन सदा देवि प्राप्यते परमात्मकः .. 53 ..
5.261.m:
Practiced as the form of Viṣṇu, it grants the liberation that is Brahman. / Listen attentively, O auspicious one, to the state in the formed and the formless: // 47
It should not be spoken to just anyone, nor to a son, nor to a stranger, / nor to the uncontrolled, the wicked, the fickle-minded, or a hypocrite, // 48
nor to one fallen from his word, nor to the blameworthy; the discourse born of yoga must not be told [to them]. / To the constantly devoted, the self-controlled, who possesses calmness and other virtues, // 49
devoted to Viṣṇu—whether a twice-born or even a śūdra—it should be given. / To the non-devotee and the impure, the place of Brahman is not spoken. // 50
Through devotion to me, quickly seize the perfection of yoga, O rich in austerity! / Know that supreme Nārāyaṇa to be uncreated, approachable through knowledge, // 51
standing in the form of sound in the head of all embodied beings. / He alone abides in the head of the living soul like the solar orb; // 52
ever risen, subtle in form, formed, he is guided through form. / Through constant practice, O goddess, the supreme self is attained. // 53

5.261.s:
śarīre sakalā devā yogino nivasaṃti hi ..
karṇe tu dakṣiṇe nadyo nivasaṃti tathā'parāḥ .. 54 ..
hṛdaye ceśvaraḥ śaṃbhurnābhau brahmā sanātanaḥ ..
pṛthvī pādatalāgre jalaṃ sarvagataṃ tathā .. 55 ..
tejo vāyustathā''kāśaṃ vidyate bhālamadhyataḥ..
haste ca paṃca tīrthāni dakṣiṇe nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 56 ..
sūryo yaddakṣiṇaṃ netraṃ candro vāmamudāhṛtam ..
bhaumaścaiva budhaścaiva nāsike dve udāhṛte .. 57 ..
guruśca dakṣiṇe karṇe vāmakarṇe tathā bhṛguḥ ..
mukhe śanaiścaraḥ prokto gude rāhuḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 58 ..
keturiṃdriyagaḥ prokto grahāḥ sarve śarīragāḥ ..
yogino dehamāsādya bhuvanāni caturdaśa .. 59 ..
pravarttaṃte sadā devi tasmādyogaṃ sadābhyaset ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa yogī pāpaṃ nikṛntati .. 6.262.60 ..
5.261.d:
शरीरे सकला देवा योगिनो निवसंति हि ..
कर्णे तु दक्षिणे नद्यो निवसंति तथाऽपराः .. 54 ..
हृदये चेश्वरः शंभुर्नाभौ ब्रह्मा सनातनः ..
पृथ्वी पादतलाग्रे जलं सर्वगतं तथा .. 55 ..
तेजो वायुस्तथा'ऽकाशं विद्यते भालमध्यतः..
हस्ते च पंच तीर्थानि दक्षिणे नात्र संशयः .. 56 ..
सूर्यो यद्दक्षिणं नेत्रं चन्द्रो वाममुदाहृतम् ..
भौमश्चैव बुधश्चैव नासिके द्वे उदाहृते .. 57 ..
गुरुश्च दक्षिणे कर्णे वामकर्णे तथा भृगुः ..
मुखे शनैश्चरः प्रोक्तो गुदे राहुः प्रकीर्तितः .. 58 ..
केतुरिंद्रियगः प्रोक्तो ग्रहाः सर्वे शरीरगाः ..
योगिनो देहमासाद्य भुवनानि चतुर्दश .. 59 ..
प्रवर्त्तंते सदा देवि तस्माद्योगं सदाभ्यसेत् ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण योगी पापं निकृन्तति .. 6.262.60 ..
5.261.m:
All the gods indeed dwell in the body of the yogin: / in the right ear rivers dwell, and likewise others [elsewhere]. // 54
In the heart is Īśvara, Śambhu; in the navel is eternal Brahmā; / the earth is at the tip of the soles of the feet, and water is all-pervading; // 55
fire, wind, and ether exist in the middle of the forehead; / and in the right hand are the five sacred fords, of this there is no doubt. // 56
The right eye is said to be the sun, the left is declared to be the moon; / Mars and Mercury are declared to be the two nostrils; // 57
Jupiter is in the right ear, and likewise Venus in the left ear; / Saturn is said to be in the mouth, and Rāhu is proclaimed in the anus; // 58
Ketu is said to be in the sense organs; all planets dwell in the body. / Reaching the body of the yogin, the fourteen worlds // 59
are always active, O goddess; therefore one should constantly practice yoga. / Particularly in the four-month rainy season, the yogin cuts down sin. // 60

5.261.s:
muhūrttamapi yo yogī mastake dhārayenmanaḥ ..
karṇai pidhāya pāpebhyo mucyate'sau na saṃśayaḥ .. 61 ..
aṃtaraṃ naiva paśyāmi viṣṇoryogaparasya vā ..
eko'pi yogī yadgehe grāsamātraṃ bhunakti ca .. 62 ..
kulāni trīṇi so'vaśyaṃ tārayedātmanā saha ..
yadi vipro bhavedyogī so'vaśyaṃ darśanādapi .. 63 ..
sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ devi pāparāśi niṣūdakaḥ ..
sakriyo brahmanirataḥ sacchūdro yogabhāgyadi .. 64 ..
bhavetsadgurubhakto vā so'pyamūrttaphalaṃ labhet ..
yo yogī niyatāhāraḥ parabrahma samādhimān .. 65 ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa harau sa layabhāgbhavet ..
yathā siddhakarasparśāllohaṃ bhavati kāṃcanam .. 66 ..
tathā mūrttaṃ hariprītyā manuṣyo layamāvrajet ..
yathā mārgajalaṃ gaṃgāpatitaṃ tridaśairapi .. 67 ..
5.261.d:
मुहूर्त्तमपि यो योगी मस्तके धारयेन्मनः ..
कर्णै पिधाय पापेभ्यो मुच्यतेऽसौ न संशयः .. 61 ..
अंतरं नैव पश्यामि विष्णोर्योगपरस्य वा ..
एकोऽपि योगी यद्गेहे ग्रासमात्रं भुनक्ति च .. 62 ..
कुलानि त्रीणि सोऽवश्यं तारयेदात्मना सह ..
यदि विप्रो भवेद्योगी सोऽवश्यं दर्शनादपि .. 63 ..
सर्वेषां प्राणिनां देवि पापराशि निषूदकः ..
सक्रियो ब्रह्मनिरतः सच्छूद्रो योगभाग्यदि .. 64 ..
भवेत्सद्गुरुभक्तो वा सोऽप्यमूर्त्तफलं लभेत् ..
यो योगी नियताहारः परब्रह्म समाधिमान् .. 65 ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण हरौ स लयभाग्भवेत् ..
यथा सिद्धकरस्पर्शाल्लोहं भवति कांचनम् .. 66 ..
तथा मूर्त्तं हरिप्रीत्या मनुष्यो लयमाव्रजेत् ..
यथा मार्गजलं गंगापतितं त्रिदशैरपि .. 67 ..
5.261.m:
A yogin who holds his mind in the crown of his head even for a muhūrta, / closing his ears, is freed from sins, without a doubt. // 61
I perceive no difference between Viṣṇu and one devoted to yoga. / If even a single yogin eats a mere morsel in someone's home, // 62
he will surely deliver three family lines along with himself. / If a brahmin becomes a yogin, by his mere darśana he will surely // 63
be the destroyer of the mass of sins of all living beings, O goddess. / If an active, righteous śūdra devoted to Brahman partakes of yoga, // 64
or becomes devoted to a true guru, he too obtains the formless fruit. / That yogin of regulated diet who is absorbed in the supreme Brahman, // 65
particularly during the four-month rainy season, partakes of dissolution in Hari. / Just as iron turns to gold by the touch of an adept's hand, // 66
so a man, though formed, attains dissolution out of love for Hari. / Just as road-water falling into the Gaṅgā is honored even by the gods // 67

5.261.s:
sevitaṃ sarvaphaladaṃ tathā yogī vimuktidaḥ ..
yathā gomayamātreṇa vahnirdīpyati sarvadā .. 68 ..
devatānāṃ mukhaṃ taddhi kīrtyate yājñikaiḥ sadā ..
evaṃ yogī sadā'bhyāsājjāyate mokṣabhājanam .. 69 ..
yogo'yaṃ sevyate devi jñānāsiddhipradaḥ sadā ..
sanakādibhirācāryairmumukṣubhiradhīśvaraiḥ .. 6.262.70 ..
prathamaṃ jñānasaṃpattirjāyate yogināṃ sadā ..
teṣāṃ gṛhītamātrastu yogī bhavati pārvati .. 71 ..
tatastu siddhayastasya tvaṇimādyāḥ purogatāḥ ..
bhavanti tatrāpi mano na dadyādyogināṃ varaḥ .. 72 ..
sarvadānakratubhavaṃ puṇyaṃ bhavati yogataḥ ..
yogātsakalakāmāptirna yogādbhuvi prāpyate .. 73 ..
yogānna hṛdayagraṃthirna yogānmamatā ripuḥ ..
na yogasiddhasya mano harttuṃ kenāpi śakyate .. 74 ..
5.261.d:
सेवितं सर्वफलदं तथा योगी विमुक्तिदः ..
यथा गोमयमात्रेण वह्निर्दीप्यति सर्वदा .. 68 ..
देवतानां मुखं तद्धि कीर्त्यते याज्ञिकैः सदा ..
एवं योगी सदाऽभ्यासाज्जायते मोक्षभाजनम् .. 69 ..
योगोऽयं सेव्यते देवि ज्ञानासिद्धिप्रदः सदा ..
सनकादिभिराचार्यैर्मुमुक्षुभिरधीश्वरैः .. 6.262.70 ..
प्रथमं ज्ञानसंपत्तिर्जायते योगिनां सदा ..
तेषां गृहीतमात्रस्तु योगी भवति पार्वति .. 71 ..
ततस्तु सिद्धयस्तस्य त्वणिमाद्याः पुरोगताः ..
भवन्ति तत्रापि मनो न दद्याद्योगिनां वरः .. 72 ..
सर्वदानक्रतुभवं पुण्यं भवति योगतः ..
योगात्सकलकामाप्तिर्न योगाद्भुवि प्राप्यते .. 73 ..
योगान्न हृदयग्रंथिर्न योगान्ममता रिपुः ..
न योगसिद्धस्य मनो हर्त्तुं केनापि शक्यते .. 74 ..
5.261.m:
and grants all fruits, so the yogin bestows liberation. / Just as fire blazes constantly from mere cow-dung, // 68
and that is always praised by sacrificers as the mouth of the gods, / so through constant practice the yogin becomes a vessel of liberation. // 69
This yoga is always cultivated, O goddess, granting knowledge and perfection, / by masters such as Sanaka and others, lords who desire liberation. (70)
First, the wealth of knowledge always arises for yogins; / as soon as it is grasped by them, O Pārvatī, one becomes a [true] yogin. (71)
Then perfections such as anima and the rest present themselves before him; / even there, the best of yogins should not fix his mind. (72)
The merit arising from all gifts and sacrifices comes from yoga; / from yoga comes the attainment of all desires; what on earth is not obtained through yoga? (73)
Through yoga there is no knot of the heart; through yoga the enemy 'sense of mine' does not exist; / no one can steal away the mind of one perfected in yoga. (74)

5.261.s:
sa eva vimalo yogī yaccittaṃ śirasi sthitam ..
sthirībhūtavyathaṃ nityaṃ daśamadvārasaṃpuṭe .. 75 ..
kaṇauṃ pidhāya martyasya nādarūpaṃ vicinvataḥ ..
tadeva praṇavasyāgraṃ tadeva brahma śāśvatam .. 76 ..
tadevānaṃtarūpākhyaṃ tadevāmṛtamuttamam ..
ghrāṇavāyau praghoṣo'yaṃ jaṭharāgnermahatpadam .. 77 ..
paṃcabhūtaṃ nivāsaṃ yajjñānarūpamidaṃ padam ..
padaṃ prāpya vimuktiḥ syājjanmasaṃsārabaṃdhanāt .. 78 ..
yadāptirdulabhā loke yogasiddhipradāyikā .. 79 ..
evaṃ brahmamayaṃ vibhāti sakalaṃ viśvaṃ caraṃ sthāvaraṃ vijñānākhyamidaṃ padaṃ sa bhagavānviṣṇuḥ svayaṃ vyāpakaḥ ..
jñātvā taṃ śirasi sthitaṃ bahuvaraṃ yogeśvarāṇāṃ paraṃ prāṇī muṃcati sarpavajjagatijāṃ nirmokamāyākṛtim .. 6.262.80 ..
5.261.d:
स एव विमलो योगी यच्चित्तं शिरसि स्थितम् ..
स्थिरीभूतव्यथं नित्यं दशमद्वारसंपुटे .. 75 ..
कणौं पिधाय मर्त्यस्य नादरूपं विचिन्वतः ..
तदेव प्रणवस्याग्रं तदेव ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् .. 76 ..
तदेवानंतरूपाख्यं तदेवामृतमुत्तमम् ..
घ्राणवायौ प्रघोषोऽयं जठराग्नेर्महत्पदम् .. 77 ..
पंचभूतं निवासं यज्ज्ञानरूपमिदं पदम् ..
पदं प्राप्य विमुक्तिः स्याज्जन्मसंसारबंधनात् .. 78 ..
यदाप्तिर्दुलभा लोके योगसिद्धिप्रदायिका .. 79 ..
एवं ब्रह्ममयं विभाति सकलं विश्वं चरं स्थावरं विज्ञानाख्यमिदं पदं स भगवान्विष्णुः स्वयं व्यापकः ..
ज्ञात्वा तं शिरसि स्थितं बहुवरं योगेश्वराणां परं प्राणी मुंचति सर्पवज्जगतिजां निर्मोकमायाकृतिम् .. 6.262.80 ..
5.261.m:
He alone is a stainless yogin whose mind is fixed in the head, / its distress perpetually calmed, in the cavity of the tenth door. (75)
When a mortal closes his ears and perceives the form of the sound (nāda), / that alone is the peak of the Praṇava (Oṃ), that alone is the eternal Brahman. (76)
That alone is called the infinite form; that alone is the supreme nectar; / this roar in the breath of the nostrils is the great realm of the digestive fire. (77)
The five elements are the dwelling which is this abode consisting of knowledge; / having attained this abode, liberation occurs from the bondage of birth in saṃsāra. (78)
The attainment of which is difficult to obtain in the world, granting perfection in yoga. (79)
Thus the entire universe, moving and unmoving, shines as consisting of Brahman; this abode called discernment is Lord Viṣṇu himself, all-pervading. / Knowing him, the supreme choice of the lords of yoga, dwelling in the head, a living being casts off the illusory form born of the world, just as a serpent casts off its slough. (80)

5.261.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāharasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye jñānayogakathanaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 262 ..
5.261.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहरस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये ज्ञानयोगकथनं नाम द्विषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 262 ..
5.261.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-second chapter, entitled 'Discourse on the Yoga of Knowledge', in the Praise of Cāturmāsya, in the Narrative of the One Reclining on Śeṣa, in the Praise of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skandapurāṇa. (262)

5.262.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
yadi cettāmasaṃ karma tyaktvā karmasu jāyate ..
tadā jñānamayo yogī jīvatāṃ mokṣadāyakaḥ .. 1 ..
5.262.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
यदि चेत्तामसं कर्म त्यक्त्वा कर्मसु जायते ..
तदा ज्ञानमयो योगी जीवतां मोक्षदायकः .. 1 ..
5.262.m: Īśvara said: / If, having abandoned tamasic action, one engages in deeds [without attachment], / then the yogin composed of knowledge grants liberation to the living. (1)

5.262.s:
yadā nirmamatā dehe yadā cittaṃ sunirmalam ..
yadā harau bhaktiyogastadā bandho na karmaṇā .. 2 ..
5.262.d:
यदा निर्ममता देहे यदा चित्तं सुनिर्मलम् ..
यदा हरौ भक्तियोगस्तदा बन्धो न कर्मणा .. 2 ..
5.262.m: When there is absence of mineness in the body, when the mind is exceedingly pure, / and when there is yoga of devotion to Hari, then there is no bondage by karma. (2)

5.262.s:
kurvanneva hi karmāṇi manaḥ śāṃtaṃ nṛṇāṃ yadā ..
tadā yogamayī siddhirjāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 3 ..
5.262.d:
कुर्वन्नेव हि कर्माणि मनः शांतं नृणां यदा ..
तदा योगमयी सिद्धिर्जायते नात्र संशयः .. 3 ..
5.262.m: Indeed, when the mind of men is tranquil while performing actions, / then the perfection consisting of yoga arises; there is no doubt about this. (3)

5.262.s:
gurutvaṃ sthānamasakṛdanubhūya mahāmatiḥ ..
jīvanviṣṇutvamāsādya karma saṃgātpramucyate .. 4 ..
5.262.d:
गुरुत्वं स्थानमसकृदनुभूय महामतिः ..
जीवन्विष्णुत्वमासाद्य कर्म संगात्प्रमुच्यते .. 4 ..
5.262.m: Repeatedly experiencing the greatness and status [of the self], the highly intelligent one, / attaining the nature of Viṣṇu while living, is liberated from attachment to action. (4)

5.262.s:
karmāṇi nityajātāni nityanaimittikāni ca ..
icchayā naiva sevyāni duḥkhatāpavivṛddhaye .. 5 ..
5.262.d:
कर्माणि नित्यजातानि नित्यनैमित्तिकानि च ..
इच्छया नैव सेव्यानि दुःखतापविवृद्धये .. 5 ..
5.262.m: Actions constantly arising, both daily and occasional, / should not be pursued out of desire, for the increase of sorrow and torment. (5)

5.262.s:
karmaṇāmīśitāraṃ ca viṣṇuṃ viddhi maheśvari ..
tasminsaṃtyajya sarvāṇi saṃsārānmucyate'khilāt .. 6 ..
5.262.d:
कर्मणामीशितारं च विष्णुं विद्धि महेश्वरि ..
तस्मिन्संत्यज्य सर्वाणि संसारान्मुच्यतेऽखिलात् .. 6 ..
5.262.m: Know Viṣṇu, O great goddess, to be the master of actions; / renouncing all [actions] unto him, one is released from all of saṃsāra. (6)

5.262.s:
etadeva paraṃ jñānametadeva paraṃ tapaḥ ..
etadeva paraṃ śreyo yatkṛṣṇe karmaṇo'rpaṇam .. 7 ..
5.262.d:
एतदेव परं ज्ञानमेतदेव परं तपः ..
एतदेव परं श्रेयो यत्कृष्णे कर्मणोऽर्पणम् .. 7 ..
5.262.m: This alone is supreme knowledge, this alone is supreme austerity, / this alone is the supreme good: that actions are dedicated to Kṛṣṇa. (7)

5.262.s:
ayaṃ hi nirmalo yogo nirguṇaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ..
tadviṣṇoḥ karma janitaṃ śubhatva pratipādanam .. 8 ..
5.262.d:
अयं हि निर्मलो योगो निर्गुणः स उदाहृतः ..
तद्विष्णोः कर्म जनितं शुभत्व प्रतिपादनम् .. 8 ..
5.262.m: For this is pure yoga; it is declared to be devoid of gunas; / actions born of that Viṣṇu demonstrate auspiciousness. (8)

5.262.s:
tāvadbhramaṃti saṃsāre pitaraḥ piṃḍatatparāḥ ..
yāvatkule bhaktiyutaḥ sto naiva prajāyate 9 ..
5.262.d:
तावद्भ्रमंति संसारे पितरः पिंडतत्पराः ..
यावत्कुले भक्तियुतः स्तो नैव प्रजायते 9 ..
5.262.m: The ancestors intent on the funeral ball wander in saṃsāra only so long / as one endowed with devotion is not born in the family. (9)

5.262.s:
tāvaddvijāni garjaṃti tāvadgarjati pātakam ..
tāvattīrthānyanekāni yāvadbhaktiṃ na viṃdati .. 6.263.10 ..
5.262.d:
तावद्द्विजानि गर्जंति तावद्गर्जति पातकम् ..
तावत्तीर्थान्यनेकानि यावद्भक्तिं न विंदति .. 6.263.10 ..
5.262.m: Twice-born duties roar so long, sin roars so long, / and numerous sacred fords exist so long, as one does not find devotion. (10)

5.262.s:
sa eva jñānavām̐lloke yogināṃ prathamo hi saḥ ..
mahākratūnāmāhartā haribhaktiyuto hi saḥ .. 11 ..
5.262.d:
स एव ज्ञानवाम्̐ल्लोके योगिनां प्रथमो हि सः ..
महाक्रतूनामाहर्ता हरिभक्तियुतो हि सः .. 11 ..
5.262.m: He alone possesses knowledge in the world; he is the foremost of yogins; / he is the performer of great sacrifices, who is endowed with devotion to Hari. (11)

5.262.s:
nimiṣaṃ nirnayanmeṣaṃ yogaḥ samabhijāyate ..
vāṇījaye yoginastu gomedhaśca prakīrtitaḥ .. .. 12 ..
5.262.d:
निमिषं निर्नयन्मेषं योगः समभिजायते ..
वाणीजये योगिनस्तु गोमेधश्च प्रकीर्तितः .. .. 12 ..
5.262.m: In the closing of an eye, yoga arises; / and for a yogin, victory over speech is proclaimed as a cattle sacrifice. (12)

5.262.s:
manaso vijaye nityamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet ..
kalpanāvijayānnityaṃ yajñaṃ sautrāmaṇiṃ labhet .. 13 ..
5.262.d:
मनसो विजये नित्यमश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ..
कल्पनाविजयान्नित्यं यज्ञं सौत्रामणिं लभेत् .. 13 ..
5.262.m: In the constant victory over the mind, one attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice; / from the constant victory over mental constructs, one attains the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice. (13)

5.262.s:
dehasyotsarjanānnityaṃ narayajñaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
paṃceṃdriyapaśūnhatvā'nagnau śīrṣe ca kuṇḍale .. 14 ..
5.262.d:
देहस्योत्सर्जनान्नित्यं नरयज्ञः प्रकीर्तितः ..
पंचेंद्रियपशून्हत्वाऽनग्नौ शीर्षे च कुण्डले .. 14 ..
5.262.m: From the constant casting off of the body, a human sacrifice is proclaimed. / Having slain the sacrificial beasts of the five senses in the fireless state, in the head and the earrings, (14)

5.262.s:
gurūpadeśavidhinā brahmabhūtatvamaśnute ..
sa yogī niyatāhārodaṇḍatritayadhārakaḥ .. 15 ..
5.262.d:
गुरूपदेशविधिना ब्रह्मभूतत्वमश्नुते ..
स योगी नियताहारोदण्डत्रितयधारकः .. 15 ..
5.262.m: he attains the state of Brahman through the precept of the guru's instruction; / that yogin eats regulated food, holding the three staves. (15)

5.262.s:
tridaṃḍī sa tu vijñeyo jñāte deve niraṃjane ..
manodaṇḍaḥ karmadaṇḍo vāgdaṃḍo yasya yoginaḥ .. 16 ..
5.262.d:
त्रिदंडी स तु विज्ञेयो ज्ञाते देवे निरंजने ..
मनोदण्डः कर्मदण्डो वाग्दंडो यस्य योगिनः .. 16 ..
5.262.m: He is to be known as a bearer of three staves (tridaṇḍin) when the spotless God is known; / the yogin whose staff is the mind, whose staff is action, and whose staff is speech— (16)

5.262.s:
sa yogī brahmarūpeṇa jīvanneva samāpyate ..
ajñānī bādhyate nityaṃ karmabhirbaṃdhanātmakaiḥ ..17 ..
5.262.d:
स योगी ब्रह्मरूपेण जीवन्नेव समाप्यते ..
अज्ञानी बाध्यते नित्यं कर्मभिर्बंधनात्मकैः ..17 ..
5.262.m: that yogin is accomplished even while living, in the form of Brahman; / the ignorant one is constantly afflicted by actions consisting of bondage. (17)

5.262.s:
kurvanneva hi karmāṇi jñānī muktiṃ prayāti hi ..
yadā hi gurubhiḥ sthānaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pratipādyate .. 18 ..
5.262.d:
कुर्वन्नेव हि कर्माणि ज्ञानी मुक्तिं प्रयाति हि ..
यदा हि गुरुभिः स्थानं ब्रह्मणः प्रतिपाद्यते .. 18 ..
5.262.m: Indeed, even while performing actions, the knower attains liberation; / for when the place of Brahman is explained by gurus, (18)

5.262.s:
tadaiṣa muktimāpnoti dehastiṣṭhati kevalam ..
yāvadbrahmaphalāvāptyai prayāti puruṣottamaḥ .. 19 ..
5.262.d:
तदैष मुक्तिमाप्नोति देहस्तिष्ठति केवलम् ..
यावद्ब्रह्मफलावाप्त्यै प्रयाति पुरुषोत्तमः .. 19 ..
5.262.m: then he attains liberation, while the body merely remains; / as long as the supreme person proceeds to attain the fruit of Brahman, (19)

5.262.s:
tāvatkarmamayī vṛttirbrahma vṛkṣāṃtarābhavet ..
avāṃtarāṇi parvāṇi jñeyāni munibhiḥ sadā .. 6.263.20 ..
5.262.d:
तावत्कर्ममयी वृत्तिर्ब्रह्म वृक्षांतराभवेत् ..
अवांतराणि पर्वाणि ज्ञेयानि मुनिभिः सदा .. 6.263.20 ..
5.262.m: so long the activity consisting of action exists inside the tree of Brahman; / intermediate stages are always to be understood by sages. (20)

5.262.s:
mokṣamārgo dvijaiścaiva śrutismṛtisamuccayāt ..
mokṣo'yaṃ nagarākāraścaturdvāra samākulaḥ .. 21 ..
5.262.d:
मोक्षमार्गो द्विजैश्चैव श्रुतिस्मृतिसमुच्चयात् ..
मोक्षोऽयं नगराकारश्चतुर्द्वार समाकुलः .. 21 ..
5.262.m: The path to liberation is known by the twice-born through the combination of Śruti and Smṛti; / this liberation is like a city equipped with four gates. (21)

5.262.s:
dvārapālāstatra nityaṃ catvārastu śamādayaḥ ..
ta eva prathamaṃ sevyā manujairmākṣadāyakāḥ .. 22 ..
5.262.d:
द्वारपालास्तत्र नित्यं चत्वारस्तु शमादयः ..
त एव प्रथमं सेव्या मनुजैर्माक्षदायकाः .. 22 ..
5.262.m: The four gatekeepers there are constantly peace and the rest; / they alone are to be cultivated first by humans, granting liberation: (22)

5.262.s:
śamaśca sadvicāraśca saṃtoṣaḥ sādhusaṃgamaḥ ..
ete vai hastagā yasya tasya siddhirna dūrataḥ .. 23 ..
5.262.d:
शमश्च सद्विचारश्च संतोषः साधुसंगमः ..
एते वै हस्तगा यस्य तस्य सिद्धिर्न दूरतः .. 23 ..
5.262.m: peace, right inquiry, contentment, and association with the virtuous; / for him in whose hands these reside, perfection is not far off. (23)

5.262.s:
yogasiddhirviṣṇubhaktyā saddharmācaraṇena ca ..
prāpyate manujairdevi hyetajjñānamalaṃ viduḥ .. 24 ..
5.262.d:
योगसिद्धिर्विष्णुभक्त्या सद्धर्माचरणेन च ..
प्राप्यते मनुजैर्देवि ह्येतज्ज्ञानमलं विदुः .. 24 ..
5.262.m: Perfection in yoga is attained by humans, O goddess, through devotion to Viṣṇu / and the practice of true righteousness; they know this to be pure knowledge. (24)

5.262.s:
jñānārthaṃ ca bhramanmartyo vidyāsthāneṣu sarvaśaḥ ..
sadyo jñānaṃ sadguruto dīpārciriva nirmalā .. 25 ..
5.262.d:
ज्ञानार्थं च भ्रमन्मर्त्यो विद्यास्थानेषु सर्वशः ..
सद्यो ज्ञानं सद्गुरुतो दीपार्चिरिव निर्मला .. 25 ..
5.262.m: A mortal wanders everywhere in seats of learning for the sake of knowledge; / immediate knowledge comes from a true guru, pure like the flame of a lamp. (25)

5.262.s:
muhūrtamātramapi yo layaṃ ciṃta yati dhruvam ..
tasya pāpasahasrāṇi vilayaṃ yāṃti tatkṣaṇāt .. 26 ..
5.262.d:
मुहूर्तमात्रमपि यो लयं चिंत यति ध्रुवम् ..
तस्य पापसहस्राणि विलयं यांति तत्क्षणात् .. 26 ..
5.262.m: Whoever steadily meditates on dissolution even for a single moment, / thousands of his sins vanish at that very instant. (26)

5.262.s:
rāgadveṣau parityajya krodhalobhavivarjitaḥ ..
sarvatra samadarśī ca viṣṇubhaktasya darśanam .. 27 ..
5.262.d:
रागद्वेषौ परित्यज्य क्रोधलोभविवर्जितः ..
सर्वत्र समदर्शी च विष्णुभक्तस्य दर्शनम् .. 27 ..
5.262.m: Abandoning passion and hatred, free from anger and greed, / seeing equally everywhere—this is the darśana of a devotee of Viṣṇu. (27)

5.262.s:
sarveṣāmapi jīvānāṃ dayā yasya hṛdi sthirā ..
śaucācārasamāyukto yogī duḥkhaṃ na viṃdati .. 28 1.
māyādhipaṭalairhīno mithyā vastuvirāgavān ..
kusaṃsargavihīnaśca yogasiddheśca lakṣaṇam .. 29 ..
5.262.d:
सर्वेषामपि जीवानां दया यस्य हृदि स्थिरा ..
शौचाचारसमायुक्तो योगी दुःखं न विंदति .. 28 1.
मायाधिपटलैर्हीनो मिथ्या वस्तुविरागवान् ..
कुसंसर्गविहीनश्च योगसिद्धेश्च लक्षणम् .. 29 ..
5.262.m: He in whose heart compassion for all living beings is steady, / endowed with pure conduct—such a yogin experiences no sorrow. (28) / Free from the veils of the power of illusion, detached from unreal things, / and free from bad company: these are the marks of perfection in yoga. (29)

5.262.s:
mamatāvahnisaṃyogo narāṇāṃ tāpadāyakaḥ ..
utpannaḥ śamanaṃ tasya yogināṃ śāṃticāraṇam .. 6.263.30 ..
5.262.d:
ममतावह्निसंयोगो नराणां तापदायकः ..
उत्पन्नः शमनं तस्य योगिनां शांतिचारणम् .. 6.263.30 ..
5.262.m: The contact with the fire of 'mineness' that has arisen causes torment to men; / its pacification is the conduct of peace of yogins. (30)

5.262.s:
indriyāṇāmathoddhṛtya manasaiva niṣedhayet ..
yathā lohena lohaṃ ca gharṣitaṃ tīkṣṇatāṃ vrajet .. 31 ..
5.262.d:
इन्द्रियाणामथोद्धृत्य मनसैव निषेधयेत् ..
यथा लोहेन लोहं च घर्षितं तीक्ष्णतां व्रजेत् .. 31 ..
5.262.m: Then, having pulled back the senses, one should restrain them with the mind alone, / just as iron rubbed by iron attains sharpness. (31)

5.262.s:
buddhirhi dvividhā dehe deyā grāhyā viśuddhidā ..
saṃsāraviṣayā tyājyā parabrahmaṇi sā śubhā .. 32 ..
5.262.d:
बुद्धिर्हि द्विविधा देहे देया ग्राह्या विशुद्धिदा ..
संसारविषया त्याज्या परब्रह्मणि सा शुभा .. 32 ..
5.262.m: For the intellect in the body is twofold: to be abandoned, and to be adopted as the giver of complete purity. / That which is directed towards worldly existence is to be abandoned; that which is directed towards the Supreme Brahman is auspicious. (32)

5.262.s:
ahaṃkāro yathā devi pāpapuṇyapradāyakaḥ ..
jñāte tattve śubhaphale kṛtaḥ saṃdhāya nānyathā .. 33 ..
5.262.d:
अहंकारो यथा देवि पापपुण्यप्रदायकः ..
ज्ञाते तत्त्वे शुभफले कृतः संधाय नान्यथा .. 33 ..
5.262.m: Just as the ego, O goddess, bestows sin and merit, / when the reality is known, it is made to unite with auspicious fruit, not otherwise. (33)

5.262.s:
śyāmalaṃ ca upasthaṃ ca rūpātītānnarāḥ śivam ..
hṛdisthaṃ siraśisthaṃ ca dvayaṃ baddhavimuktaye .. .. 34 ..
5.262.d:
श्यामलं च उपस्थं च रूपातीतान्नराः शिवम् ..
हृदिस्थं सिरशिस्थं च द्वयं बद्धविमुक्तये .. .. 34 ..
5.262.m: Men [meditate on] the dark-hued and the seated [one], Śiva beyond forms; / that which resides in the heart and that which resides in the head—both are for the liberation of the bound. (34)

5.262.s:
etadakṣaramavyakamamṛtaṃ sakalaṃ tava ..
rūparūpaviṣṇurūparūpamūrtiniveditam .. 36 ..
evaṃ jñātvā vimucyeta yogī saṃsārabandhanāt ..
gurūpadeśādgṛhastho labhate nānyathā kvacit ..36..
5.262.d:
एतदक्षरमव्यकममृतं सकलं तव ..
रूपरूपविष्णुरूपरूपमूर्तिनिवेदितम् .. 36 ..
एवं ज्ञात्वा विमुच्येत योगी संसारबन्धनात् ..
गुरूपदेशाद्गृहस्थो लभते नान्यथा क्वचित् ..36..
5.262.m:
This imperishable, unmanifest, immortal [reality], the whole of yours, / is presented as the embodiment whose form is the form of Viṣṇu, whose form is forms. (35)
Knowing thus, the yogin is liberated from the bondage of worldly existence; / through the guru's instruction, a householder attains [it], never otherwise anywhere. (36)

5.262.s:
yadā guruḥ prasannātmā tasya viśvaṃ prasīdati ..
guruśca toṣito yena saṃtuṣṭāḥ pitṛdevatāḥ .. 37 ..
5.262.d:
यदा गुरुः प्रसन्नात्मा तस्य विश्वं प्रसीदति ..
गुरुश्च तोषितो येन संतुष्टाः पितृदेवताः .. 37 ..
5.262.m: When the guru's soul is pleased, the universe is pleased with him; / and he by whom the guru is satisfied has satisfied the ancestors and deities. (37)

5.262.s:
gurūpadeśaḥ pratimā sadvicāraḥ same manaḥ ..
kriyā ca jñānasahitā mokṣasiddherhi lakṣaṇam [. 38 ..
5.262.d:
गुरूपदेशः प्रतिमा सद्विचारः समे मनः ..
क्रिया च ज्ञानसहिता मोक्षसिद्धेर्हि लक्षणम् [. 38 ..
5.262.m: The instruction of the guru, the image, right reflection, an even mind, / and action conjoined with knowledge—this is indeed the mark of the attainment of liberation. (38)

5.262.s:
kriyāpatirviṣṇureva svayameva hi niṣkri yaḥ ..
sa ca prāṇavirūpāya dvādaśākṣaravījakaḥ ..39..
5.262.d:
क्रियापतिर्विष्णुरेव स्वयमेव हि निष्क्रि यः ..
स च प्राणविरूपाय द्वादशाक्षरवीजकः ..39..
5.262.m: The lord of ritual action is Viṣṇu alone, who is himself free from action; / and he is the seed of the twelve syllables for the multiform breath. (39)

5.262.s:
dvādaśākṣarakaṃ cakraṃ sarvapāpanibarhaṇam ..
duṣṭānāṃ damanaṃ caiva parabrahmapradāyakam .. 6.263.40 ..
5.262.d:
द्वादशाक्षरकं चक्रं सर्वपापनिबर्हणम् ..
दुष्टानां दमनं चैव परब्रह्मप्रदायकम् .. 6.263.40 ..
5.262.m: The twelve-syllabled discus destroys all sins, / subdues the wicked, and bestows the Supreme Brahman. (40)

5.262.s:
etadeva paraṃ brahma dvādaśākṣararūpadhṛk ..
mayā prakāśitaṃ devi skande hi vimalaṃ tava ..41..
5.262.d:
एतदेव परं ब्रह्म द्वादशाक्षररूपधृक् ..
मया प्रकाशितं देवि स्कन्दे हि विमलं तव ..41..
5.262.m: This very Supreme Brahman assumes the form of the twelve syllables; / it has been revealed by me to you, O goddess, as pure, in Skanda. (41)

5.262.s:
etatsāraṃ yogināṃ dhyānarūpaṃ bhaktigrāhyaṃ śraddhayā cintayecca ..
cāturmāsye janmakoṭyāṃ ca jātaṃ pāpaṃ dagdhvā muktidaḥ kaiṭabhāriḥ .. 42 ..
5.262.d:
एतत्सारं योगिनां ध्यानरूपं भक्तिग्राह्यं श्रद्धया चिन्तयेच्च ..
चातुर्मास्ये जन्मकोट्यां च जातं पापं दग्ध्वा मुक्तिदः कैटभारिः .. 42 ..
5.262.m: This is the essence for yogins, the form of meditation, graspable by devotion; one should contemplate it with faith. / In the Cāturmāsya, having burned away the sin born in ten million births, the enemy of Kaiṭabha grants liberation. (42)

5.262.s:
..brahmovāca .. ..
etasminnagare tatra kṣīrasāgaramadhyataḥ ..
ujjahāra vimānāgre tejobhārābhipīḍitaḥ .. 43 ..
5.262.d:
..ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नगरे तत्र क्षीरसागरमध्यतः ..
उज्जहार विमानाग्रे तेजोभाराभिपीडितः .. 43 ..
5.262.m: Brahmā said: / In that city, from the middle of the Ocean of Milk, / afflicted by the weight of splendor, [a creature] emerged before the aerial chariot. (43)

5.262.s:
uro bāhukṛtiṃ kurvansānnidhyaṃ samupāgataḥ ..
mahāmatsyo'jñātapūrvaḥ sannidhāne'nahaṃkṛtiḥ .. 44 ..
5.262.d:
उरो बाहुकृतिं कुर्वन्सान्निध्यं समुपागतः ..
महामत्स्योऽज्ञातपूर्वः सन्निधानेऽनहंकृतिः .. 44 ..
5.262.m: Fashioning its arms upon its chest, it approached the presence— / a great fish, unknown before, free from egoism in that presence. (44)

5.262.s:
huṃkāragarbhe matsyaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā taṃ sa maheśvaraḥ ..
tejasā staṃbhayāmāsa vākyametaduvāca ha .. 45 ..
5.262.d:
हुंकारगर्भे मत्स्यं च दृष्ट्वा तं स महेश्वरः ..
तेजसा स्तंभयामास वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह .. 45 ..
5.262.m: Seeing that fish with the syllable huṃ in its belly, the Great Lord / paralyzed [it] with his splendor and spoke these words: (45)

5.262.s:
kastvaṃ matsyodarasthaśca devo yakṣo'tha mānuṣaḥ ..
kathaṃ jīvasi dehāṃtargato mama vada prabho .. 46 ..
5.262.d:
कस्त्वं मत्स्योदरस्थश्च देवो यक्षोऽथ मानुषः ..
कथं जीवसि देहांतर्गतो मम वद प्रभो .. 46 ..
5.262.m: “Who are you, dwelling in the belly of a fish—a god, a yakṣa, or a mortal? / How do you live, having entered within a body? Tell me, O lord.” (46)

5.262.s:
.. matsya uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ matsyodare kṣiptaḥ samudre kṣīrasaṃbhave ..
mātrā tu pitṛvākyena nāyaṃ mama kulānvitaḥ ..47..
5.262.d:
.. मत्स्य उवाच .. ..
अहं मत्स्योदरे क्षिप्तः समुद्रे क्षीरसंभवे ..
मात्रा तु पितृवाक्येन नायं मम कुलान्वितः ..47..
5.262.m: The fish said: / “I was thrown into the belly of a fish in the ocean produced from milk / by my mother at my father's word: ‘He does not belong to my family.’ (47)

5.262.s:
kulakṣayabhayāttena jātaṃ svakulanāśanam ..
gaṃḍāṃtayogajanito bālo na gṛhakarmakṛt .. 48 ..
5.262.d:
कुलक्षयभयात्तेन जातं स्वकुलनाशनम् ..
गंडांतयोगजनितो बालो न गृहकर्मकृत् .. 48 ..
5.262.m: Out of fear of the destruction of the lineage: ‘He is born as the destroyer of his own lineage; / born under the Gandānta conjunction, this boy will not perform the duties of the household.’ (48)

5.262.s:
iti mātrā duḥkhitayā nirastaḥ śṛṇu vaṃśajaḥ ..
jhaṣeṇāpi gṛhīto'smi kālo me'tra mahānabhūt .. 49 ..
5.262.d:
इति मात्रा दुःखितया निरस्तः शृणु वंशजः ..
झषेणापि गृहीतोऽस्मि कालो मेऽत्र महानभूत् .. 49 ..
5.262.m: Thus cast out by my grieving mother—hear, O offspring of the race— / I was swallowed by a fish, and a long time has passed for me here. (49)

5.262.s:
tava vākyāmṛtairebhirjñānayogo mahānabhūt ..
tena tvaṃ sakalo jñāto mayā mūrto'tha mūrttagaḥ. ..6.263.50...
5.262.d:
तव वाक्यामृतैरेभिर्ज्ञानयोगो महानभूत् ..
तेन त्वं सकलो ज्ञातो मया मूर्तोऽथ मूर्त्तगः. ..6.263.50...
5.262.m: By these nectarean words of yours, a great yoga of knowledge arose; / by that, you, the complete one, having form and seated in form, have been known by me. (50)

5.262.s:
anujñāṃ mama deveśa dehi niṣkramaṇāya ca ..
yathā'haṃ pitṛpo brahmanbhavānyāścāpi lakṣyate .. 51 ..
5.262.d:
अनुज्ञां मम देवेश देहि निष्क्रमणाय च ..
यथाऽहं पितृपो ब्रह्मन्भवान्याश्चापि लक्ष्यते .. 51 ..
5.262.m: Grant me permission, O Lord of Gods, to come forth, / so that, O Brahmā, I may protect my ancestors and Bhavānī may also be beheld.” (51)

5.262.s:
.. hara uvāca .. .. vipro'si sutarūpo'si pūjyosyāsi babhāṣataḥ ..
bahirniṣkrama vegena staṃbhito'si mahājhaṣaḥ .. 52 ..
5.262.d:
.. हर उवाच .. .. विप्रोऽसि सुतरूपोऽसि पूज्योस्यासि बभाषतः ..
बहिर्निष्क्रम वेगेन स्तंभितोऽसि महाझषः .. 52 ..
5.262.m: Hara said: “You are a brahmin, you have the form of a son, you are worthy of worship.” Speaking thus: / “Come outside swiftly; the great fish has been immobilized.” (52)

5.262.s:
tato'sau śirasā jāta utkleśānmatsyayojitaḥ ..
tato hi vikṛtaṃ vaktraṃ kṣaṇādbahirupāgataḥ .. 53 ..
5.262.d:
ततोऽसौ शिरसा जात उत्क्लेशान्मत्स्ययोजितः ..
ततो हि विकृतं वक्त्रं क्षणाद्बहिरुपागतः .. 53 ..
5.262.m: Then, head-first, he emerged, expelled by the fish due to churning; / from its distorted mouth, he came out in an instant. (53)

5.262.s:
rūpavānpratimāyukto matsyagaṃdhena saṃyutaḥ ..
somakāṃtisamastatra hyabhavaddivyagaṃdhabhāk .. 854 ..
5.262.d:
रूपवान्प्रतिमायुक्तो मत्स्यगंधेन संयुतः ..
सोमकांतिसमस्तत्र ह्यभवद्दिव्यगंधभाक् .. 854 ..
5.262.m: Handsome, well-proportioned, though filled with the smell of fish, / equal in luster to the moon, he became endowed with a celestial fragrance there. (54)

5.262.s:
umāpi praṇataṃ cāmuṃ sutaṃ svotsaṃgabhājanam ..
cakāra tasya nāmāpi haraḥ paramaharṣitaḥ .. 895 ..
yasmānmatsyodarājjāto yogināṃ pravaro hyayam ..
tasmāttu matsya nātheti loke khyāto bhaviṣyati .. 56 ..
acchedyaḥ syānnaratanurjñānayogasya pāragaḥ ..
nirmatsaro'pi nirdvaṃdvo nirāśo brahmasevakaḥ .. 57 ..
jīvanmuktaśca bhavitā bhuvanāni caturdaśa ..
ityuktaśca maheśānaṃ praṇamaṃśca punaḥpunaḥ ..
maheśvareṇa sahito maṃdarācalamāyayau .. 58 ..
.. brahmovāca .. ..
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ devīṃ skandamāliṃgya so'gamat .. 59 ..
tataḥ sā pārvatī hṛṣṭā prāpya jñānamanuttamam ..
evaṃ sā paramāṃ siddhiṃ praṇavasyaprabhā janam .. 6.263.60 ..
sā prāpya jagatāṃ mātā dvādaśākṣarajāṃbunā ..
imāṃ matsyendranāthasya cotpattiṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti ca .. 61 ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet..62..
5.262.d:
उमापि प्रणतं चामुं सुतं स्वोत्संगभाजनम् ..
चकार तस्य नामापि हरः परमहर्षितः .. 895 ..
यस्मान्मत्स्योदराज्जातो योगिनां प्रवरो ह्ययम् ..
तस्मात्तु मत्स्य नाथेति लोके ख्यातो भविष्यति .. 56 ..
अच्छेद्यः स्यान्नरतनुर्ज्ञानयोगस्य पारगः ..
निर्मत्सरोऽपि निर्द्वंद्वो निराशो ब्रह्मसेवकः .. 57 ..
जीवन्मुक्तश्च भविता भुवनानि चतुर्दश ..
इत्युक्तश्च महेशानं प्रणमंश्च पुनःपुनः ..
महेश्वरेण सहितो मंदराचलमाययौ .. 58 ..
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं देवीं स्कन्दमालिंग्य सोऽगमत् .. 59 ..
ततः सा पार्वती हृष्टा प्राप्य ज्ञानमनुत्तमम् ..
एवं सा परमां सिद्धिं प्रणवस्यप्रभा जनम् .. 6.263.60 ..
सा प्राप्य जगतां माता द्वादशाक्षरजांबुना ..
इमां मत्स्येन्द्रनाथस्य चोत्पत्तिं यः शृणोति च .. 61 ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत्..62..
5.262.m:
Umā, too, placed that bowing son upon her own lap; / and Hara, exceedingly delighted, gave him a name: (55)
“Since he was born from the belly of a fish, and he is the foremost of yogins, / therefore he shall be known in the world as Matsyanātha. (56)
He shall possess an invulnerable human body, a master of the yoga of knowledge, / free from malice, beyond dualities, without desire, a servant of Brahman. (57)
He shall be liberated while living throughout the fourteen worlds.” / Addressed thus, bowing again and again to the Great Lord, / accompanied by the Great Lord, he went to Mount Mandara. (58)
Brahmā said: / Having circumambulated the goddess and embraced Skanda, he departed. (59)
Then Pārvatī was joyful, having obtained supreme knowledge; / thus she [attained] supreme perfection, the vessel of the splendor of the Praṇava. (60)
The mother of the worlds, having obtained that with the water of the twelve syllables— / and whoever hears this origin of Matsyendranātha, (61)
especially during the Cāturmāsya, attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. (62)

5.262.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhsryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye matsyendranāthotpattikathanaṃ nāma triṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..263..
5.262.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाह्स्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये मत्स्येन्द्रनाथोत्पत्तिकथनं नाम त्रिषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः..263..
5.262.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-third chapter, entitled “The Narration of the Origin of Matsyendranātha,” in the Cāturmāsyamāhātmya, in the story of Śeṣaśāyin, in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya, in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, the Great Purāṇa in eighty-one thousand verses. (263)

5.263.s:
brahmovāca..
kārtikeyaśca pārvatyāḥ prāṇebhyaścātivallabhaḥ..
saṃkrīḍati samīpastho nānāceṣṭābhirudyataḥ..1..
5.263.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच..
कार्तिकेयश्च पार्वत्याः प्राणेभ्यश्चातिवल्लभः..
संक्रीडति समीपस्थो नानाचेष्टाभिरुद्यतः..1..
5.263.m: Brahmā said: / Kārtikeya, dearer than life to Pārvatī, / played nearby, engaged in various childish antics. (1)

5.263.s:
raktakāṃtirmahātejāḥ ṣaṇmukho'dbhuta vikramaḥ..
kvacidgāyati cātyarthaṃ kvacinnṛtyati svecchayā..2..
5.263.d:
रक्तकांतिर्महातेजाः षण्मुखोऽद्भुत विक्रमः..
क्वचिद्गायति चात्यर्थं क्वचिन्नृत्यति स्वेच्छया..2..
5.263.m: Of red luster, of great splendor, six-faced, of wondrous prowess, / sometimes he sang loudly, and sometimes he danced at will. (2)

5.263.s:
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā vinayāvanataḥ kvacit..
kvacicca gaṃgāpuline sikatālepanākṛtiḥ..3..
5.263.d:
मातरं पितरं दृष्ट्वा विनयावनतः क्वचित्..
क्वचिच्च गंगापुलिने सिकतालेपनाकृतिः..3..
5.263.m: Seeing his mother and father, he bowed in humility at times; / and at times on the sandbank of the Gaṅgā, his form was smeared with sand. (3)

5.263.s:
gaṇaiḥ saha vicinvāno vividhānvanabhūruhān..
evaṃ prakrīḍitastasya divasāḥ paṃca jajñire..4..
5.263.d:
गणैः सह विचिन्वानो विविधान्वनभूरुहान्..
एवं प्रक्रीडितस्तस्य दिवसाः पंच जज्ञिरे..4..
5.263.m: Searching with the gaṇas for various forest trees, / thus sporting, five days passed for him. (4)

5.263.s:
tato devā mahendrādyāstārakatrāsavidrutāḥ..
stuvantaḥ śaṃkaraṃ sarve tārakasya jighṛkṣayā..5..
5.263.d:
ततो देवा महेन्द्राद्यास्तारकत्रासविद्रुताः..
स्तुवन्तः शंकरं सर्वे तारकस्य जिघृक्षया..5..
5.263.m: Then the gods, led by Mahendra, put to flight by the terror of Tāraka, / all praised Śaṃkara, desiring the destruction of Tāraka. (5)

5.263.s:
cakruḥ kumāraṃ senānyaṃ jāhnavyāṃ svagaṇaiḥ surāḥ..
sasvanurdevavādyāni puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta ha..6..
5.263.d:
चक्रुः कुमारं सेनान्यं जाह्नव्यां स्वगणैः सुराः..
सस्वनुर्देववाद्यानि पुष्पवर्षं पपात ह..6..
5.263.m: At the Jāhnavī, the gods with their troops appointed Kumāra as general of the army; / divine instruments resounded, and a shower of flowers fell. (6)

5.263.s:
vahnistu svāṃ dadau śaktiṃ himavānvāhanaṃ dadau..
sarvadevasamudbhūtagaṇakoṭisamāvṛtaḥ..7..
5.263.d:
वह्निस्तु स्वां ददौ शक्तिं हिमवान्वाहनं ददौ..
सर्वदेवसमुद्भूतगणकोटिसमावृतः..7..
5.263.m: Fire gave his own spear; Himavat gave a mount; / surrounded by tens of millions of gaṇas sprung from all the gods, (7)

5.263.s:
praṇamya munisaṃghebhyaḥ prayayau ripuvigrahe..
tāmravatyāṃ nagaryāṃ ca śaṃkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān..8..
5.263.d:
प्रणम्य मुनिसंघेभ्यः प्रययौ रिपुविग्रहे..
ताम्रवत्यां नगर्यां च शंखं दध्मौ प्रतापवान्..8..
5.263.m: having bowed to the assemblies of sages, he went forth to battle the enemy; / and in the city of Tāmravatī, the mighty one blew his conch. (8)

5.263.s:
tatastārakasainyasya daityadānavakoṭayaḥ..
samājagmustasya purācchaṃkhanādabhayāturāḥ..9..
5.263.d:
ततस्तारकसैन्यस्य दैत्यदानवकोटयः..
समाजग्मुस्तस्य पुराच्छंखनादभयातुराः..9..
5.263.m: Then, from the army of Tāraka, tens of millions of daityas and dānavas / came forth from his city, agitated by the fear of the conch's blast. (9)

5.263.s:
svavāhanasamārūḍhāḥ saṃyatā baladarpitāḥ..
devāḥ sarve'pi yuyudhuḥ skandatejopabṛṃhitāḥ..6.264.10..
5.263.d:
स्ववाहनसमारूढाः संयता बलदर्पिताः..
देवाः सर्वेऽपि युयुधुः स्कन्दतेजोपबृंहिताः..6.264.10..
5.263.m: Mounted on their own conveyances, prepared, arrogant in their strength, / all the gods also fought, invigorated by Skanda's splendor. (10)

5.263.s:
tadā dānavasainyāni nijaghāna ca sarvaśaḥ..
viṣṇucakreṇa te chinnāḥ petururvyāṃ sahasraśaḥ..11..
5.263.d:
तदा दानवसैन्यानि निजघान च सर्वशः..
विष्णुचक्रेण ते छिन्नाः पेतुरुर्व्यां सहस्रशः..11..
5.263.m: Then he struck down the armies of the Dānavas on every side; / severed by Viṣṇu's discus, they fell upon the earth by the thousands.

5.263.s:
tato bhagnāśca śataśo dānavā nihatāstadā..
nadyaḥ śoṇitasaṃbhūtā jātā bahuvidhāmune..12..
5.263.d:
ततो भग्नाश्च शतशो दानवा निहतास्तदा..
नद्यः शोणितसंभूता जाता बहुविधामुने..12..
