5.263.m: Then, O sage, broken by hundreds, the Dānavas were slain at that time; / rivers born of blood arose of manifold kinds.

5.263.s:
tadbhagnaṃ dānavabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa yuyudhe raṇe..
babhaṃja sadyo deveśo bāṇajālairanekadhā..13..
5.263.d:
तद्भग्नं दानवबलं दृष्ट्वा स युयुधे रणे..
बभंज सद्यो देवेशो बाणजालैरनेकधा..13..
5.263.m: Seeing that Dānava army broken, he fought in battle; / the lord of the gods immediately shattered [them] in many ways with hosts of arrows.

5.263.s:
śaktināyudhya gaṃginyāścikṣepa kṛṣṇapreritāḥ..
sarathaṃ ca sayaṃtāraṃ cakre taṃ bhasmasātkṣaṇāt..14..
5.263.d:
शक्तिनायुध्य गंगिन्याश्चिक्षेप कृष्णप्रेरिताः..
सरथं च सयंतारं चक्रे तं भस्मसात्क्षणात्..14..
5.263.m: Having fought with his spear, urged by Kṛṣṇa, he hurled it, / and in an instant reduced him to ashes along with his chariot and charioteer.

5.263.s:
śeṣāḥ pātālamagamanhataṃ dṛṣṭvā'tha tārakam..
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve śasaṃsustasya vikramam.. 15..
5.263.d:
शेषाः पातालमगमन्हतं दृष्ट्वाऽथ तारकम्..
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे शसंसुस्तस्य विक्रमम्.. 15..
5.263.m: Seeing Tāraka slain, the remainder went to Pātāla. / Then all the hosts of gods praised his valour.

5.263.s:
devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭistathā'bhavat..
te labdhavijayāḥ sarve maheśvarapurogamāḥ.. 16..
5.263.d:
देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिस्तथाऽभवत्..
ते लब्धविजयाः सर्वे महेश्वरपुरोगमाः.. 16..
5.263.m: The drums of the gods sounded, and a shower of flowers fell. / Having obtained victory, all of them, led by Maheśvara,

5.263.s:
siṣicuḥ sarvadevānāṃ senāpatye ṣaḍānanam..
tataḥ skaṃdaṃ samāliṃgya pārvatī harṣagadgadā..17..
5.263.d:
सिषिचुः सर्वदेवानां सेनापत्ये षडाननम्..
ततः स्कंदं समालिंग्य पार्वती हर्षगद्गदा..17..
5.263.m: consecrated the six-faced one to the supreme command of all the gods. / Then, embracing Skanda, Pārvatī, stammering with joy,

5.263.s:
māṃgalyāni tadā cakre svasakhībhiḥ samāvṛtā..
evaṃ ca tārakaṃ hatvā saptame'hani bālakaḥ..18..
5.263.d:
मांगल्यानि तदा चक्रे स्वसखीभिः समावृता..
एवं च तारकं हत्वा सप्तमेऽहनि बालकः..18..
5.263.m: performed auspicious rites, surrounded by her female friends. / Having thus slain Tāraka on the seventh day, the boy,

5.263.s:
maṃdarācalamāsādya pitarau saṃpraharṣayan..
uvāca sakalaṃ skandaḥ paramānaṃdanirbharaḥ..19..
5.263.d:
मंदराचलमासाद्य पितरौ संप्रहर्षयन्..
उवाच सकलं स्कन्दः परमानंदनिर्भरः..19..
5.263.m: reaching Mount Mandara and bringing great joy to his parents, / Skanda, filled with supreme bliss, related everything.

5.263.s:
kāle dārakriyāṃ tasya cintayāmāsa śaṃkaraḥ..
sa uvāca prasannātmā gāṃgeyamamitadyutim..6.264.20..
5.263.d:
काले दारक्रियां तस्य चिन्तयामास शंकरः..
स उवाच प्रसन्नात्मा गांगेयममितद्युतिम्..6.264.20..
5.263.m: In due course, Śaṃkara thought of his marriage. / With a gracious mind, he spoke to Gāṅgeya of boundless splendour:

5.263.s:
prāptaḥ kālastava vibho pāṇigrahaṇasaṃmataḥ..
kuru dārānsamāsādya dharmaste puṃsasaṃmataḥ..21.
5.263.d:
प्राप्तः कालस्तव विभो पाणिग्रहणसंमतः..
कुरु दारान्समासाद्य धर्मस्ते पुंससंमतः..21.
5.263.m: “The time suitable for taking a wife has arrived for you, O lord. / Having obtained a wife, make marriage your duty, as approved for a man.

5.263.s:
krīḍasva vividhairbhogairvimānaiḥ saha kāmikaiḥ..
tacchrutvā bhagavānskandaḥ pitaraṃ vākyamabravīt..
ahameva hi sarvatra dṛśyaḥ sarvagaṇeṣu ca..
dṛśyādṛśyapadārtheṣu kiṃ gṛhṇāmi tyajāmi kim..23..
5.263.d:
क्रीडस्व विविधैर्भोगैर्विमानैः सह कामिकैः..
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्स्कन्दः पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्..
अहमेव हि सर्वत्र दृश्यः सर्वगणेषु च..
दृश्यादृश्यपदार्थेषु किं गृह्णामि त्यजामि किम्..23..
5.263.m: Sport with various pleasures and wish-fulfilling aerial chariots.” / Hearing that, the blessed Skanda said to his father: / “I alone indeed am visible everywhere and in all hosts; / among visible and invisible things, what should I grasp, what should I abandon?

5.263.s:
yāḥ striyaḥ sakalā viśve pārvatyā tāḥ samā hi me..
narāḥ sarve'pi deveśa bhavadvattānvilokaye..24..
5.263.d:
याः स्त्रियः सकला विश्वे पार्वत्या ताः समा हि मे..
नराः सर्वेऽपि देवेश भवद्वत्तान्विलोकये..24..
5.263.m: All the women who exist in the universe are indeed equal to Pārvatī to me. / All men too, O lord of the gods, I behold as like unto you.

5.263.s:
tvaṃ gururmāṃ ca rakṣasva punarnarakamajjanāt..
yena jñātamidaṃ jñānaṃ tvatprasādādakhaṃḍitam..25..
5.263.d:
त्वं गुरुर्मां च रक्षस्व पुनर्नरकमज्जनात्..
येन ज्ञातमिदं ज्ञानं त्वत्प्रसादादखंडितम्..25..
5.263.m: You are my guru; protect me from sinking again into hell! / By your grace this undivided knowledge has been known [by me];

5.263.s:
punareva mahāghorasaṃsārābdhau nimajjaye..
dīpahasto yathā vastu dṛṣṭvā tatkaraṇaṃ tyajet..26..
5.263.d:
पुनरेव महाघोरसंसाराब्धौ निमज्जये..
दीपहस्तो यथा वस्तु दृष्ट्वा तत्करणं त्यजेत्..26..
5.263.m: would [you] plunge [me] once more into the ocean of the most dreadful worldly existence? / Just as one holding a lamp in hand, having seen the object, drops the instrument,

5.263.s:
tathā jñānamadhiprāpya yogī tyajati saṃsṛtim..
jñātvā sarvagataṃ brahma sarvajña parameśvara..27..
5.263.d:
तथा ज्ञानमधिप्राप्य योगी त्यजति संसृतिम्..
ज्ञात्वा सर्वगतं ब्रह्म सर्वज्ञ परमेश्वर..27..
5.263.m: so the yogi, having attained knowledge, abandons worldly existence. / Having known the all-pervading brahman, O omniscient supreme lord,

5.263.s:
nivarttaṃte kriyāḥ sarvā yasya taṃ yoginaṃ viduḥ..
viṣaye lubdhacittānāṃ vane'pi jāyate ratiḥ..28..
5.263.d:
निवर्त्तंते क्रियाः सर्वा यस्य तं योगिनं विदुः..
विषये लुब्धचित्तानां वनेऽपि जायते रतिः..28..
5.263.m: one for whom all actions cease is known as a yogi. / For those whose minds are greedy for sensory objects, attachment arises even in a forest;

5.263.s:
sarvatra samadṛṣṭīnāṃ gehe muktirhi śāśvatī..
jñānameva maheśāna manuṣyāṇāṃ sudurlabham..29..
5.263.d:
सर्वत्र समदृष्टीनां गेहे मुक्तिर्हि शाश्वती..
ज्ञानमेव महेशान मनुष्याणां सुदुर्लभम्..29..
5.263.m: for those of equal vision everywhere, liberation is eternal even in a home. / Knowledge alone, O Maheśāna, is exceedingly difficult for human beings to attain.

5.263.s:
labdhaṃ jñānaṃ kathamapi paṃḍito naiva pātayet..
nāhamasmi na mātā me na pitā na ca bāṃdhavaḥ..6.264.30..
5.263.d:
लब्धं ज्ञानं कथमपि पंडितो नैव पातयेत्..
नाहमस्मि न माता मे न पिता न च बांधवः..6.264.30..
5.263.m: A wise man should never cast down knowledge once it has somehow been attained. / I am not, nor is my mother, nor father, nor kinsman;

5.263.s:
jñānaṃ prāpya pṛthakbhāvamāpanno bhuvaneṣvaham..
prāpyaṃ bhāgamidaṃ daivātprabhāvāttava nārhasi..31..
5.263.d:
ज्ञानं प्राप्य पृथक्भावमापन्नो भुवनेष्वहम्..
प्राप्यं भागमिदं दैवात्प्रभावात्तव नार्हसि..31..
5.263.m: having attained knowledge, I have reached a state separate from the worlds. / By good fortune and by your power this portion was to be obtained; you ought not

5.263.s:
vaktumevaṃvidhaṃ vākyaṃ mumukṣorme na saṃśayaḥ..
yadāgrahaparā devī punaḥpunarabhāṣata..32..
5.263.d:
वक्तुमेवंविधं वाक्यं मुमुक्षोर्मे न संशयः..
यदाग्रहपरा देवी पुनःपुनरभाषत..32..
5.263.m: to speak such words to me who desire liberation; of this there is no doubt.” / When the goddess, intent on her insistence, spoke again and again,

5.263.s:
tadā tau pitarau natvā gato'sau krauñcaparvatam..
tatrāśrame mahāpuṇye cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ..33..
5.263.d:
तदा तौ पितरौ नत्वा गतोऽसौ क्रौञ्चपर्वतम्..
तत्राश्रमे महापुण्ये चचार परमं तपः..33..
5.263.m: he then bowed to both his parents and went to Mount Krauñca. / There, in a most holy hermitage, he performed supreme austerity.

5.263.s:
jajāpa paramaṃ brahma dvādaśākṣarabījakam..
pūrvaṃ dhyānena sarvāṇi vaśīkṛtyendriyāṇi ca..34..
5.263.d:
जजाप परमं ब्रह्म द्वादशाक्षरबीजकम्..
पूर्वं ध्यानेन सर्वाणि वशीकृत्येन्द्रियाणि च..34..
5.263.m: He muttered the supreme brahman, the twelve-syllabled seed-syllable, / having first brought all the senses under control through meditation.

5.263.s:
mamatāṃ saṃviyujyātha jñānayogamavāptavān..
siddhayastasya nirvighnā aṇimādyā yadā''gatāḥ..35..
5.263.d:
ममतां संवियुज्याथ ज्ञानयोगमवाप्तवान्..
सिद्धयस्तस्य निर्विघ्ना अणिमाद्या यदा'ऽगताः..35..
5.263.m: Then, having cast aside the sense of mineness, he attained the yoga of knowledge. / When the unobstructed perfections, beginning with lightness and the rest, approached him,

5.263.s:
tadā tāsāṃ gaṇā kruddho vākyametaduvāca ha..
mamāpi duṣṭabhāvena yadi yūyamupāgatāḥ..36..
5.263.d:
तदा तासां गणा क्रुद्धो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह..
ममापि दुष्टभावेन यदि यूयमुपागताः..36..
5.263.m: then, angered at their hosts, he said these words: / “Even to me, if you have come with wicked intent,

5.263.s:
tadāsmatsamaśāṃtānāṃ nābhibhūtiṃ kariṣyatha..
evaṃ jñātvā maheśo'pi yato jñānamahodayam..37..
5.263.d:
तदास्मत्समशांतानां नाभिभूतिं करिष्यथ..
एवं ज्ञात्वा महेशोऽपि यतो ज्ञानमहोदयम्..37..
5.263.m: then you shall not overpower us who are equally tranquil!” / Having known thus, even Maheśa, because the great dawning of knowledge [occurred],

5.263.s:
matto'pi jñānayogenaskando'pyadhikabhāvabhṛt..
vismayāviṣṭahṛdayaḥ pārvatīmanuśiṣṭavān..38..
5.263.d:
मत्तोऽपि ज्ञानयोगेनस्कन्दोऽप्यधिकभावभृत्..
विस्मयाविष्टहृदयः पार्वतीमनुशिष्टवान्..38..
5.263.m: [thinking,] “Even more than I, Skanda has attained a higher state through the yoga of knowledge,” / his heart filled with wonder, instructed Pārvatī.

5.263.s:
putraśokaparāṃ comāṃ śubhairvākyāmṛtairharaḥ..
cāturmāsasya māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam..39..
5.263.d:
पुत्रशोकपरां चोमां शुभैर्वाक्यामृतैर्हरः..
चातुर्मासस्य माहात्म्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्..39..
5.263.m: And Hara [consoled] Umā, who was devoted to grief for her son, with auspicious, nectar-like words / [concerning] the māhātmya of the Cāturmāsya, which destroys all sin:

5.263.s:
maheśvaro vā madhukaiṭabhārirhṛdyāśrito dhyānamayo'dvitīyaḥ..
abhedabuddhyā paramārtihaṃtā ripuḥ sa evātipriyo bhavettataḥ..6.264.40..
5.263.d:
महेश्वरो वा मधुकैटभारिर्हृद्याश्रितो ध्यानमयोऽद्वितीयः..
अभेदबुद्ध्या परमार्तिहंता रिपुः स एवातिप्रियो भवेत्ततः..6.264.40..
5.263.m: “Whether Maheśvara or the enemy of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, dwelling in the heart, consisting of meditation, without a second— / by a mindset of non-duality, the destroyer of supreme distress, even an enemy, becomes exceedingly dear from that.”

5.263.s:
sūta uvāca..
etadvaḥ kathitaṃ viprāścāturmāsyasamudbhavam..
māhātmyaṃ vistareṇaiva kimanyacchrotumicchatha..41..
5.263.d:
सूत उवाच..
एतद्वः कथितं विप्राश्चातुर्मास्यसमुद्भवम्..
माहात्म्यं विस्तरेणैव किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छथ..41..
5.263.m: Sūta said: / “This māhātmya arising from the Cāturmāsya has been told to you in detail, O brahmins. What else do you wish to hear?”

5.263.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye tārakāsuravadho nāma catuḥṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..264..
5.263.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये तारकासुरवधो नाम चतुःषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः..264..
5.263.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, entitled “The Slaying of Tārakāsura”, in the section on the māhātmya of the Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of the one who reclines on Śeṣa, in the māhātmya of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

5.264.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
prabhūtāni tvayoktāni vratāni niyamāstathā..
prasupte puṃḍarīkākṣe yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate..1..
5.264.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः..
प्रभूतानि त्वयोक्तानि व्रतानि नियमास्तथा..
प्रसुप्ते पुंडरीकाक्षे येषां संख्या न विद्यते..1..
5.264.m: The seers said: / “Abundant vows and observances have been spoken of by you, / of which there is no count while the lotus-eyed one is asleep.

5.264.s:
aśaktyā hi śarīrasya niyamānāṃ kathaṃ caret..
vrataṃ hi sukumārāṃgo dānairvāpi vadasva naḥ..2..
5.264.d:
अशक्त्या हि शरीरस्य नियमानां कथं चरेत्..
व्रतं हि सुकुमारांगो दानैर्वापि वदस्व नः..2..
5.264.m: Because of bodily weakness, how could one of delicate limbs / perform an observance or vow, or through gifts? Tell us!”

5.264.s:
sūta uvāca..
aśakto niyamaṃ kartuṃ sukumāro bhavettu yaḥ..
tena tatra prakartavyaṃ vikhyātaṃ bhīṣmapaṃcakam..3..
5.264.d:
सूत उवाच..
अशक्तो नियमं कर्तुं सुकुमारो भवेत्तु यः..
तेन तत्र प्रकर्तव्यं विख्यातं भीष्मपंचकम्..3..
5.264.m: Sūta said: / “One who is unable to keep the observance, who is delicate of body, / by him the renowned Bhīṣmapañcaka should be performed there.

5.264.s:
kārttikasya site pakṣa ekādaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ..
prātarutthāya vipreṃdra kartavyaṃ daṃtadhāvanam..4..
5.264.d:
कार्त्तिकस्य सिते पक्ष एकादश्यां समाहितः..
प्रातरुत्थाय विप्रेंद्र कर्तव्यं दंतधावनम्..4..
5.264.m: On the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, composed in mind, / having risen in the morning, O lord of brahmins, the cleansing of teeth is to be performed.

5.264.s:
tatastu niyamaṃ kuryādvāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ..
pūrvoktānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ niyamānāṃ dvijottamāḥ..5..
5.264.d:
ततस्तु नियमं कुर्याद्वासुदेवपरायणः..
पूर्वोक्तानां च सर्वेषां नियमानां द्विजोत्तमाः..5..
5.264.m: Then, devoted to Vāsudeva, he should undertake the observance / of all the previously mentioned observances, O best of the twice-born.

5.264.s:
upavāsaḥ prakartavyastasminnahani bhaktitaḥ..
aśaktyā vā śarīrasya hemaṃ dadyātsvaśaktitaḥ..6..
5.264.d:
उपवासः प्रकर्तव्यस्तस्मिन्नहनि भक्तितः..
अशक्त्या वा शरीरस्य हेमं दद्यात्स्वशक्तितः..6..
5.264.m: A fast is to be performed on that day with devotion; / or, through bodily inability, he should give gold according to his capacity.

5.264.s:
brāhmaṇāya haviṣyānnaṃ dātavyaṃ vaiṣṇavairnaraiḥ.
evaṃ pañcadinaṃ yāvatkartavyaṃ vratamuttamam..7..
5.264.d:
ब्राह्मणाय हविष्यान्नं दातव्यं वैष्णवैर्नरैः.
एवं पञ्चदिनं यावत्कर्तव्यं व्रतमुत्तमम्..7..
5.264.m: Sacrificial food should be given to a brahmin by Vaiṣṇava men. / In this way, for five days, this excellent vow is to be performed.

5.264.s:
pūjanīyo hṛṣīkeśo jalaśāyisvarūpadhṛk..
gaṃdhairdhūpaiśca naivedyai rātrijāgaraṇairapi..8..
5.264.d:
पूजनीयो हृषीकेशो जलशायिस्वरूपधृक्..
गंधैर्धूपैश्च नैवेद्यै रात्रिजागरणैरपि..8..
5.264.m: Hṛṣīkeśa, who bears the form of reclining on the waters, should be worshipped / with perfumes, incenses, food offerings, and also keeping awake at night.

5.264.s:
ṣaṣṭhe'hani tato jāte pūjayedbrāhmaṇottamān..
tāṃśca vastrairhiraṇyena miṣṭānnena prabhaktitaḥ..9..
5.264.d:
षष्ठेऽहनि ततो जाते पूजयेद्ब्राह्मणोत्तमान्..
तांश्च वस्त्रैर्हिरण्येन मिष्टान्नेन प्रभक्तितः..9..
5.264.m: Then, when the sixth day arrives, he should worship the best of brahmins, / [honouring] them with garments, gold, and sweet food, with great devotion.

5.264.s:
tataḥ kṛtāṃjalirbhūtvā yācayedbrāhmaṇottamān..
sarve me niyamāḥ prāptā yuṣmākaṃ ca prasādataḥ..6.265.10..
5.264.d:
ततः कृतांजलिर्भूत्वा याचयेद्ब्राह्मणोत्तमान्..
सर्वे मे नियमाः प्राप्ता युष्माकं च प्रसादतः..6.265.10..
5.264.m: Then, having joined his palms, he should pray to the best of brahmins: / ‘All my observances have been accomplished by your grace.’

5.264.s:
tatastairapi vaktavyaṃ caturmāsīsamudbhavam..
vratānāṃ niyamānāṃ ca vrataṃ bhūyāttavākhilam..11..
5.264.d:
ततस्तैरपि वक्तव्यं चतुर्मासीसमुद्भवम्..
व्रतानां नियमानां च व्रतं भूयात्तवाखिलम्..11..
5.264.m: Then it should also be said by them: ‘May your vow of all the vows / and observances arising from the Cāturmāsya be complete!’

5.264.s:
tato visarjya tānviprānbhojanaṃ svayamācaret..
sarvāhāreṇa rājeṃdra paṃcagavyaprapūrvakam..12..
5.264.d:
ततो विसर्ज्य तान्विप्रान्भोजनं स्वयमाचरेत्..
सर्वाहारेण राजेंद्र पंचगव्यप्रपूर्वकम्..12..
5.264.m: Then, having dismissed those brahmins, he himself should take food, / eating all kinds of food, O best of kings, preceded by the five products of the cow.”

5.264.s:
yaḥ karoti vrataṃ tasya phalaṃ syādbahupuṇyadam..
yaḥ punarvratametaddhi kurute dinapaṃcakam..
upavāsaparastasya phalaṃ śataguṇaṃ bhavet..13..
5.264.d:
यः करोति व्रतं तस्य फलं स्याद्बहुपुण्यदम्..
यः पुनर्व्रतमेतद्धि कुरुते दिनपंचकम्..
उपवासपरस्तस्य फलं शतगुणं भवेत्..13..
5.264.m: For whoever performs the vow, the fruit yields abundant merit; / but whoever undertakes this very vow for five days, / devoted to fasting, his fruit becomes a hundredfold.

5.264.s:
ekādaśyāṃ hareḥ pūjāṃ jātipuṣpaiḥ samācaret..
dvādaśyāṃ bilvapatreṇa śatapatryā tataḥ param..
trayodaśyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ surabhyā bhaktipūrvakam..14..
5.264.d:
एकादश्यां हरेः पूजां जातिपुष्पैः समाचरेत्..
द्वादश्यां बिल्वपत्रेण शतपत्र्या ततः परम्..
त्रयोदश्यां चतुर्दश्यां सुरभ्या भक्तिपूर्वकम्..14..
5.264.m: On the eleventh lunar day, one should worship Hari with jasmine flowers; / on the twelfth with bilva leaf; next with rose petals; / on the thirteenth and fourteenth with fragrant tulsi, full of devotion.

5.264.s:
bhṛṃgarājena puṇyena paurṇamāsyāṃ prapūjayet..
pratipaddivase sarvaiḥ pūjanīyo janārdanaḥ..
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam..15..
5.264.d:
भृंगराजेन पुण्येन पौर्णमास्यां प्रपूजयेत्..
प्रतिपद्दिवसे सर्वैः पूजनीयो जनार्दनः..
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम्..15..
5.264.m: On the full-moon day one should worship him with meritorious bhṛṅgarāja. / On the first day of the lunar fortnight, Janārdana is to be worshipped by all; / cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and water touched with kuśa grass—

5.264.s:
pratipaddivase sarvānprāśayetkāyaśuddhaye..
agaraṃ guggulaṃ caiva karpūraṃ tagaraṃ tvacā..16..
5.264.d:
प्रतिपद्दिवसे सर्वान्प्राशयेत्कायशुद्धये..
अगरं गुग्गुलं चैव कर्पूरं तगरं त्वचा..16..
5.264.m: all these one should sip on the first day of the lunar fortnight for the purification of the body; / and aloe, bdellium, camphor, tagara, cinnamon—

5.264.s:
ekaikaṃ nirvapeddhūpaṃ pratipaddivase'khilam..
jalaśāyī jagadyoniḥ śeṣaparyaṃkamāśritaḥ..17..
5.264.d:
एकैकं निर्वपेद्धूपं प्रतिपद्दिवसेऽखिलम्..
जलशायी जगद्योनिः शेषपर्यंकमाश्रितः..17..
5.264.m: one should offer each incense completely on the first day of the lunar fortnight. / [Saying:] 'O sleeper upon the waters, source of the universe, who rest on the couch of Śeṣa!

5.264.s:
arghaṃ gṛhṇātu me devo bhīṣmapaṃcakasiddhaye..
maṃtreṇānena dātavyo hyargho devasya bhaktitaḥ..18..
5.264.d:
अर्घं गृह्णातु मे देवो भीष्मपंचकसिद्धये..
मंत्रेणानेन दातव्यो ह्यर्घो देवस्य भक्तितः..18..
5.264.m: May the Lord accept my offering of water for the success of the Bhīṣmapañcaka vow!' / With this mantra water should be offered to the Lord with devotion.

5.264.s:
śaṃkhatoyaṃ samādāya sapuṣpaphalacaṃdanaiḥ..
naivedyaṃ paramānnaṃ ca svaśaktyā nirvapeddvijāḥ..19..
5.264.d:
शंखतोयं समादाय सपुष्पफलचंदनैः..
नैवेद्यं परमान्नं च स्वशक्त्या निर्वपेद्द्विजाः..19..
5.264.m: Taking water in a conch shell with flowers, fruits, and sandalwood paste, / and offering milk-rice according to one's means, O twice-born ones,

5.264.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ vrataṃ vai bhīṣmapaṃcakam..
saṃprāpyate phalaṃ caiva vratānāṃ niyamaiḥ saha..6.265.20..
5.264.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं व्रतं वै भीष्मपंचकम्..
संप्राप्यते फलं चैव व्रतानां नियमैः सह..6.265.20..
5.264.m: this entire Bhīṣmapañcaka vow has been related to you; / and its fruit is obtained together with the observances of the vows.

5.264.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ.. yadetadbhavatā proktamaśūnyaśāyinīvratam..
indreṇa yatkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ tuṣṭyarthaṃ cakrapāṇinaḥ..
prasuptasya mahābhāga phalaṃ caiva prakīrtitam..21..
5.264.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः.. यदेतद्भवता प्रोक्तमशून्यशायिनीव्रतम्..
इन्द्रेण यत्कृतं पूर्वं तुष्ट्यर्थं चक्रपाणिनः..
प्रसुप्तस्य महाभाग फलं चैव प्रकीर्तितम्..21..
5.264.m: The seers said: / This Aśūnyaśayanī vow which was described by you, / which was performed of old by Indra for the pleasure of the wielder of the discus / while he lay sleeping, O highly fortunate one, and its fruit was proclaimed—

5.264.s:
kasminkāle prakartavyaṃ kenaiva vidhinā tathā..
tasmātsūta mahābhāga vidhānaṃ vistarādvada..22..
5.264.d:
कस्मिन्काले प्रकर्तव्यं केनैव विधिना तथा..
तस्मात्सूत महाभाग विधानं विस्तराद्वद..22..
5.264.m: at what time is it to be performed, and by what rite? / Therefore, O highly fortunate Sūta, declare the procedure in detail!

5.264.s:
sūta uvāca..
śrāvaṇyāṃ samatītāyāṃ dvitīyādivase sthite..
prātarutthāya viprendrā nakṣatre viṣṇudaivate..
pāpiṣṭhaiḥ patitairmlecchaiḥ saṃbhāṣaṃ naiva kārayet..23..
5.264.d:
सूत उवाच..
श्रावण्यां समतीतायां द्वितीयादिवसे स्थिते..
प्रातरुत्थाय विप्रेन्द्रा नक्षत्रे विष्णुदैवते..
पापिष्ठैः पतितैर्म्लेच्छैः संभाषं नैव कारयेत्..23..
5.264.m: Sūta said: / When the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa has passed, on the second lunar day, / having risen in the morning, O best of brahmins, when the asterism has Viṣṇu as its deity, / one must not hold conversation with sinners, outcasts, or mlecchas.

5.264.s:
tato madhyāhnasamaye snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ..
jalaśāyinamāsādya maṃtreṇānena pūjayet..24..
5.264.d:
ततो मध्याह्नसमये स्नात्वा धौतांबरः शुचिः..
जलशायिनमासाद्य मंत्रेणानेन पूजयेत्..24..
5.264.m: Then, having bathed at midday, clean in washed garments, / approaching the sleeper upon the waters, one should worship him with this mantra:

5.264.s:
śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkāṃta śrīdhāmañchrīpate'vyaya..
gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmadam..25..
5.264.d:
श्रीवत्सधारिञ्छ्रीकांत श्रीधामञ्छ्रीपतेऽव्यय..
गार्हस्थ्यं मा प्रणाशं मे यातु धर्मार्थकामदम्..25..
5.264.m: 'O bearer of the Śrīvatsa, beloved of Śrī, abode of Śrī, lord of Śrī, imperishable one! / May my householder's life, which grants duty, wealth, and desire, not perish!

5.264.s:
pitaro mā praṇaśyaṃtu mā praṇaśyaṃtu cāgnayaḥ..
devatā mā praṇaśyaṃtu matto dāṃpatyabhedataḥ..26..
5.264.d:
पितरो मा प्रणश्यंतु मा प्रणश्यंतु चाग्नयः..
देवता मा प्रणश्यंतु मत्तो दांपत्यभेदतः..26..
5.264.m: May the ancestors not perish, and may the sacred fires not perish! / May the deities not perish from me through the separation of husband and wife!

5.264.s:
lakṣmyā viyujyase kṛṣṇa na kadācidyathā bhavān..
tathā kalatrasambandho deva mā me praṇaśyatu..27..
5.264.d:
लक्ष्म्या वियुज्यसे कृष्ण न कदाचिद्यथा भवान्..
तथा कलत्रसम्बन्धो देव मा मे प्रणश्यतु..27..
5.264.m: Just as you, O Kṛṣṇa, are never separated from Lakṣmī, / even so, O Lord, may my union with my wife not perish!

5.264.s:
lakṣmyā hyaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ yathā te deva sarvadā..
śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathā janmani janmani.. 28..
5.264.d:
लक्ष्म्या ह्यशून्यं शयनं यथा ते देव सर्वदा..
शय्या ममाप्यशून्यास्तु तथा जन्मनि जन्मनि.. 28..
5.264.m: Just as your couch, O Lord, is never empty of Lakṣmī, / so may my bed also be not empty in birth after birth!'

5.264.s:
evamarthaṃ nivedyātha tato vipraṃ prapūjayet..
yathāśaktyā dvijaśreṣṭhā vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet..29..
5.264.d:
एवमर्थं निवेद्याथ ततो विप्रं प्रपूजयेत्..
यथाशक्त्या द्विजश्रेष्ठा वित्तशाठ्यं विवर्जयेत्..29..
5.264.m: Having thus made the request, one should then worship a brahmin; / according to one's capacity, O best of twice-born ones, one should avoid dishonesty regarding wealth.

5.264.s:
evaṃ bhādrapade māsi āśvine kārtike tathā..
pūjayecca jagannāthaṃ jalaśāyinamacyutam..6.265.30..
5.264.d:
एवं भाद्रपदे मासि आश्विने कार्तिके तथा..
पूजयेच्च जगन्नाथं जलशायिनमच्युतम्..6.265.30..
5.264.m: Thus in the month of Bhādrapada, and likewise in Āśvina and Kārtika, / one should worship the Lord of the world, Acyuta sleeping upon the waters.

5.264.s:
akṣārabhojanaṃ kāryaṃ viśeṣāttailavarjitam..
samāptau ca tato dadyādbrāhmaṇeṃdrāya bhaktitaḥ..31..
5.264.d:
अक्षारभोजनं कार्यं विशेषात्तैलवर्जितम्..
समाप्तौ च ततो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणेंद्राय भक्तितः..31..
5.264.m: Saltless food should be eaten, especially avoiding oil; / and upon completion, one should then give with devotion to a noble brahmin

5.264.s:
phalavrīhisamopetāṃ śayyāṃ vastrasamanvitām..
suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ ca tathaiva ca phalaṃ labhet..32..
5.264.d:
फलव्रीहिसमोपेतां शय्यां वस्त्रसमन्विताम्..
सुवर्णं दक्षिणायां च तथैव च फलं लभेत्..32..
5.264.m: a bed provided with fruits and rice and furnished with cloths, / and gold as a sacrificial gift; and in this way one will obtain the fruit.

5.264.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute samyagvratametatsamāhitaḥ..
tasya tuṣṭipathaṃ yāti jalaśāyī jagadguruḥ..33..
5.264.d:
एवं यः कुरुते सम्यग्व्रतमेतत्समाहितः..
तस्य तुष्टिपथं याति जलशायी जगद्गुरुः..33..
5.264.m: Whoever performs this vow properly with concentrated mind, / enters the path of satisfaction of the sleeper upon the waters, the teacher of the universe.

5.264.s:
yathā śakrasya saṃtuṣṭaḥ pūrvameva dvijottamāḥ..
aśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ tasya bhavejjanmani janmani..34..
5.264.d:
यथा शक्रस्य संतुष्टः पूर्वमेव द्विजोत्तमाः..
अशून्यं शयनं तस्य भवेज्जन्मनि जन्मनि..34..
5.264.m: Just as he was pleased with Śakra of old, O best of twice-born ones, / that man's bed will not be empty in birth after birth.

5.264.s:
aṣṭamāsakṛtaṃ pāpamajñānājjñānato'pi vā..
aśūnyaśayanātsarvaṃ vratānnāśaṃ nayetpumān..35..
5.264.d:
अष्टमासकृतं पापमज्ञानाज्ज्ञानतोऽपि वा..
अशून्यशयनात्सर्वं व्रतान्नाशं नयेत्पुमान्..35..
5.264.m: Sin committed during eight months, whether through ignorance or knowledge, / a man brings to destruction through this Aśūnyaśayana vow.

5.264.s:
putrahīnā ca yā nārī kākavandhyā ca yā bhavet..
vidhavā yā karotyetadvratamevaṃ samāhitā..
tasyāstuṣṭo jagannāthaḥ kāyaśuddhiṃ prayacchati..36..
5.264.d:
पुत्रहीना च या नारी काकवन्ध्या च या भवेत्..
विधवा या करोत्येतद्व्रतमेवं समाहिता..
तस्यास्तुष्टो जगन्नाथः कायशुद्धिं प्रयच्छति..36..
5.264.m: And whatever woman is without a son, or has borne only one child, / or is a widow, who performs this vow thus with concentrated mind— / pleased with her, the Lord of the world bestows bodily purity.

5.264.s:
na tasyā jāyate buddhiḥ kadācitpāpasaṃbhavā..
na kāmopahatā buddhiḥ kathaṃcidapi jāyate..37..
5.264.d:
न तस्या जायते बुद्धिः कदाचित्पापसंभवा..
न कामोपहता बुद्धिः कथंचिदपि जायते..37..
5.264.m: Never does an intention born of sin arise in her; / never in any way is her mind overcome by lust.

5.264.s:
kumārikāpi yā samyagvratametatsamācaret..
sā patiṃ labhate viprāḥ kulīnaṃ rūpasaṃyutam..38..
5.264.d:
कुमारिकापि या सम्यग्व्रतमेतत्समाचरेत्..
सा पतिं लभते विप्राः कुलीनं रूपसंयुतम्..38..
5.264.m: Even an unmarried maiden who properly undertakes this vow, / obtains a husband of noble lineage and endowed with beauty, O brahmins.

5.264.s:
niṣkāmaḥ kurute yastu vratametatsamāhitaḥ..
cāturmāsyudbhavānāṃ ca niyamānāṃ phalaṃ labhet..39..
5.264.d:
निष्कामः कुरुते यस्तु व्रतमेतत्समाहितः..
चातुर्मास्युद्भवानां च नियमानां फलं लभेत्..39..
5.264.m: And he who, free from desire, performs this vow with concentrated mind, / obtains the fruit of the observances arising from the four-month period.

5.264.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye jalaśāyyupākhyāne aśūnyaśayanavratamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcaṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..265..
5.264.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये जलशाय्युपाख्याने अशून्यशयनव्रतमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः..265..
5.264.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of the Aśūnyaśayana Vow in the Story of the Sleeper upon the Waters,' in the Glory of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.265.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
śrutāni mukhyatīrthāni tatkṣetraprodbhavāni ca..
yeṣu snāto naraḥ smyaksarva tīrthaphalaṃ labhet..1..
5.265.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः..
श्रुतानि मुख्यतीर्थानि तत्क्षेत्रप्रोद्भवानि च..
येषु स्नातो नरः स्म्यक्सर्व तीर्थफलं लभेत्..1..
5.265.m: The seers said: / The principal sacred fords originating in that sacred field have been heard, / bathed in which a man properly obtains the fruit of all sacred fords.

5.265.s:
liṃgāni ca mahābhāga tatra mukhyāni yāni ca..
yairdṛṣṭairlabhyate śreyaḥ sarveṣāṃ tāni no vada..2..
5.265.d:
लिंगानि च महाभाग तत्र मुख्यानि यानि च..
यैर्दृष्टैर्लभ्यते श्रेयः सर्वेषां तानि नो वद..2..
5.265.m: And which are the principal liṅgas there, O highly fortunate one, / by seeing which welfare is obtained by all? Tell them to us!

5.265.s:
sūta uvāca..
tatra ca maṃkaṇākhyaṃ tu liṃgamasti suśobhanam..
tathā siddheśvaraṃ nāma gautameśvarasaṃyutam..3..
5.265.d:
सूत उवाच..
तत्र च मंकणाख्यं तु लिंगमस्ति सुशोभनम्..
तथा सिद्धेश्वरं नाम गौतमेश्वरसंयुतम्..3..
5.265.m: Sūta said: / There is indeed a very beautiful liṅga named Maṅkaṇa; / likewise one named Siddheśvara, together with Gautameśvara,

5.265.s:
kapāleśvamanyacca caturthaṃ parikīrtitam..
ekaikaṃ sarvaliṃgānāṃ phalaṃ yacchatyasaṃśayam..
yathoktavidhinā samyagyathoktaṃ dvijasattamāḥ..4..
5.265.d:
कपालेश्वमन्यच्च चतुर्थं परिकीर्तितम्..
एकैकं सर्वलिंगानां फलं यच्छत्यसंशयम्..
यथोक्तविधिना सम्यग्यथोक्तं द्विजसत्तमाः..4..
5.265.m: and Kapāleśvara is proclaimed as the fourth. / Each one gives the fruit of all liṅgas without a doubt, / when properly [worshipped] according to the prescribed rule, as has been said, O best of twice-born ones.

5.265.s:
tatra tāvatpravakṣyāmi maṃkaṇeśvarajaṃ phalam..
makārākṣarayuktasya liṃgasyātra dvijottamāḥ..5..
5.265.d:
तत्र तावत्प्रवक्ष्यामि मंकणेश्वरजं फलम्..
मकाराक्षरयुक्तस्य लिंगस्यात्र द्विजोत्तमाः..5..
5.265.m: There, first I will declare the fruit arising from Maṅkaṇeśvara, / the liṅga endowed with the syllable 'Ma' here, O best of twice-born ones.

5.265.s:
śivarātriṃ samāsādya yastasya puruṣo dvijāḥ..
kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ rātrau nirāhāraḥ sthitaḥ śuciḥ..6..
5.265.d:
शिवरात्रिं समासाद्य यस्तस्य पुरुषो द्विजाः..
कुर्याज्जागरणं रात्रौ निराहारः स्थितः शुचिः..6..
5.265.m: The man who, on reaching Śivarātri, O twice-born ones, / keeps vigil through the night, remaining fast-free and pure,

5.265.s:
sarvaliṃgodbhavaṃ caiva phalaṃ darśanasaṃbhavam..
jāyate nātra saṃdeha ityuvāca haraḥ svayam..7..
5.265.d:
सर्वलिंगोद्भवं चैव फलं दर्शनसंभवम्..
जायते नात्र संदेह इत्युवाच हरः स्वयम्..7..
5.265.m: the fruit arising from all liṅgas and produced by their darśana / arises for him, there is no doubt in this—so Hara himself declared.

5.265.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
śivarātrirmahābhāga kasminkāle tu sā bhavet..
vidhyānaṃ caiva māhātmyaṃ sarvaṃ no vistarādvada..8..
5.265.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः..
शिवरात्रिर्महाभाग कस्मिन्काले तु सा भवेत्..
विध्यानं चैव माहात्म्यं सर्वं नो विस्तराद्वद..8..
5.265.m: The seers said: / At what time does that Śivarātri occur, O highly fortunate one? / Declare to us all the rule and its māhātmya in detail!

5.265.s:
sūta uvāca.. māghasya kṛṣṇapakṣe yā tithiścaiva caturdaśī..
tasyā rātriḥ samākhyātā śivarātrisamudbhavā..9..
5.265.d:
सूत उवाच.. माघस्य कृष्णपक्षे या तिथिश्चैव चतुर्दशी..
तस्या रात्रिः समाख्याता शिवरात्रिसमुद्भवा..9..
5.265.m: Sūta said: / The fourteenth lunar day in the dark half of Māgha— / the night of that [day] is proclaimed as being Śivarātri.

5.265.s:
tasyāṃ sarveṣu liṃgeṣu sadā saṃkramate haraḥ..
viśeṣātsarvapuṇyeṣu khyāteyaṃ maṃkaṇeśvare..6.266.10..
5.265.d:
तस्यां सर्वेषु लिंगेषु सदा संक्रमते हरः..
विशेषात्सर्वपुण्येषु ख्यातेयं मंकणेश्वरे..6.266.10..
5.265.m: On that night, Hara always enters into all liṅgas, / especially among all holy ones; this is famous in Maṅkaṇeśvara.

5.265.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
śivarātriḥ kathaṃ jātā kenaiṣā ca vinirmitā..
kasmādbahuphalā jātā sarvaṃ no vistarādvada..11..
5.265.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः..
शिवरात्रिः कथं जाता केनैषा च विनिर्मिता..
कस्माद्बहुफला जाता सर्वं नो विस्तराद्वद..11..
5.265.m: The seers said: / How did Śivarātri arise, and by whom was it established? / Why has it become productive of great fruit? Tell us all in detail!

5.265.s:
sūta uvāca..
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi pūrvavṛttaṃ kathānakam..
bhartṛyajñasya saṃvādamaśvasenasya bhūpateḥ..12..
5.265.d:
सूत उवाच..
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि पूर्ववृत्तं कथानकम्..
भर्तृयज्ञस्य संवादमश्वसेनस्य भूपतेः..12..
5.265.m: Sūta said: / Here I shall tell you an ancient narrative of past events: / the conversation between Bhartṛyajña and King Aśvasena.

5.265.s:
ānartādhipatiḥ pūrvamaśvasena iti smṛtaḥ..
āsīddharmaparo nityaṃ vedavedāgaṃpāragaḥ..13..
5.265.d:
आनर्ताधिपतिः पूर्वमश्वसेन इति स्मृतः..
आसीद्धर्मपरो नित्यं वेदवेदागंपारगः..13..
5.265.m: Formerly, there was a ruler of Ānarta named Aśvasena. / He was ever devoted to dharma and had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.265.s:
bhartṛyajñaḥ purā tena idaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ kutūhalāt..
kalikālaṃ samudvīkṣya vardhamānaṃ dinedine..14..
5.265.d:
भर्तृयज्ञः पुरा तेन इदं पृष्टः कुतूहलात्..
कलिकालं समुद्वीक्ष्य वर्धमानं दिनेदिने..14..
5.265.m: Out of curiosity, he previously asked Bhartṛyajña this question, / seeing the Kali Age waxing day by day.

5.265.s:
aśvasena uvāca..
kalikālakṛte kiṃcidvrataṃ me vada sanmune..
svalpāyāsaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam..15..
5.265.d:
अश्वसेन उवाच..
कलिकालकृते किंचिद्व्रतं मे वद सन्मुने..
स्वल्पायासं महत्पुण्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्..15..
5.265.m: Aśvasena said: / 'O good sage, tell me of some observance for the Kali Age / involving little exertion yet yielding great merit and destroying all sins.

5.265.s:
svalpāyuṣaḥ sadā martyā brahmankṛtayuge purā..
tretāyāṃ dvāpare caiva kimu prāpte kalau yuge..16.
5.265.d:
स्वल्पायुषः सदा मर्त्या ब्रह्मन्कृतयुगे पुरा..
त्रेतायां द्वापरे चैव किमु प्राप्ते कलौ युगे..16.
5.265.m: Mortals always had short lifespans, O brahmin, formerly in the Kṛta age, / and likewise in the Tretā and Dvāpara; how much more so when the Kali age has arrived!

5.265.s: tasmādvarṣavrataṃ tyaktvā kiṃcidekāhnikaṃ vada..17..
5.265.d: तस्माद्वर्षव्रतं त्यक्त्वा किंचिदेकाह्निकं वद..17..
5.265.m: Therefore, leave aside year-long observances and tell me of one lasting a single day.

5.265.s:
śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇikam..
na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ vāsya na vā kṛtam..18.
5.265.d:
श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम्..
न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतं वास्य न वा कृतम्..18.
5.265.m: One should do today the work of tomorrow, and in the morning the work of the afternoon; / for death does not wait to see whether a man’s work is done or undone.'

5.265.s:
tasya tadvacaṃ śrutvā bhartṛyajña udāradhīḥ..
abravītsuciraṃ dhyātvā jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā.. 19..
5.265.d:
तस्य तद्वचं श्रुत्वा भर्तृयज्ञ उदारधीः..
अब्रवीत्सुचिरं ध्यात्वा ज्ञात्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा.. 19..
5.265.m: Hearing his words, the noble-minded Bhartṛyajña / meditated for a long time, perceived with divine vision, and spoke:

5.265.s:
asti rājanvrataṃ puṇyaṃ śivarātrītisaṃjñitam..
ekāhnikaṃ mahārāja sarvapātakanāśanam..6.266.20..
5.265.d:
अस्ति राजन्व्रतं पुण्यं शिवरात्रीतिसंज्ञितम्..
एकाह्निकं महाराज सर्वपातकनाशनम्..6.266.20..
5.265.m: 'O king, there is an auspicious observance known as Śivarātri, / lasting a single day, O great king, which destroys all sins.

5.265.s:
tatra yaddīyate dānaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ tathaiva ca..
sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti rātri jāgaraṇe kṛte..21..
5.265.d:
तत्र यद्दीयते दानं हुतं जप्तं तथैव च..
सर्वमक्षयतां याति रात्रि जागरणे कृते..21..
5.265.m: Whatever gift is offered, whatever is sacrificed, and whatever is recited in prayer there, / all becomes inexhaustible when the night vigil is observed.

5.265.s:
aputro labhate putrānadhano dhanamāpnuyāt..
svalpāyurdīrghamāyuṣyaṃ śatrūṇāṃ caiva saṃkṣayam..22..
5.265.d:
अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रानधनो धनमाप्नुयात्..
स्वल्पायुर्दीर्घमायुष्यं शत्रूणां चैव संक्षयम्..22..
5.265.m: The childless obtains sons; the poor acquires wealth; / one of short life attains long life, and also the destruction of enemies.

5.265.s:
yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyanvratametatsamācaret..
taṃtaṃ samāpnuyānmartyo niṣkāmo mokṣamāpnuyāt..23..
5.265.d:
यंयं काममभिध्यायन्व्रतमेतत्समाचरेत्..
तंतं समाप्नुयान्मर्त्यो निष्कामो मोक्षमाप्नुयात्..23..
5.265.m: Whatever desire a mortal keeps in mind while undertaking this observance, / that very desire he will obtain; if free of desire, he will attain liberation.

5.265.s:
kārpaṇyenātha vittena yadi kuryātprajāgaram..
tathā varṣakṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ..24..
5.265.d:
कार्पण्येनाथ वित्तेन यदि कुर्यात्प्रजागरम्..
तथा वर्षकृतात्पापान्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः..24..
5.265.m: Even if he keeps vigil with stinginess or with [modest] wealth, / he is nonetheless freed from the sin accumulated over a year; of this there is no doubt.

5.265.s:
yāni kānyatra liṃgāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca..
teṣu saṃkramate devastasyāṃ rātrau yato haraḥ..25..
5.265.d:
यानि कान्यत्र लिंगानि स्थावराणि चराणि च..
तेषु संक्रमते देवस्तस्यां रात्रौ यतो हरः..25..
5.265.m: Because whatever liṅgas there are here, both stationary and movable, / into them Lord Hara enters on that night;

5.265.s:
śivarātristataḥ proktā tena sā haravallabhā..
prārthitaḥ sa suraiḥ sarvairlokānugrahakāmyayā..26..
5.265.d:
शिवरात्रिस्ततः प्रोक्ता तेन सा हरवल्लभा..
प्रार्थितः स सुरैः सर्वैर्लोकानुग्रहकाम्यया..26..
5.265.m: therefore it is called Śivarātri, and for that reason it is dear to Hara. / He was prayed to by all the gods out of a desire to show grace to the worlds:

5.265.s:
bhagavankalikāle'sminsarvapāpasamanvite..
varṣapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ dinamekaṃ kṣitau vraja..
yena tvatpūjayā pūtā martyāḥ śuddhimavāpnuyuḥ..27..
5.265.d:
भगवन्कलिकालेऽस्मिन्सर्वपापसमन्विते..
वर्षपापविशुद्ध्यर्थं दिनमेकं क्षितौ व्रज..
येन त्वत्पूजया पूता मर्त्याः शुद्धिमवाप्नुयुः..27..
5.265.m: "O Blessed One, in this Kali Age filled with all manner of sins, / go to the earth for a single day to purify the sins of the year, / so that, purified by your worship, mortals may attain purity.

5.265.s:
tato dattaṃ hutaṃ teṣāmasmākamupatiṣṭhati..
yaducchiṣṭaṃ narairdattaṃ tadvṛthā jāyate'khilam..28..
5.265.d:
ततो दत्तं हुतं तेषामस्माकमुपतिष्ठति..
यदुच्छिष्टं नरैर्दत्तं तद्वृथा जायतेऽखिलम्..28..
5.265.m: Only then will what is offered and sacrificed by them reach us. / Whatever is offered by men when defiled turns entirely to waste.

5.265.s:
kalikāle na cāsmākaṃ kiṃcidevopatiṣṭhati..
aśuddhairmānavairdattaṃ prabhūtamapi śaṃkara..29..
5.265.d:
कलिकाले न चास्माकं किंचिदेवोपतिष्ठति..
अशुद्धैर्मानवैर्दत्तं प्रभूतमपि शंकर..29..
5.265.m: And in the Kali Age, nothing at all reaches us / when offered by impure men, even if abundant, O Śaṃkara."

5.265.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca..
māghamāsasya kṛṣṇāyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ sureśvara..
ahaṃ yāsyāmi bhūpṛṣṭhe rātrau naiva divā kalau..6.266.30..
5.265.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच..
माघमासस्य कृष्णायां चतुर्दश्यां सुरेश्वर..
अहं यास्यामि भूपृष्ठे रात्रौ नैव दिवा कलौ..6.266.30..
5.265.m: The Blessed One said: / 'On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Māgha, O lord of the gods, / I will go to the surface of the earth in the Kali Age—by night, not by day.

5.265.s:
liṃgeṣu ca samasteṣu caleṣu sthāvareṣu ca..
saṃkramiṣyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ varṣapāpaviśuddhaye..31..
5.265.d:
लिंगेषु च समस्तेषु चलेषु स्थावरेषु च..
संक्रमिष्याम्यसंदिग्धं वर्षपापविशुद्धये..31..
5.265.m: And into all liṅgas, movable and stationary, / I shall enter without doubt, for the purification of the sins of the year.

5.265.s:
tasyāṃ rātrau hi me pūjāṃ yaḥ kariṣyati mānavaḥ..
maṃtrairetaiḥ suraśreṣṭha vipāpmā sa bhaviṣyati..32..
5.265.d:
तस्यां रात्रौ हि मे पूजां यः करिष्यति मानवः..
मंत्रैरेतैः सुरश्रेष्ठ विपाप्मा स भविष्यति..32..
5.265.m: For whatever person performs my worship on that night / with these mantras, O best of the gods, shall be freed from sin:

5.265.s:
oṃ sadyojātāya namaḥ..
oṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ..
oṃ ghorāya namaḥ..
oṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ..
oṃ īśānāya namaḥ..
evaṃ vaktrāṇi saṃpūjya gandhapuṣpānulepanaiḥ..
vastrairdīpaiśca naivedyaistato'rghaṃ saṃpradāpayet..
maṃtreṇānena saṃpūjya māṃ dhyātvā manasi sthitam..33.
5.265.d:
ओं सद्योजाताय नमः..
ओं वामदेवाय नमः..
ओं घोराय नमः..
ओं तत्पुरुषाय नमः..
ओं ईशानाय नमः..
एवं वक्त्राणि संपूज्य गन्धपुष्पानुलेपनैः..
वस्त्रैर्दीपैश्च नैवेद्यैस्ततोऽर्घं संप्रदापयेत्..
मंत्रेणानेन संपूज्य मां ध्यात्वा मनसि स्थितम्..33.
5.265.m: "Om, reverence to Sadyojāta; / Om, reverence to Vāmadeva; / Om, reverence to Ghora; / Om, reverence to Tatpuruṣa; / Om, reverence to Īśāna." / Having thus worshipped the faces with perfumes, flowers, unguents, / garments, lamps, and food-offerings, he should then present the water offering, / worshipping with this mantra and meditating on me seated in his mind:

5.265.s:
gaurīvallabha deveśa sarvādya śaśiśekhara..
varṣapāpaviśuddhyarthamargho me pratigṛhyatām..34.
5.265.d:
गौरीवल्लभ देवेश सर्वाद्य शशिशेखर..
वर्षपापविशुद्ध्यर्थमर्घो मे प्रतिगृह्यताम्..34.
5.265.m: "O beloved of Gaurī, lord of the gods, first of all, adorned with the moon! / May my water offering be accepted for the purification of the sins of the year."

5.265.s:
tataḥ saṃpūjayedvipraṃ bhojanācchādanādibhiḥ..
dattvātha dakṣiṇāṃ tasmai vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet..35..
5.265.d:
ततः संपूजयेद्विप्रं भोजनाच्छादनादिभिः..
दत्त्वाथ दक्षिणां तस्मै वित्तशाठ्यं विवर्जयेत्..35..
5.265.m: Then he should worship a brahmin with food, clothing, and other gifts; / and having given him a priestly fee, he must avoid stinginess with his wealth,

5.265.s: dharmākhyānakathābhiśca salāsyaistāṃḍavaistathā..36..
5.265.d: धर्माख्यानकथाभिश्च सलास्यैस्तांडवैस्तथा..36..
5.265.m: and [pass the night] with stories and discourses on dharma, and with lāsya and tāṇḍava dances.

5.265.s:
evaṃ kariṣyate yo'tra vratametatsureśvara..
varṣapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ bhaviṣyati..37..
5.265.d:
एवं करिष्यते योऽत्र व्रतमेतत्सुरेश्वर..
वर्षपापविशुद्ध्यर्थं प्रायश्चित्तं भविष्यति..37..
5.265.m: Whoever performs this observance in this manner, O lord of the gods, / will obtain an expiation for the purification of the sins of the year.'

5.265.s:
tacchrutvā tridaśāḥ sarve praṇamya śaśiśekharam..
saṃprahṛṣṭā naraśreṣṭha svāni sthānāni bhejire..38..
5.265.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा त्रिदशाः सर्वे प्रणम्य शशिशेखरम्..
संप्रहृष्टा नरश्रेष्ठ स्वानि स्थानानि भेजिरे..38..
5.265.m: Hearing that, all the gods bowed down to the moon-crested god / and, greatly delighted, O best of men, returned to their respective abodes.

5.265.s:
preṣayāmāsururvyāṃ ca nāradaṃ munisattamam..
prabodhanāya lokānāṃ śivarātrikṛte sadā..39..
5.265.d:
प्रेषयामासुरुर्व्यां च नारदं मुनिसत्तमम्..
प्रबोधनाय लोकानां शिवरात्रिकृते सदा..39..
5.265.m: And they dispatched Nārada, the best of sages, to the earth / to awaken the worlds forever concerning the Śivarātri.

5.265.s:
so'pi gatvā dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ śrāvayāmāsa sarvataḥ..
śivarātrestu māhātmyaṃ yaduktaṃ śūlapāṇinā.. 6.266.40..
5.265.d:
सोऽपि गत्वा धरापृष्ठं श्रावयामास सर्वतः..
शिवरात्रेस्तु माहात्म्यं यदुक्तं शूलपाणिना.. 6.266.40..
5.265.m: He too went to the surface of the earth and proclaimed everywhere / the māhātmya of Śivarātri, as spoken by the Trident-holder.

5.265.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti saṃjātā śivarātrirdharātale..
sarvakāmapradā puṇyā sarvapātakanāśinī..41..
5.265.d:
ततः प्रभृति संजाता शिवरात्रिर्धरातले..
सर्वकामप्रदा पुण्या सर्वपातकनाशिनी..41..
5.265.m: From that time forth, Śivarātri came into being on the earth's surface, / bestowing all desires, auspicious, and destroying all sins.

5.265.s:
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi purāvṛttaṃ kathānakam..
yadvṛttaṃ naimiṣāraṇye lubdhakasyātra kasyacit..42..
5.265.d:
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि पुरावृत्तं कथानकम्..
यद्वृत्तं नैमिषारण्ये लुब्धकस्यात्र कस्यचित्..42..
5.265.m: Here I shall relate to you an ancient story of what took place / in Naimiṣāraṇya concerning a certain hunter.

5.265.s:
tatrāsīllubdhakaḥ kaścijjātimātrānna karmataḥ..
vyasenānābhibhūtātmā paravittāpahārakaḥ..43.
5.265.d:
तत्रासील्लुब्धकः कश्चिज्जातिमात्रान्न कर्मतः..
व्यसेनानाभिभूतात्मा परवित्तापहारकः..43.
5.265.m: There was a hunter there, hunter by birth alone and not by conduct, / his mind overcome by vice, a stealer of others' wealth.

5.265.s:
na kadācidvrataṃ tena na dattaṃ na japaḥ kṛtaḥ..
kevalaṃ ca hṛtaṃ vittaṃ lokānāṃ chalasaṃśrayāt..44..
5.265.d:
न कदाचिद्व्रतं तेन न दत्तं न जपः कृतः..
केवलं च हृतं वित्तं लोकानां छलसंश्रयात्..44..
5.265.m: He never observed a vow, gave no gifts, and performed no prayer; / he only seized the wealth of people by resorting to deceit.

5.265.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya śivarātriḥ samāgatā..
māghamāse'sitepakṣe sarvapātakanāśinī..45..
5.265.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य शिवरात्रिः समागता..
माघमासेऽसितेपक्षे सर्वपातकनाशिनी..45..
5.265.m: Then at a certain time, Śivarātri arrived / in the dark fortnight of the month of Māgha, destroying all sins.

5.265.s:
tatrāstyāyatanaṃ puṇyaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ..
tatra jāgaraṇaṃ rātrau prārabdhaṃ bahubhirjjanaiḥ..46..
5.265.d:
तत्रास्त्यायतनं पुण्यं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः..
तत्र जागरणं रात्रौ प्रारब्धं बहुभिर्ज्जनैः..46..
5.265.m: There was a holy temple there of the god of gods, the Trident-holder; / a night vigil was undertaken there by many people,

5.265.s:
nārībhirnaraśārdūla bhūṣitābhiḥ subhūṣaṇaiḥ..
athāsau ciṃtayāmāsa coro dṛṣṭvātha jāgaram..47..
5.265.d:
नारीभिर्नरशार्दूल भूषिताभिः सुभूषणैः..
अथासौ चिंतयामास चोरो दृष्ट्वाथ जागरम्..47..
5.265.m: and by women adorned with fine ornaments, O tiger among men. / Then that thief, seeing the vigil, thought to himself:

5.265.s:
gacchāmi yadi kāṃcitstrīṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ paribhūṣitām..
niṣkrāṃtāṃ bāhyataścāsya prāsādasyāpnuyāmaham..48..
5.265.d:
गच्छामि यदि कांचित्स्त्रीं भूषणैः परिभूषिताम्..
निष्क्रांतां बाह्यतश्चास्य प्रासादस्याप्नुयामहम्..48..
5.265.m: 'If I can catch some woman adorned with ornaments / coming out to the exterior of this temple,

5.265.s: tato hatvā samādāya bhūṣaṇāni vrajāmyaham..49.
5.265.d: ततो हत्वा समादाय भूषणानि व्रजाम्यहम्..49.
5.265.m: then I will kill her, take her ornaments, and depart.'

5.265.s:
evaṃ niścitya manasā gatastasya samīpataḥ.
karṇikāraṃ samāruhya sthito guptastato hi saḥ..6.266.50..
5.265.d:
एवं निश्चित्य मनसा गतस्तस्य समीपतः.
कर्णिकारं समारुह्य स्थितो गुप्तस्ततो हि सः..6.266.50..
5.265.m: Having so resolved in his mind, he went near it, / climbed a karṇikāra tree, and stayed there in hiding.

5.265.s:
vīkṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvā nārīniṣkrāmaṇodbhavāḥ..
caurakarmapravṛttasya śītārtasya viśeṣataḥ..51..
5.265.d:
वीक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वा नारीनिष्क्रामणोद्भवाः..
चौरकर्मप्रवृत्तस्य शीतार्तस्य विशेषतः..51..
5.265.m: Watching in all directions for the exit of women, / occupied with the deed of theft, and especially afflicted by the cold,

5.265.s:
alpāpi nidrā nāyātā na ca nārī vinirgatā..
tasyādhastāttato liṃgamabhavattu dharodbhavam..
gatvā ca patrāṇyādāya pracikṣepāsya copari..52..
5.265.d:
अल्पापि निद्रा नायाता न च नारी विनिर्गता..
तस्याधस्तात्ततो लिंगमभवत्तु धरोद्भवम्..
गत्वा च पत्राण्यादाय प्रचिक्षेपास्य चोपरि..52..
5.265.m: not even a little sleep came to him, nor did any woman come out. / Beneath that tree there was an earthen liṅga; / he plucked leaves and dropped them down upon it.

5.265.s:
etasminneva kāle tu prodgatastīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ..
asatīnāṃ ca caurāṇāṃ kāmināmasukhāvahaḥ.. 53..
5.265.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु प्रोद्गतस्तीक्ष्णदीधितिः..
असतीनां च चौराणां कामिनामसुखावहः.. 53..
5.265.m: At that very time, the sharp-rayed sun arose, / bringing displeasure to unchaste women, thieves, and passionate lovers.

5.265.s:
tato narāśca nāryaśca jagmuḥ svaṃsvaṃ niketanam..
upacāraparāḥ śāṃtāḥ praṇipatya maheśvaram..54..
5.265.d:
ततो नराश्च नार्यश्च जग्मुः स्वंस्वं निकेतनम्..
उपचारपराः शांताः प्रणिपत्य महेश्वरम्..54..
5.265.m: Then men and women departed to their respective homes, / tranquil after performing their service, having bowed down to the Great Lord.

5.265.s:
so'pi cauro nirāśaśca kṣutkṣāmaḥ śītavihvalaḥ..
avatīrya drumāttasmādupāyaṃ kaṃcidāśritaḥ..55..
5.265.d:
सोऽपि चौरो निराशश्च क्षुत्क्षामः शीतविह्वलः..
अवतीर्य द्रुमात्तस्मादुपायं कंचिदाश्रितः..55..
5.265.m: The thief too, disappointed, emaciated with hunger and trembling with cold, / climbed down from that tree and resorted to some means [of livelihood].

5.265.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā paṃcatvaṃ samapadyata..
jāto jātismaraḥ so'tha daśārṇādhipatergṛhe..56..
5.265.d:
ततः कालेन महता पंचत्वं समपद्यत..
जातो जातिस्मरः सोऽथ दशार्णाधिपतेर्गृहे..56..
5.265.m: Then after a long time he met his death. / He was born remembering his former birth in the house of the king of Daśārṇa,

5.265.s:
upavāsaprabhāvena balādapi prajāgarāt..
śivarātrestathā tasya liṅgasyāpi prapūjayā..57..
5.265.d:
उपवासप्रभावेन बलादपि प्रजागरात्..
शिवरात्रेस्तथा तस्य लिङ्गस्यापि प्रपूजया..57..
5.265.m: by virtue of the fast, through the vigil kept perforce, / and by the worship of that liṅga on Śivarātri.

5.265.s:
tato rājyaṃ samāsādya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat..
kārayāmāsa liṃgasya prāsādaṃ tasya śobhanam..58..
5.265.d:
ततो राज्यं समासाद्य पितृपैतामहं महत्..
कारयामास लिंगस्य प्रासादं तस्य शोभनम्..58..
5.265.m: Then, having attained the great kingdom of his fathers and grandfathers, / he had a beautiful temple built for that liṅga.

5.265.s:
varṣevarṣe samāśritya śivarātrau prajāgarāt..
upavāsaparobhūtvā gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ..59..
5.265.d:
वर्षेवर्षे समाश्रित्य शिवरात्रौ प्रजागरात्..
उपवासपरोभूत्वा गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः..59..
5.265.m: Year after year resorting [there], keeping vigil on Śivarātri, / intent on fasting, amidst the sounds of songs and musical instruments,

5.265.s:
dharmākhyānakathābhiśca gītadhvanibhireva ca..
pūrvoktamaṃtraiḥ saṃpūjya arghaṃ dattvā vidhānataḥ..
saṃtarpya brāhmaṇānkāmairjagāma nilayaṃ nijam..6.266.60..
5.265.d:
धर्माख्यानकथाभिश्च गीतध्वनिभिरेव च..
पूर्वोक्तमंत्रैः संपूज्य अर्घं दत्त्वा विधानतः..
संतर्प्य ब्राह्मणान्कामैर्जगाम निलयं निजम्..6.266.60..
5.265.m: and with stories narrating righteousness, and with the sounds of singing, / having worshipped with the previously mentioned mantras, having offered libations according to the injunctions, / and having gratified the brahmins with desired gifts, he would go to his own abode.

5.265.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya śivarātrau samāgatāḥ..
prāsāde tatra munayaḥ prāptā śāṇḍilyapūrvakāḥ..61..
5.265.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य शिवरात्रौ समागताः..
प्रासादे तत्र मुनयः प्राप्ता शाण्डिल्यपूर्वकाः..61..
5.265.m: Then, after some time had passed, on Śivarātri there arrived / at that temple sages headed by Śāṇḍilya.

5.265.s:
śāṃḍilyo'tha bharadvājo yavakrīto'tha gālavaḥ..
pulastyaḥ pulaho gārgyastathānye bahavo nṛpa..62..
5.265.d:
शांडिल्योऽथ भरद्वाजो यवक्रीतोऽथ गालवः..
पुलस्त्यः पुलहो गार्ग्यस्तथान्ये बहवो नृप..62..
5.265.m: Śāṇḍilya, Bharadvāja, Yavakrīta, and Gālava, / Pulastya, Pulaha, Gārgya, and many others, O king.

5.265.s:
so'pi rājā bṛhatseno daśārṇādhipateḥ sutaḥ..
saṃprāpto jāgaraṃ kartuṃ tasya liṃgasya cāgrataḥ..63..
5.265.d:
सोऽपि राजा बृहत्सेनो दशार्णाधिपतेः सुतः..
संप्राप्तो जागरं कर्तुं तस्य लिंगस्य चाग्रतः..63..
5.265.m: That King Bṛhatsena too, the son of the lord of Daśārṇa, / arrived to keep vigil before that liṅga.

5.265.s:
pūjayitvā tato devaṃ praṇipatya munīśvarān..
upaviṣṭastasya cāgre hyanujñāto dvijottamaiḥ..64..
5.265.d:
पूजयित्वा ततो देवं प्रणिपत्य मुनीश्वरान्..
उपविष्टस्तस्य चाग्रे ह्यनुज्ञातो द्विजोत्तमैः..64..
5.265.m: Having worshipped the god, and having bowed before the foremost of sages, / he sat before him with the permission of those best of the twice-born.

5.265.s:
tatastasyāgrataścakruḥ kathāste bahudhā nṛpa..
rājarṣīṇāmatītānāṃ brahmarṣīṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ..65..
5.265.d:
ततस्तस्याग्रतश्चक्रुः कथास्ते बहुधा नृप..
राजर्षीणामतीतानां ब्रह्मर्षीणां विशेषतः..65..
5.265.m: Then, before him, they recounted diverse tales, O king, / especially of royal seers and brahmin seers of the past.

5.265.s:
atha kasminkathāṃte sa taiḥ pṛṣṭo brahmavādibhiḥ..
kautukāviṣṭacittaiśca vismayotphullalocanaiḥ..66..
5.265.d:
अथ कस्मिन्कथांते स तैः पृष्टो ब्रह्मवादिभिः..
कौतुकाविष्टचित्तैश्च विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनैः..66..
5.265.m: Then, at the end of a certain story, he was asked by those who proclaim the Veda, / their minds filled with curiosity and their eyes wide with wonder:

5.265.s:
rājanpṛcchāmahe sarve vayaṃ kautūhalānvitāḥ..
yadi bravīṣi naḥ satyaṃ devatāyatane sthitaḥ..67..
5.265.d:
राजन्पृच्छामहे सर्वे वयं कौतूहलान्विताः..
यदि ब्रवीषि नः सत्यं देवतायतने स्थितः..67..
5.265.m: "O king, filled with curiosity, we all ask you: / tell us the truth, as you stand in the temple of the god.

5.265.s:
rājovāca..
yadi jñāsyāmi vipreṃdrāḥ kathayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam..
devasyāgre ca saṃpṛṣṭaḥ satyenātmānamālabhe..68..
5.265.d:
राजोवाच..
यदि ज्ञास्यामि विप्रेंद्राः कथयिष्याम्यसंशयम्..
देवस्याग्रे च संपृष्टः सत्येनात्मानमालभे..68..
5.265.m:
The king said:
If I know, O foremost of vipras, I shall certainly tell it; / and being questioned before the god, I pledge myself on truth."

5.265.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
puṣkalāni parityajya kasmāddānānyanekaśaḥ..
jāgaraṃ kartukāmo'tra svadeśādupatiṣṭhasi..69..
5.265.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः..
पुष्कलानि परित्यज्य कस्माद्दानान्यनेकशः..
जागरं कर्तुकामोऽत्र स्वदेशादुपतिष्ठसि..69..
5.265.m:
"The seers said:
Abandoning copious gifts in various ways, why do you / wait upon [him] from your own land, wishing to keep vigil here?

5.265.s:
varṣevarṣe sadā prāpte nūnaṃ tvaṃ vetsi kāraṇam..
rahasyaṃ yadi te na syāttadbravīhi narādhipa..6.266.70..
5.265.d:
वर्षेवर्षे सदा प्राप्ते नूनं त्वं वेत्सि कारणम्..
रहस्यं यदि ते न स्यात्तद्ब्रवीहि नराधिप..6.266.70..
5.265.m: Year after year, whenever it arrives, you surely know the reason; / if it is not a secret of yours, tell it, O lord of men."

5.265.s:
sūta uvāca..
savailakṣyaṃ smitaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ prāha sa durmanāḥ..
rahasyaṃ paramaṃ hyetadavācyaṃ hi dvijottamāḥ..71..
5.265.d:
सूत उवाच..
सवैलक्ष्यं स्मितं कृत्वा ततः प्राह स दुर्मनाः..
रहस्यं परमं ह्येतदवाच्यं हि द्विजोत्तमाः..71..
5.265.m:
Sūta said:
Smiling with embarrassment, he then said, downcast in mind: / "This is a supreme secret, not to be spoken, O best of the twice-born;

5.265.s: tathāpi ca vadiṣyāmi pṛṣṭo devāgrato yataḥ..72..
5.265.d: तथापि च वदिष्यामि पृष्टो देवाग्रतो यतः..72..
5.265.m: nevertheless, I will tell it, since I am questioned in front of the god."

5.265.s:
tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa pūrvadehasamudbhavam..
malimlucastato nūnaṃ śivarātrisamudbhavam..73..
5.265.d:
ततः स कथयामास पूर्वदेहसमुद्भवम्..
मलिम्लुचस्ततो नूनं शिवरात्रिसमुद्भवम्..73..
5.265.m: Then he related his origin in a former body, / and how Śivarātri indeed arose for the thief,

5.265.s:
cauryabhāvena devasya pūjanaṃ jāgarastathā..
upavāsaṃ vinā tena śivarātrau purā kṛtam..74..
5.265.d:
चौर्यभावेन देवस्य पूजनं जागरस्तथा..
उपवासं विना तेन शिवरात्रौ पुरा कृतम्..74..
5.265.m: and how in the past, with the disposition of a thief, the worship of the god, / the vigil, without fasting, was performed by him on Śivarātri,

5.265.s:
jātismaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ janmajātaṃ yathātatham..
tataste munayaḥ sarve sādhuvādānpṛthagvidhān..75..
5.265.d:
जातिस्मरणसंयुक्तं जन्मजातं यथातथम्..
ततस्ते मुनयः सर्वे साधुवादान्पृथग्विधान्..75..
5.265.m: and how the birth arose as it was, endowed with memory of former births. / Then all those sages, [offering] various words of praise

5.265.s:
nṛpottamasya rājarṣerdattvāśīrbhiḥ samanvitān..
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā prajagmuste nijāśramān..76..
5.265.d:
नृपोत्तमस्य राजर्षेर्दत्त्वाशीर्भिः समन्वितान्..
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा प्रजग्मुस्ते निजाश्रमान्..76..
5.265.m: accompanied by blessings to the best of kings, the royal seer, / having kept vigil during the night, departed to their own hermitages.

5.265.s:
so'pi rājāsamabhyarcya taṃ devaṃ tāndvijottamān..
jagāma svapuraṃ paścātkṛtvā rātrau prajāgaram..77..
5.265.d:
सोऽपि राजासमभ्यर्च्य तं देवं तान्द्विजोत्तमान्..
जगाम स्वपुरं पश्चात्कृत्वा रात्रौ प्रजागरम्..77..
5.265.m: That king too, having properly worshipped that god and those best of the twice-born, / went to his own city after having kept vigil during the night.

5.265.s:
bhartṛyajña uvāca..
śivarātriḥ samutpannā evaṃ bhūmitale nṛpa..
evaṃvidhaṃ ca māhātmyaṃ tasyāste parikīrtitam..78..
5.265.d:
भर्तृयज्ञ उवाच..
शिवरात्रिः समुत्पन्ना एवं भूमितले नृप..
एवंविधं च माहात्म्यं तस्यास्ते परिकीर्तितम्..78..
5.265.m:
Bhartṛyajña said:
Thus, O king, Śivarātri arose on the surface of the earth; / and such māhātmya of it has been proclaimed to you.

5.265.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryā sa nṛpasattama..
kalikāle viśeṣeṇa ya icchedbhūtimātmanaḥ..79..
5.265.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कार्या स नृपसत्तम..
कलिकाले विशेषेण य इच्छेद्भूतिमात्मनः..79..
5.265.m: Therefore, with every effort, it must be observed, O best of kings, / especially in the Kali age, by one who desires his own prosperity.

5.265.s:
eṣā kṛtā dilīpena nalena nahuṣeṇa ca..
māndhātrā dhuṃdhumāreṇa sagareṇa yuyutsunā..6.266.80..
5.265.d:
एषा कृता दिलीपेन नलेन नहुषेण च..
मान्धात्रा धुंधुमारेण सगरेण युयुत्सुना..6.266.80..
5.265.m: It was performed by Dilīpa, by Nala, and by Nahuṣa, / by Māndhātṛ, Dhundhumāra, Sagara, and Yuyutsu,

5.265.s:
tathānyaiśca viśeṣeṇa samyakchraddhāsamanvitaiḥ..
prāptāśca hṛdgatāḥ kāmā ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ..81..
5.265.d:
तथान्यैश्च विशेषेण सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितैः..
प्राप्ताश्च हृद्गताः कामा ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः..81..
5.265.m: and likewise by others especially, endowed with perfect faith; / and their heart's desires were attained, both divine and human.

5.265.s:
tathā caiva tu sāvitryā śriyā devyā tu sītayā..
aruṃdhatyā sarasvatyā menayā raṃbhayā tathā..82..
5.265.d:
तथा चैव तु सावित्र्या श्रिया देव्या तु सीतया..
अरुंधत्या सरस्वत्या मेनया रंभया तथा..82..
5.265.m: And likewise by Sāvitrī, by the goddess Śrī, by Sītā, / by Arundhatī, Sarasvatī, Menā, and Rambhā,

5.265.s:
iṃdrāṇyātha dṛṣadvatyā svadhayā svāhayā tathā..
ratyā prītyā prabhāvatyā gāyatryā ca nṛpottama..
sarvāḥ prāptāḥ priyānkāmānatisaubhāgyasaṃyutān..83..
5.265.d:
इंद्राण्याथ दृषद्वत्या स्वधया स्वाहया तथा..
रत्या प्रीत्या प्रभावत्या गायत्र्या च नृपोत्तम..
सर्वाः प्राप्ताः प्रियान्कामानतिसौभाग्यसंयुतान्..83..
5.265.m: by Indrāṇī, Dṛṣadvatī, Svadhā, and Svāhā, / by Rati, Prīti, Prabhāvatī, and Gāyatrī, O best of kings; / they all attained their beloved desires, endowed with great good fortune.

5.265.s:
yaścaitāṃ paṭhate vyuṣṭiṃ bhāvena śivasaṃnidhau.
dinajātpātakātso'pi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ..84..
5.265.d:
यश्चैतां पठते व्युष्टिं भावेन शिवसंनिधौ.
दिनजात्पातकात्सोऽपि मुच्यते नात्र संशयः..84..
5.265.m: And whoever recites this reward with devotion in the presence of Śiva, / he too is liberated from the sin born of the day; of this there is no doubt.

5.265.s:
nāsti gaṃgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti devo haropamaḥ..
śivarātreḥ paraṃ nāsti tapaḥ satyaṃ mayoditam..85..
5.265.d:
नास्ति गंगासमं तीर्थं नास्ति देवो हरोपमः..
शिवरात्रेः परं नास्ति तपः सत्यं मयोदितम्..85..
5.265.m: There is no sacred ford equal to Gaṅgā; there is no god like Hara; / there is no austerity higher than Śivarātri: I have spoken the truth.

5.265.s:
sarvaratnamayo meruḥ sarvāścaryamayaṃ tapaḥ..
sarvadharmamayī rājañchivarātriḥ prakīrtitāḥ..86..
5.265.d:
सर्वरत्नमयो मेरुः सर्वाश्चर्यमयं तपः..
सर्वधर्ममयी राजञ्छिवरात्रिः प्रकीर्तिताः..86..
5.265.m: Meru is composed of all jewels; austerity is full of all wonders; / Śivarātri is proclaimed to be composed of all righteousness, O king.

5.265.s:
garuḍaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ yadvannadīnāṃ sāgaro yathā.
pradhānaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ śivarātristathottamā..87..
5.265.d:
गरुडः पक्षिणां यद्वन्नदीनां सागरो यथा.
प्रधानः सर्वधर्माणां शिवरात्रिस्तथोत्तमा..87..
5.265.m: Just as Garuḍa is [foremost] among birds, as the ocean is among rivers, / so Śivarātri is the foremost, the highest among all religious duties.

5.265.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śivārātrimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..266..
5.265.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शिवारात्रिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षट्षष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः..266..
5.265.m: Thus in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra, the two hundred and sixty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Śivarātri.'

5.266.s:
sūta uvāca..
tasmādeṣā mahārāja śivarātrirvipaścitā...
kartavyā puruṣeṇātra lokadvayamabhīpsunā..1..
5.266.d:
सूत उवाच..
तस्मादेषा महाराज शिवरात्रिर्विपश्चिता...
कर्तव्या पुरुषेणात्र लोकद्वयमभीप्सुना..1..
5.266.m:
Sūta said:
Therefore, O great king, this Śivarātri should be observed / by a wise man here who desires both worlds.

5.266.s:
ānarta uvāca..
maṃkaṇeśvaramāhātmyaṃ mayā vistarataḥ śrutam..
śivarātrisamopetaṃ yattvayā parikīrtitam.. 2..
5.266.d:
आनर्त उवाच..
मंकणेश्वरमाहात्म्यं मया विस्तरतः श्रुतम्..
शिवरात्रिसमोपेतं यत्त्वया परिकीर्तितम्.. 2..
5.266.m:
Ānarta said:
The māhātmya of Maṅkaṇeśvara has been heard by me at length, / together with Śivarātri, as was proclaimed by you.

5.266.s:
sāṃprataṃ vada me kṛtsnaṃ siddheśvarasamudbhavam..
vistareṇa mahābhāga paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me..3..
5.266.d:
सांप्रतं वद मे कृत्स्नं सिद्धेश्वरसमुद्भवम्..
विस्तरेण महाभाग परं कौतूहलं हि मे..3..
5.266.m: Now tell me in full the origin of Siddheśvara / at length, O fortunate one, for great indeed is my curiosity.

5.266.s:
bhartṛyajña uvāca..
siddheśvara iti khyāto mahādevo mahīpate..
tasyotpattistvayā pūrvaṃ śrutātra vadato mama..4..
5.266.d:
भर्तृयज्ञ उवाच..
सिद्धेश्वर इति ख्यातो महादेवो महीपते..
तस्योत्पत्तिस्त्वया पूर्वं श्रुतात्र वदतो मम..4..
5.266.m:
Bhartṛyajña said:
Mahādeva is renowned as Siddheśvara, O lord of the earth; / his origin was heard by you before as I spoke here.

5.266.s:
sāṃprataṃ tatphalaṃ vacmi tasmindṛṣṭe tu dānajam..
yatphalaṃ jāyate nṝṇāṃ cakravartitva saṃbhavam..5..
5.266.d:
सांप्रतं तत्फलं वच्मि तस्मिन्दृष्टे तु दानजम्..
यत्फलं जायते नॄणां चक्रवर्तित्व संभवम्..5..
5.266.m: Now I declare the fruit arising from a gift when he is seen, / the fruit that arises for men, consisting of imperial sovereignty.

5.266.s:
tulāpuruṣadānaṃ ca tatra rājanpraśaśyate..
ya iccheccakravartitvaṃ samaste dharaṇītale..6..
5.266.d:
तुलापुरुषदानं च तत्र राजन्प्रशश्यते..
य इच्छेच्चक्रवर्तित्वं समस्ते धरणीतले..6..
5.266.m: And the gift of the person weighed on scales is praised there, O king, / for one who desires imperial sovereignty over the entire surface of the earth.

5.266.s:
ānarta uvāca..
tulāpuruṣadānasya yo vidhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ..
taṃ me sarvaṃ samācakṣva vistareṇa mahāmune..7..
5.266.d:
आनर्त उवाच..
तुलापुरुषदानस्य यो विधिः परिकीर्तितः..
तं मे सर्वं समाचक्ष्व विस्तरेण महामुने..7..
5.266.m:
Ānarta said:
The rite of the gift of the person weighed on scales which is proclaimed— / declare all of that to me at length, O great sage.

5.266.s:
bhartṛyajña uvāca..
caṃdrasūryoparāge vā ayane viṣuve tathā..
tīrthe vā puruṣaśreṣṭha tulāpuruṣasaṃbhavam..8..
5.266.d:
भर्तृयज्ञ उवाच..
चंद्रसूर्योपरागे वा अयने विषुवे तथा..
तीर्थे वा पुरुषश्रेष्ठ तुलापुरुषसंभवम्..8..
5.266.m:
Bhartṛyajña said:
During an eclipse of the moon or the sun, or at a solstice, or at an equinox, / or at a sacred ford, O best of men, relating to the person weighed on scales,

5.266.s:
praśaṃsaṃti vidhiṃ samyakprāpte vā ceṃdusaṃkṣaye..
brāhmaṇānāṃ sudāṃtānāmanuṣṭhānavatāṃ satām..9..
5.266.d:
प्रशंसंति विधिं सम्यक्प्राप्ते वा चेंदुसंक्षये..
ब्राह्मणानां सुदांतानामनुष्ठानवतां सताम्..9..
5.266.m: they rightly praise the rite; or when the new moon has arrived, / to self-controlled, observant, virtuous brahmins,

5.266.s:
vedādhyayanayuktānāṃ nirdoṣāṇāṃ ca pārthiva..
vibhajya sa bhaveddeyo naikasya ca kathaṃcana..6.267.10..
5.266.d:
वेदाध्ययनयुक्तानां निर्दोषाणां च पार्थिव..
विभज्य स भवेद्देयो नैकस्य च कथंचन..6.267.10..
5.266.m: who are engaged in the study of the Veda and faultless, O ruler of the earth, / it should be given after dividing it, and under no circumstances to a single one.

5.266.s:
śucau deśe same puṇye pūrvottaraplave śubhe..
maṃḍapaṃ kārayedvidvān ramyaṃ ṣa़ośahastakam..
tanmadhye kārayedvediṃ caturhasta pramāṇataḥ.
yajamānasya hastena hastaikena samucchritām..12..
5.266.d:
शुचौ देशे समे पुण्ये पूर्वोत्तरप्लवे शुभे..
मंडपं कारयेद्विद्वान् रम्यं ष़ओशहस्तकम्..
तन्मध्ये कारयेद्वेदिं चतुर्हस्त प्रमाणतः.
यजमानस्य हस्तेन हस्तैकेन समुच्छ्रिताम्..12..
5.266.m: In a clean, level, holy, and auspicious place that slopes toward the east or north, / the learned man should have a charming pavilion constructed, measuring sixteen cubits. / In its center he should have an altar made, measuring four cubits, / and raised up by one cubit measured by the arm of the patron.

5.266.s:
caturhastāni kuṇḍāni caturdikṣu prakalpayeta ..
ekahastapramāṇāni āyāmavyāsavistarāt..
aiśānyāmaparāṃ vediṃ hastamātrāṃ nyasecchubhām..
ratnimātrotthitāṃ caiva grahāṃstatra prakalpayet.. 14..
5.266.d:
चतुर्हस्तानि कुण्डानि चतुर्दिक्षु प्रकल्पयेत ..
एकहस्तप्रमाणानि आयामव्यासविस्तरात्..
ऐशान्यामपरां वेदिं हस्तमात्रां न्यसेच्छुभाम्..
रत्निमात्रोत्थितां चैव ग्रहांस्तत्र प्रकल्पयेत्.. 14..
5.266.m: He should prepare fire pits of four cubits in the four directions, / measuring one cubit in length and breadth. / In the northeast he should place another auspicious altar measuring just one cubit, / raised merely a span; and there he should arrange the planets.

5.266.s:
yugmāṃśca ṛtvijaḥ kāryāścaturdikṣu yathākramam..
bahvṛco'dhvaryaścaiva cchaṃdogātharvaṇāvapi.. 15..
5.266.d:
युग्मांश्च ऋत्विजः कार्याश्चतुर्दिक्षु यथाक्रमम्..
बह्वृचोऽध्वर्यश्चैव च्छंदोगाथर्वणावपि.. 15..
5.266.m: And twin officiating priests should be appointed in the four directions in proper order: / a Ṛgvedic priest, a Yajurvedic priest, a Sāmavedic priest, and an Atharvavedic priest.

5.266.s:
tūṣṇīṃ tu devatāhomastaiḥ kāryaḥ susamāhitaiḥ..
talliṃgairnṛpatemaṃtraiḥ svaśaktyā japa eva ca..16..
5.266.d:
तूष्णीं तु देवताहोमस्तैः कार्यः सुसमाहितैः..
तल्लिंगैर्नृपतेमंत्रैः स्वशक्त्या जप एव च..16..
5.266.m: A silent oblation to the deities should be performed by them, being fully concentrated, / and recitation according to their capacity with mantras having those specific deities' marks, O king.

5.266.s:
ekahastapraviṣṭaṃ tu caturhastocchritaṃ tathā..
staṃbhadvayaṃ tu kartavyaṃ vediyāmyottare sthitam..17..
5.266.d:
एकहस्तप्रविष्टं तु चतुर्हस्तोच्छ्रितं तथा..
स्तंभद्वयं तु कर्तव्यं वेदियाम्योत्तरे स्थितम्..17..
5.266.m: Two pillars should be erected, sunk one cubit deep / and four cubits high, situated to the south and north of the altar.

5.266.s:
tanmadhye suśubhaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ staṃbhajātyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ nyaset..
candanaḥ khadiro vātha bilvovā'śvattha eva vā.. 18..
5.266.d:
तन्मध्ये सुशुभं काष्ठं स्तंभजात्यं दृढं न्यसेत्..
चन्दनः खदिरो वाथ बिल्वोवाऽश्वत्थ एव वा.. 18..
5.266.m: Between them he should place a very auspicious, strong crossbeam made of timber suitable for pillars: / either sandalwood, acacia, bilva, or aśvattha;

5.266.s:
tiṃduko devadārurvā śrīparṇī vā vaṭo'thavā..
aṣṭau vṛkṣāḥ śubhāḥ śastāḥ staṃbhārthaṃ nṛpasattam..19..
5.266.d:
तिंदुको देवदारुर्वा श्रीपर्णी वा वटोऽथवा..
अष्टौ वृक्षाः शुभाः शस्ताः स्तंभार्थं नृपसत्तम्..19..
5.266.m: or timduka, devadāru, śrīparṇī, or banyan— / these eight trees are deemed auspicious and commended for the pillars, O best of kings.

5.266.s:
śikyadvaya samopetāṃ tanmadhye vinyasettulām..
snātaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ..6.267.20.
pūrayitvā samaṃtācca lokapālānyathākramam..
staṃbhānsaṃpūjayatpaścādgandhamālyānulepanaiḥ..21..
5.266.d:
शिक्यद्वय समोपेतां तन्मध्ये विन्यसेत्तुलाम्..
स्नातः शुक्लांबरधरः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनः..6.267.20.
पूरयित्वा समंताच्च लोकपालान्यथाक्रमम्..
स्तंभान्संपूजयत्पश्चाद्गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः..21..
5.266.m: In their middle he should suspend a balance fitted with two pans. / Having bathed, wearing white garments, adorned with white garlands and ointments, / after fully worshiping the world-guardians all around in their proper order, / he should then worship the pillars with perfumes, garlands, and unguents.

5.266.s:
tulāṃ ca pārthivaśreṣṭha puṇyāhaṃ ca prakīrtayet..
yajamāno nijaiḥ sarvairāyudhaiḥ kāyasaṃsthitaiḥ..22..
5.266.d:
तुलां च पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ पुण्याहं च प्रकीर्तयेत्..
यजमानो निजैः सर्वैरायुधैः कायसंस्थितैः..22..
5.266.m: And he should praise the balance, O best of kings, and proclaim an auspicious day; / the patron, bearing all his own weapons on his body,

5.266.s:
paścimāṃ diśamāsthāya prāṅmukhaḥ śraddhayā'nvitaḥ..
kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā imaṃ maṃtramudīrayet..23..
5.266.d:
पश्चिमां दिशमास्थाय प्राङ्मुखः श्रद्धयाऽन्वितः..
कृतांजलिपुटो भूत्वा इमं मंत्रमुदीरयेत्..23..
5.266.m: taking his stand in the western direction facing east, endowed with faith, / having folded his hands in reverence, should utter this mantra:

5.266.s:
brahmaṇo duhitā nityaṃ satyaṃ paramamāśritā..
kāśyapī gotrataścaiva nāmato viśrutā tulā..24..
5.266.d:
ब्रह्मणो दुहिता नित्यं सत्यं परममाश्रिता..
काश्यपी गोत्रतश्चैव नामतो विश्रुता तुला..24..
5.266.m: “O balance, daughter of Brahmā, ever resting upon supreme truth, / belonging by lineage to Kaśyapa, celebrated by name as Tulā!

5.266.s:
tvaṃ tule satyanāmāsi svabhīṣṭaṃ cātmanaḥ śubham..
kariṣyāmi prasādaṃ me sāṃnidhyaṃ kuru sāṃpratam..25..
5.266.d:
त्वं तुले सत्यनामासि स्वभीष्टं चात्मनः शुभम्..
करिष्यामि प्रसादं मे सांनिध्यं कुरु सांप्रतम्..25..
5.266.m: You, O balance, are truly named; grant your favor to me, / and now manifest your presence, so that I may accomplish my own auspicious desire.”

5.266.s:
tatastasyāṃ samāruhya svaśaktyā yatsamāhṛtam..
dānārthaṃ pūrvamāyojyaṃ śikyenyasminnarottama..26..
5.266.d:
ततस्तस्यां समारुह्य स्वशक्त्या यत्समाहृतम्..
दानार्थं पूर्वमायोज्यं शिक्येन्यस्मिन्नरोत्तम..26..
5.266.m: Then, having mounted onto it, whatever has been gathered according to one's means / should first be placed into the other pan for the sake of giving, O best of men:

5.266.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vā'tha vastraṃ cānyadabhīpsitam..
yāvatsāmyaṃ bhavedrājannātmano'bhyadhikaṃ ca vā..27..
5.266.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं वाऽथ वस्त्रं चान्यदभीप्सितम्..
यावत्साम्यं भवेद्राजन्नात्मनोऽभ्यधिकं च वा..27..
5.266.m: gold, silver, cloth, or anything else desired, / until an equality is reached, O king, or [the gifts] exceed his own [weight].

5.266.s:
tato'bhīṣṭāṃ samāsādya devatāṃ śikyamāśritaḥ..
udakaṃ jalamadhye ca tadarthaṃ prakṣipeddrutam..28..
5.266.d:
ततोऽभीष्टां समासाद्य देवतां शिक्यमाश्रितः..
उदकं जलमध्ये च तदर्थं प्रक्षिपेद्द्रुतम्..28..
5.266.m: Then, having reached the desired deity while seated in the pan, / he should quickly cast water into water for that purpose,

5.266.s:
satilaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ ca sākṣataṃ vidhipūrvakam..
avatīrya tataḥ sarvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo nivedayet..29..
5.266.d:
सतिलं सहिरण्यं च साक्षतं विधिपूर्वकम्..
अवतीर्य ततः सर्वं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो निवेदयेत्..29..
5.266.m: together with sesamum, gold, and unbroken grains, in accordance with the injunctions. / Then, having stepped down, he should offer it all to the brahmins.

5.266.s: yatphalaṃ prāpyate paścāttadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu..6.267.30..
5.266.d: यत्फलं प्राप्यते पश्चात्तदिहैकमनाः शृणु..6.267.30..
5.266.m: Whatever fruit is attained thereafter, hear that now with single-minded attention:

5.266.s:
ajānatā jānatā vā yatpāpaṃ tu bhavetkṛtam..
tatsarvaṃ nāśayenmartyo dānasyāsya prabhāvataḥ..31..
5.266.d:
अजानता जानता वा यत्पापं तु भवेत्कृतम्..
तत्सर्वं नाशयेन्मर्त्यो दानस्यास्य प्रभावतः..31..
5.266.m: Whatever sin has been committed unknowingly or knowingly, / a mortal destroys it all by the power of this gift.

5.266.s:
yāvanmātraṃ kṛtaṃ pāpamatītaṃ nṛpasattama..
tāvanmātraṃ kṣayaṃ yāti tulāpuruṣadānataḥ..32..
5.266.d:
यावन्मात्रं कृतं पापमतीतं नृपसत्तम..
तावन्मात्रं क्षयं याति तुलापुरुषदानतः..32..
5.266.m: Whatever past sin has been committed, O best of kings, / that much goes to destruction through the gift of the person weighed in the balance.

5.266.s:
īśvarāṇāṃ samādiṣṭaṃ kāyakleśabhayātmanām..
puraścaraṇametaddhi dānaṃ taulyasamudbhavam..33..
5.266.d:
ईश्वराणां समादिष्टं कायक्लेशभयात्मनाम्..
पुरश्चरणमेतद्धि दानं तौल्यसमुद्भवम्..33..
5.266.m: For lords who fear bodily affliction, this preparatory rite / of a gift originating from a weighing balance has been prescribed.

5.266.s:
etaddattaṃ dilīpena kārtavīryeṇa bhūpate..
pṛthunā purukutsena tathānyairapi pārthivaiḥ..34..
5.266.d:
एतद्दत्तं दिलीपेन कार्तवीर्येण भूपते..
पृथुना पुरुकुत्सेन तथान्यैरपि पार्थिवैः..34..
5.266.m: This was given by Dilīpa, by Kārtavīrya, O king, / by Pṛthu, by Purukutsa, and likewise by other kings.

5.266.s:
etatpuṇyaṃ praśasyaṃ ca sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām.
tulāpuruṣadānaṃ ca sarvopadravanāśanam..35..
5.266.d:
एतत्पुण्यं प्रशस्यं च सर्वकामप्रदं नृणाम्.
तुलापुरुषदानं च सर्वोपद्रवनाशनम्..35..
5.266.m: This gift of a person weighed in the balance is holy, praiseworthy, / bestowing all desires upon mortals, and destroying all afflictions.

5.266.s:
ādhayo vyādhayo na syurna vaidhavyaṃ gadodbhavam..
saṃjāyate nṛpaśreṣṭha na viyogaḥ svabandhubhiḥ..
tulāpuruṣadānasya phalametadudāhṛtam..36..
5.266.d:
आधयो व्याधयो न स्युर्न वैधव्यं गदोद्भवम्..
संजायते नृपश्रेष्ठ न वियोगः स्वबन्धुभिः..
तुलापुरुषदानस्य फलमेतदुदाहृतम्..36..
5.266.m: Mental distress and bodily diseases do not arise, nor does widowhood caused by sickness / occur, O best of kings, nor separation from one's own kinsmen: / such is declared to be the fruit of the gift of a person weighed in the balance.

5.266.s:
tulāpuruṣadānasya pradattasya nṛpottama..
na śakyate kathayituṃ phalaṃ yatsyātkalau yuge..37..
5.266.d:
तुलापुरुषदानस्य प्रदत्तस्य नृपोत्तम..
न शक्यते कथयितुं फलं यत्स्यात्कलौ युगे..37..
5.266.m: The fruit that results in the Kali age from the gift of a person weighed in the balance / having been given, O best of kings, cannot be described.

5.266.s:
dakṣiṇāmūrtimāsādya siddheśvaravibhoḥ puraḥ..
yaḥ prayacchati bhūpāla sahasraguṇitaṃ phalam..38..
5.266.d:
दक्षिणामूर्तिमासाद्य सिद्धेश्वरविभोः पुरः..
यः प्रयच्छति भूपाल सहस्रगुणितं फलम्..38..
5.266.m: Approaching Dakṣiṇāmūrti in the presence of the all-pervading lord Siddheśvara, / he who bestows it, O protector of the earth, obtains a thousandfold fruit.

5.266.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena prāpya siddheśvaraṃ vibhum..
tulāpuruṣadānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ suvivekinā.39..
5.266.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन प्राप्य सिद्धेश्वरं विभुम्..
तुलापुरुषदानं च कर्तव्यं सुविवेकिना.39..
5.266.m: Therefore, by every effort having approached the all-pervading lord Siddheśvara, / the gift of a person weighed in the balance should be performed by one who possesses true discernment.

5.266.s:
ekatra sarvatīrthāni sarvāṇyāyatanāni ca..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre kathitāni svayaṃbhuvā..6.267.40..
5.266.d:
एकत्र सर्वतीर्थानि सर्वाण्यायतनानि च..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे कथितानि स्वयंभुवा..6.267.40..
5.266.m: All the sacred fords and all the shrines together / in the sacred field arising from Hāṭakeśvara have been spoken of by the self-manifest [Brahmā].

5.266.s:
siddheśvaraḥ suraśreṣṭha ekatra samudāhṛtaḥ..
tasmindṛṣṭe tathā spṛṣṭe pūjite nṛpasattama..
sarveṣāṃ labhate martyaḥ phalaṃ yatparikīrtitam..41..
5.266.d:
सिद्धेश्वरः सुरश्रेष्ठ एकत्र समुदाहृतः..
तस्मिन्दृष्टे तथा स्पृष्टे पूजिते नृपसत्तम..
सर्वेषां लभते मर्त्यः फलं यत्परिकीर्तितम्..41..
5.266.m: Siddheśvara, O best of gods, is declared to be [all of them] united in one place; / when he is seen, touched, and worshiped, O best of kings, / a mortal obtains the fruit that has been proclaimed for all of them.

5.266.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śrīsiddheśvaramāhātmye tulāpuruṣadānamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptaṣaṣṭyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..267..
5.266.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये श्रीसिद्धेश्वरमाहात्म्ये तुलापुरुषदानमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तषष्ट्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः..267..
5.266.m: Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of the Gift of a Person Weighed in the Balance in the Glory of Śrī Siddheśvara', in the Glory of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.267.s:
ānarta uvāca..
karmaṇā kena martye ca narāṇāṃ jāyate vada..
cakravartitvamakhilaṃ sarvaśatruvimardanam..1..
5.267.d:
आनर्त उवाच..
कर्मणा केन मर्त्ये च नराणां जायते वद..
चक्रवर्तित्वमखिलं सर्वशत्रुविमर्दनम्..1..
5.267.m: Ānarta said: / Tell [me], by what action among mortals does there arise for men / complete universal sovereignty that crushes all enemies?

5.267.s:
bhartṛyajña uvāca..
durlabhaṃ bhūmipālatvaṃ sarvapāpairnarādhipa..
tapobhirniyamairdānaistathānyaiśca śubhairvrataiḥ.. 2..
5.267.d:
भर्तृयज्ञ उवाच..
दुर्लभं भूमिपालत्वं सर्वपापैर्नराधिप..
तपोभिर्नियमैर्दानैस्तथान्यैश्च शुभैर्व्रतैः.. 2..
5.267.m: Bhartṛyajña said: / Kingship is difficult to attain by all sins, O king of men, / [and is won] through austerities, religious restraints, gifts, and likewise other auspicious vows.

5.267.s:
yaḥ punarbhūpatirbhūtvā pṛthvīṃ dadyāddhiraṇmayīm..
gautameśvaradevasya purataḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ..
cakravartī bhavennūnamevamāha pitāmahaḥ.. 3..
5.267.d:
यः पुनर्भूपतिर्भूत्वा पृथ्वीं दद्याद्धिरण्मयीम्..
गौतमेश्वरदेवस्य पुरतः श्रद्धयान्वितः..
चक्रवर्ती भवेन्नूनमेवमाह पितामहः.. 3..
5.267.m: He who, having become a king, gives a golden earth / in the presence of the god Gautameśvara with faith, / surely becomes a universal emperor; so said the grandfather [Brahmā].

5.267.s:
māṃdhātā dhundhumāraśca hariścaṃdraḥ purūravāḥ.
bharataḥ kārtavīryaśca ṣaḍete cakravartinaḥ..4.
5.267.d:
मांधाता धुन्धुमारश्च हरिश्चंद्रः पुरूरवाः.
भरतः कार्तवीर्यश्च षडेते चक्रवर्तिनः..4.
5.267.m: Māndhātṛ, Dhundhumāra, Hariścandra, Purūravas, / Bharata, and Kārtavīrya—these are the six universal emperors.

5.267.s:
pṛthvīdānaṃ purā kṛtvā gautameśvarasaṃnidhau.
dattvā hiraṇmayīṃ pṛthvīṃ sārvabhaumāstataḥ sthitāḥ..5..
5.267.d:
पृथ्वीदानं पुरा कृत्वा गौतमेश्वरसंनिधौ.
दत्त्वा हिरण्मयीं पृथ्वीं सार्वभौमास्ततः स्थिताः..5..
5.267.m: Having in ancient times made the gift of the earth in the presence of Gautameśvara, / having given a golden earth, they consequently stood as emperors over the whole earth.

5.267.s:
ānarta uvāca..
bhagavankena vidhinā dātavyā sā vasundharā..
ahaṃ dāsyāmi tāṃ nūnaṃ śraddhā me mahatī sthitā..6..
5.267.d:
आनर्त उवाच..
भगवन्केन विधिना दातव्या सा वसुन्धरा..
अहं दास्यामि तां नूनं श्रद्धा मे महती स्थिता..6..
5.267.m: Ānarta said: / O venerable one, by what rite should that earth be given? / I will certainly give it; great faith resides in me.

5.267.s:
bhartṛyajña uvāca..
kāryā palaśatenorvī vṛttākārā nṛpottama..
tadardhenāthavā śaktyā paṃcaviṃśatpalātmikā..7..
5.267.d:
भर्तृयज्ञ उवाच..
कार्या पलशतेनोर्वी वृत्ताकारा नृपोत्तम..
तदर्धेनाथवा शक्त्या पंचविंशत्पलात्मिका..7..
5.267.m: Bhartṛyajña said: / The earth should be made of one hundred palas, circular in shape, O best of kings; / or with half of that, or according to one's capacity, consisting of twenty-five palas.

5.267.s:
dharādāne mahārāja vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet..
naiva paṃcapalādarvākpradātavyā kathañcana..
lavaṇekṣusurāsarpirdadhidugdhajalodbhavāḥ..
samudrāḥ sapta caitāṃstu kakṣāyāṃ tatra darśayet..9..
5.267.d:
धरादाने महाराज वित्तशाठ्यं विवर्जयेत्..
नैव पंचपलादर्वाक्प्रदातव्या कथञ्चन..
लवणेक्षुसुरासर्पिर्दधिदुग्धजलोद्भवाः..
समुद्राः सप्त चैतांस्तु कक्षायां तत्र दर्शयेत्..9..
5.267.m: In making the gift of the earth, O great king, one should avoid stinginess regarding wealth; / it should never be given below five palas under any circumstances. / The oceans arising from salt, sugarcane juice, liquor, ghee, curds, milk, and water— / one should display these seven oceans within its zone there.

5.267.s:
jaṃbūplakṣakuśakrauṃcaśākaśālmalipuṣkarāḥ.
samudrānsaritaḥ sapta dvaiguṇyena prakalpayet..6.268.10..
5.267.d:
जंबूप्लक्षकुशक्रौंचशाकशाल्मलिपुष्कराः.
समुद्रान्सरितः सप्त द्वैगुण्येन प्रकल्पयेत्..6.268.10..
5.267.m: The [continents of] Jambū, Plakṣa, Kuśa, Krauñca, Śāka, Śālmali, and Puṣkara, / the oceans, and the seven rivers one should fashion, each doubling in size.

5.267.s:
mahendro malayaḥ sahyo himavāngaṃdhamādanaḥ..
viṃdhyaḥ śṛṃgī ca saptaiva kalpayetkulaparvatān..11..
madhye prakalpayenmeruṃ dikṣu viṣkambhaparvatān..
jaṃbūnyagrodhanīpāṃśca plakṣaścaiva tathā drumān..12..
5.267.d:
महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यो हिमवान्गंधमादनः..
विंध्यः शृंगी च सप्तैव कल्पयेत्कुलपर्वतान्..11..
मध्ये प्रकल्पयेन्मेरुं दिक्षु विष्कम्भपर्वतान्..
जंबून्यग्रोधनीपांश्च प्लक्षश्चैव तथा द्रुमान्..12..
5.267.m:
Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Himavat, Gandhamādana,
Vindhya, and Śṛṅgin: one should fashion precisely these seven principal mountain ranges.
In the center, one should fashion Meru, and in the cardinal directions, the supporting mountains;
likewise the trees: the rose-apple, the banyan, the kadamba, and the plakṣa.

5.267.s:
gaṃgādyāḥ saritastatra prādhānyena prakalpayet..
evaṃ nirmāpya vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ hemamayīṃ nṛpa..13..
maṃḍapaṃ kārayetpaścādyathāpūrvaṃ prakalpitam..14..
5.267.d:
गंगाद्याः सरितस्तत्र प्राधान्येन प्रकल्पयेत्..
एवं निर्माप्य वसुधां सर्वां हेममयीं नृप..13..
मंडपं कारयेत्पश्चाद्यथापूर्वं प्रकल्पितम्..14..
5.267.m:
There one should fashion the rivers, foremost among them the Gaṅgā.
Having thus fashioned the entire earth made of gold, O king,
one should then cause a pavilion to be built, constructed as described before.

5.267.s:
kuṇḍāni toraṇānyeva brāhmaṇagrahapūjane..
pūrvavatsakalaṃ kṛtvā madhye vediṃ prakalpayet..15..
5.267.d:
कुण्डानि तोरणान्येव ब्राह्मणग्रहपूजने..
पूर्ववत्सकलं कृत्वा मध्ये वेदिं प्रकल्पयेत्..15..
5.267.m:
Sacrificial pits and archways indeed for worship of the brahmins and planets—
having made everything as before, one should fashion an altar in the middle.

5.267.s:
